entries.definition: The ring is a domain and, in every finite extension of its fraction field, its integral closure is finite as a module over the ring.

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Domain of characteristic zero
entries.definition: The ring is a domain and the unital map from the integers is injective. Its fraction field then has characteristic zero.

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Analytically unramified local ring
entries.definition: The ring is Noetherian and local, and its completion at its maximal ideal is reduced.

entries.subject: ideal
entries.name: Analytically unramified prime
entries.definition: For a prime ideal $\mathfrak p$ of a Noetherian local ring $R$, the completion of the local ring $R/\mathfrak p$ at its maximal ideal is reduced.

entries.topic: Modules with a sequence of scalars
entries.subject: module-sequence
entries.name: Koszul-regular sequence on a module
entries.definition: For an $R$-module $M$ and finite sequence $\mathbf f$ in $R$, require $H_i(K_\bullet(\mathbf f)\otimes_R M)=0$ for every $i>0$.

entries.topic: Modules with a sequence of scalars
entries.subject: module-sequence
entries.name: H₁-regular sequence on a module
entries.definition: For an $R$-module $M$ and finite sequence $\mathbf f$ in $R$, require $H_1(K_\bullet(\mathbf f)\otimes_R M)=0$.

entries.subject: ring-parameters
entries.name: Koszul-regular sequence in a ring
entries.definition: For a finite sequence $\mathbf f$ in $R$, require $H_i(K_\bullet(\mathbf f))=0$ for every $i>0$.

entries.subject: ring-parameters
entries.name: H₁-regular sequence in a ring
entries.definition: For a finite sequence $\mathbf f$ in $R$, require $H_1(K_\bullet(\mathbf f))=0$.

entries.subject: module-pair
entries.name: Stably isomorphic modules
entries.definition: For two $R$-modules $M,N$, there are nonnegative integers $m,n$ with $M\oplus R^m\cong N\oplus R^n$ as $R$-modules.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Stably free module
entries.definition: An $R$-module $M$ is stably isomorphic to some free $R$-module. Equivalently, $M\oplus R^m$ is free for some finite $m\geq0$. The free module need not have finite rank.

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Absolutely integrally closed ring
entries.definition: Every monic polynomial in $R[T]$ splits into linear factors over $R$.

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: A root for every positive-degree monic polynomial
entries.definition: For every monic polynomial of positive degree in $R[T]$, at least one root belongs to $R$.

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Auto-associated local ring
entries.definition: The ring $R$ is local and its maximal ideal is weakly associated to the $R$-module $R$: it is minimal over the annihilator of some element of $R$.

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Nonzero annihilators of proper finite ideals
entries.definition: For each proper finitely generated ideal $J\subset R$, the annihilator $\operatorname{Ann}_R(J)$ contains a nonzero element.

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Injections of projective modules universally injective
entries.definition: Every injective homomorphism of projective modules remains injective after tensoring with an arbitrary module over the ring.

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Inclusions of finite projectives split
entries.definition: Every injective homomorphism between finite projective modules is split as a map of modules.

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Inclusions of arbitrary free modules split
entries.definition: Every injective homomorphism between free modules of arbitrary rank is split as a map of modules.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Rank of a module over a domain
entries.definition: For a domain $R$ with fraction field $K$, the rank of $M$ is the cardinal dimension $\dim_K(M\otimes_R K)$.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Reflexive module over a domain
entries.definition: For a domain $R$, the evaluation map $M\to\operatorname{Hom}_R(\operatorname{Hom}_R(M,R),R)$ taking $x$ to evaluation at $x$ is an isomorphism.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Reflexive localization at every prime
entries.definition: For a domain $R$, the localization $M_{\mathfrak p}$ is a reflexive $R_{\mathfrak p}$-module for every prime $\mathfrak p$.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Reflexive localization at every maximal ideal
entries.definition: For a domain $R$, the localization $M_{\mathfrak m}$ is a reflexive $R_{\mathfrak m}$-module for every maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Finite free embedding with torsion-free cokernel
entries.definition: For a domain $R$, there exists a short exact sequence $0\to M\to F\to N\to0$ in which $F$ is finite free and $N$ is torsion free.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Reflexive hull
entries.definition: For a finite module $M$ over a Noetherian domain $R$, the reflexive hull is its double dual $M^{**}=\operatorname{Hom}_R(\operatorname{Hom}_R(M,R),R)$.

entries.subject: module-element
entries.name: Content ideal of an element
entries.definition: For $x\in M$ with $M$ flat over $A$, the content ideal of $x$, when it exists, is the least ideal $I\subseteq A$ satisfying $x\in IM$.

entries.subject: ring-map-module
entries.name: Strict transform on an affine blowup chart
entries.definition: For an ideal $I\subset R$, an element $a\in I$ and the affine blowup algebra $S=R[I/a]$, the strict transform of an $R$-module $M$ is $(M\otimes_R S)$ modulo its $a$-power torsion submodule.

entries.subject: complex
entries.name: Koszul complex of a linear map
entries.definition: For an $R$-linear map $\varphi:E\to R$, use the exterior algebra $\bigwedge_R E$ with $E$ in homological degree one. The differential of degree $-1$ is the derivation taking $e\in E$ to $\varphi(e)$.

entries.subject: complex
entries.name: Koszul complex of a sequence
entries.definition: For $f_1,\ldots,f_r\in R$, take the Koszul complex of $R^r\to R$ sending the $i$th basis element to $f_i$.

entries.subject: topological-ring
entries.name: Topological ring
entries.definition: The topology on $R$ makes addition and multiplication continuous on $R\times R$ with its product topology.

entries.subject: topological-module
entries.name: Topological module
entries.definition: For a topological ring $R$, the topology on $M$ makes addition on $M\times M$ and the scalar action on $R\times M$ continuous.

entries.subject: topological-ring-map
entries.name: Homomorphism of topological rings
entries.definition: The ring homomorphism is continuous for the specified topologies.

entries.subject: topological-module-map
entries.name: Homomorphism of topological modules
entries.definition: The $R$-linear map is continuous for the specified topologies.

entries.subject: topological-ring
entries.name: Linearly topologized ring
entries.definition: In a topological ring $R$, the zero element has a neighbourhood basis consisting of ideals of $R$.

entries.subject: topological-module
entries.name: Linearly topologized module
entries.definition: In a topological module, the zero element has a neighbourhood basis consisting of submodules.

entries.topic: Topological rings with a fixed ideal
entries.subject: topological-ring-ideal-pair
entries.name: Ideal of definition
entries.definition: In a linearly topologized ring $R$, an ideal $I$ is an ideal of definition if it is open and every neighbourhood of zero contains some power $I^n$.

entries.subject: topological-ring
entries.name: Pre-admissible topological ring
entries.definition: The ring is linearly topologized and has an ideal of definition.

entries.subject: topological-ring
entries.name: Admissible topological ring
entries.definition: The ring is pre-admissible and complete, with completeness including separatedness in the source convention.

entries.subject: topological-ring
entries.name: Pre-adic topological ring
entries.definition: The ring is linearly topologized and has an ideal of definition $I$ whose powers form a neighbourhood basis at zero.

entries.subject: topological-ring
entries.name: Adic topological ring
entries.definition: The ring is pre-adic and complete, with completeness including separatedness.

entries.subject: topological-ring
entries.name: Complete separated linearly topologized ring
entries.definition: The ring is linearly topologized and the canonical map $R\to\varprojlim_U R/U$ is an isomorphism, with $U$ running over its open ideals.

entries.subject: topological-ring-map
entries.name: Formally smooth map of topological rings
entries.definition: The source and target are linearly topologized and the map $R\to S$ is continuous. For every discrete $R$-algebra $B$ with continuous structure map, square-zero ideal $J\subset B$ and continuous $R$-map $S\to B/J$, there exists a continuous $R$-map $S\to B$ lifting it.

entries.topic: Ring maps with a fixed ideal
entries.subject: ring-map-ideal-pair
entries.name: Formally smooth for the target adic topology
entries.definition: For a ring map $R\to S$ and ideal $\mathfrak n\subseteq S$, give $R$ the discrete topology and $S$ the $\mathfrak n$-adic topology. The map is formally smooth as a map of these topological rings.

entries.subject: field-family
entries.name: p-independent subset
entries.definition: For a characteristic-$p$ field extension $K/k$ and a subset $E\subseteq K$, the monomials in $E$ with finite support and exponents less than $p$ are linearly independent over the compositum $kK^p$.

entries.subject: field-family
entries.name: p-basis of a field extension
entries.definition: For a characteristic-$p$ field extension $K/k$ and a subset $E\subseteq K$, the monomials in $E$ with finite support and exponents less than $p$ form a basis of $K$ as a vector space over $kK^p$.

entries.subject: field-family
entries.name: Linearly independent differentials in characteristic p
entries.definition: For a characteristic-$p$ field extension $K/k$ and a subset $E\subseteq K$, the family $(dx)_{x\in E}$ is $K$-linearly independent in $\Omega_{K/k}$.

entries.subject: field-family
entries.name: Differential basis in characteristic p
entries.definition: For a characteristic-$p$ field extension $K/k$ and a subset $E\subseteq K$, the family $(dx)_{x\in E}$ is a $K$-basis of $\Omega_{K/k}$.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Character module functor
entries.definition: The character module of $M$ is $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbf Z}(M,\mathbf Q/\mathbf Z)$, with scalar action $(r\lambda)(x)=\lambda(rx)$. It is contravariantly functorial in $M$.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Free cover on the underlying set of a module
entries.definition: The free cover of $M$ is the surjection $\bigoplus_{m\in M}R[m]\to M$ sending $[m]$ to $m$. The construction is covariantly functorial in $M$.

entries.subject: complex
entries.name: K-flat complex
entries.definition: A specified complex $K^\bullet$ is K-flat when $\operatorname{Tot}(E^\bullet\otimes_R K^\bullet)$ is acyclic for every acyclic complex $E^\bullet$ of $R$-modules. This predicate applies to a complex representing a derived object.

entries.subject: complex
entries.name: Derived tensor product
entries.definition: For $K,L\in D(R)$, replace $L$ by a quasi-isomorphic K-flat complex and take the direct-sum total complex of its tensor product with a representative of $K$. This yields the derived object $K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}L$.

entries.subject: algebra-pair
entries.name: Tor-independent algebras over the base
entries.definition: The pair of $R$-algebras $(A,B)$ satisfies $\operatorname{Tor}^R_i(A,B)=0$ for all $i>0$.

entries.subject: complex
entries.name: Finite projective dimension of a derived object
entries.definition: The object of $D(R)$ has a bounded representative consisting of projective $R$-modules.

entries.subject: complex-interval
entries.name: Projective amplitude in a specified interval
entries.definition: Given $a\leq b$, the object of $D(R)$ admits a representative consisting of projective modules and concentrated in cohomological degrees $[a,b]$.

entries.subject: complex
entries.name: Finite injective dimension of a derived object
entries.definition: The object of $D(R)$ has a bounded representative consisting of injective $R$-modules.

entries.subject: complex-interval
entries.name: Injective amplitude in a specified interval
entries.definition: Given $a\leq b$, the object of $D(R)$ admits a representative consisting of injective modules and concentrated in cohomological degrees $[a,b]$.

entries.subject: module-ideal-pair
entries.name: Module projective relative to an ideal
entries.definition: For a module $M$ and an ideal $I$ over $R$, multiplication by every $a\in I$ on $M$ factors through a projective $R$-module. In the source this condition is called $I$-projectivity.

entries.subject: module-ideal-pair
entries.name: Ideal annihilates first Ext from the module
entries.definition: For every $R$-module $N$ the ideal $I$ annihilates $\operatorname{Ext}^1_R(M,N)$.

entries.subject: ring-map-module
entries.name: Relatively finitely presented module
entries.definition: For a finite type map $R\to A$ and an $A$-module $M$, there exists a surjection $R[X_1,\ldots,X_n]\to A$ making $M$ finitely presented over that polynomial ring.

entries.subject: ring-map-complex
entries.name: Relative m-pseudo-coherence of a complex
entries.definition: For a finite type map $R\to A$, an integer $m$ and a complex of $A$-modules $K$, there is a finite polynomial presentation $R[X_1,\ldots,X_n]\twoheadrightarrow A$ for which $K$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent over the polynomial ring.

entries.subject: ring-map-complex
entries.name: Relative pseudo-coherence of a complex
entries.definition: For a finite type map $R\to A$, the complex of $A$-modules is $m$-pseudo-coherent relative to $R$ for every integer $m$.

entries.subject: ring-map-module
entries.name: Relative m-pseudo-coherence of a module
entries.definition: For a finite type map $R\to A$ and an integer $m$, the complex $M[0]$ of the $A$-module is $m$-pseudo-coherent relative to $R$.

entries.subject: ring-map-module
entries.name: Relative pseudo-coherence of a module
entries.definition: For a finite type map $R\to A$, the complex $M[0]$ of the $A$-module is pseudo-coherent relative to $R$.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Pseudo-coherent ring map
entries.definition: The map $R\to A$ is of finite type and $A$ as an $A$-module is pseudo-coherent relative to $R$.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Perfect ring map
entries.definition: The map $R\to A$ is pseudo-coherent and $A$ as an $R$-module has finite Tor dimension.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Perfect target over a finite polynomial presentation
entries.definition: For the map $R\to A$, some surjection $R[X_1,\ldots,X_n]\to A$ makes $A$ admit a finite resolution by finite projective $R[X_1,\ldots,X_n]$-modules.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Target module of finite Tor dimension
entries.definition: For the map $R\to A$, the target $A$ as an $R$-module has finite Tor dimension.

entries.subject: ring-map-complex
entries.name: Perfect complex relative to a ring
entries.definition: For a flat map of finite presentation $R\to A$ and an object $K\in D(A)$, the object $K$ is pseudo-coherent over $A$ and has finite Tor dimension over $R$.

entries.subject: module-ideal-pair
entries.name: Module with ideal-power torsion
entries.definition: For every $x\in M$ some positive power $I^n$ of the chosen ideal annihilates $x$. The exponent can depend on $x$.

entries.subject: module-scalar-pair
entries.name: Module with scalar-power torsion
entries.definition: For every $x\in M$ some positive power $f^n$ of the chosen scalar annihilates $x$. The exponent can depend on $x$.

entries.subject: complex-ideal-pair
entries.name: Derived-complete complex
entries.definition: For $K\in D(A)$ and an ideal $I\subseteq A$, one has $\operatorname{RHom}_A(A_f,K)=0$ for every $f\in I$.

entries.subject: module-ideal-pair
entries.name: Derived-complete module
entries.definition: The object $M[0]$ is derived complete with respect to the chosen ideal $I\subseteq A$.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Weakly étale ring map
entries.definition: Both $A\to B$ and the multiplication map $B\otimes_A B\to B$ are flat.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Flat multiplication map of a tensor square
entries.definition: For the chosen map $A\to B$, the multiplication map $B\otimes_A B\to B$ is flat.

entries.subject: local-ring
entries.name: Number of branches of a local ring
entries.definition: Count the minimal primes of the henselization $A^h$, using $\infty$ for an infinite set.

entries.subject: local-ring
entries.name: Number of geometric branches of a local ring
entries.definition: Count the minimal primes of the strict henselization $A^{sh}$, using $\infty$ for an infinite set.

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Formally catenary local ring
entries.definition: The ring $A$ is Noetherian local, and for every minimal prime $\mathfrak p\subset A$ the scheme $\operatorname{Spec}(\widehat A/\mathfrak p\widehat A)$ is equidimensional.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Extension of discrete valuation rings
entries.definition: The rings $A,B$ are discrete valuation rings and $A\to B$ is injective and local.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Ramification index of an extension of discrete valuation rings
entries.definition: For an extension $A\to B$ of discrete valuation rings, its ramification index is the integer $e\geq1$ with $\mathfrak m_A B=\mathfrak m_B^e$.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Weakly unramified extension of discrete valuation rings
entries.definition: The map is an extension of discrete valuation rings with ramification index $e=1$.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Extension of discrete valuation rings with separable residue extension
entries.definition: The map is an extension of discrete valuation rings and $\kappa_B/\kappa_A$ is separable as a field extension, without assuming finite degree.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Extension of discrete valuation rings formally smooth for the target adic topology
entries.definition: The map is an extension of discrete valuation rings and is formally smooth for the $\mathfrak m_B$-adic topology, with the source taken discrete in the equivalent definition.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Residue degree of an extension of valuation rings
entries.definition: For an injective local map of valuation rings $A\to B$ with finite residue field extension, the residue degree is $[\kappa_B:\kappa_A]$. This also applies to extensions of discrete valuation rings.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Extension of valuation rings
entries.definition: The rings $A,B$ are valuation rings and $A\to B$ is injective and local.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Weakly unramified extension of valuation rings
entries.definition: The map is an extension of valuation rings whose induced homomorphism of value groups $\Gamma_A\to\Gamma_B$ is an isomorphism.

entries.subject: valued-field-extension
entries.name: Finite separable extension unramified with respect to a DVR
entries.definition: Let $A$ be a DVR with fraction field $K$, let $L/K$ be finite separable, and let $B$ be the integral closure of $A$ in $L$. Every localization of $B$ at a maximal ideal has ramification index one over $A$ and a separable residue extension.

entries.subject: valued-field-extension
entries.name: Finite separable extension tamely ramified with respect to a DVR
entries.definition: Use the integral closure $B$ of a DVR $A$ in the finite separable extension $L/K$ of its fraction field. Either $\kappa_A$ has characteristic zero, or it has characteristic $p>0$ and all maximal-ideal residue extensions are separable with ramification indices prime to $p$.

entries.subject: valued-field-extension
entries.name: Finite separable extension totally ramified with respect to a DVR
entries.definition: For a DVR $A$ and a finite separable extension $L/K$ of its fraction field, the integral closure of $A$ in $L$ has a unique maximal ideal and its residue field is $\kappa_A$.

entries.topic: Galois extensions with a specified prime
entries.subject: galois-prime
entries.name: Decomposition group at a prime
entries.definition: For a finite Galois extension $L/K$ of the fraction field of a DVR $A$ and a maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ of its integral closure $B$, take the stabilizer of $\mathfrak m$ in $\operatorname{Gal}(L/K)$.

entries.topic: Galois extensions with a specified prime
entries.subject: galois-prime
entries.name: Inertia group at a prime
entries.definition: Let $A$ be a DVR with fraction field $K$, let $L/K$ be finite Galois and let $\mathfrak m$ be a maximal ideal of the integral closure of $A$ in $L$. The inertia group is the kernel of the action of the decomposition group at $\mathfrak m$ on the residue field $\kappa(\mathfrak m)$.

entries.topic: Galois extensions with a specified prime
entries.subject: galois-prime
entries.name: Wild inertia group
entries.definition: For a maximal ideal in the integral closure of a DVR in a finite Galois extension, take the subgroup of inertia acting trivially on $\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2$.

entries.topic: Galois extensions with a specified prime
entries.subject: galois-prime
entries.name: Tame inertia group
entries.definition: For a maximal ideal in the integral closure of a DVR in a finite Galois extension, take the quotient of inertia by wild inertia.

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Discrete valuation ring of mixed characteristic
entries.definition: The ring is a discrete valuation ring whose fraction field has characteristic zero and whose residue field has characteristic $p>0$.

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Absolute ramification index
entries.definition: For a mixed-characteristic discrete valuation ring $A$ of residue characteristic $p$, take the ramification index of $\mathbf Z_{(p)}\to A$.

entries.subject: ramification-solution
entries.name: Weak solution to eliminating ramification
entries.definition: Fix an extension $A\subset B$ of DVRs with fraction fields $K\subset L$ and a finite extension $K_1/K$. Let $A_1$ be the integral closure of $A$ in $K_1$, and let $B_1$ be the integral closure of $B$ in $(L\otimes_K K_1)_{\mathrm{red}}$. For each maximal ideal $\mathfrak q$ of $B_1$ lying over a maximal ideal $\mathfrak p$ of $A_1$, the map $(A_1)_{\mathfrak p}\to(B_1)_{\mathfrak q}$ must be weakly unramified.

entries.subject: ramification-solution
entries.name: Solution to eliminating ramification
entries.definition: Fix an extension $A\subset B$ of DVRs with fraction fields $K\subset L$ and a finite extension $K_1/K$. Let $A_1$ be the integral closure of $A$ in $K_1$, and let $B_1$ be the integral closure of $B$ in $(L\otimes_K K_1)_{\mathrm{red}}$. For each maximal ideal $\mathfrak q$ of $B_1$ lying over a maximal ideal $\mathfrak p$ of $A_1$, the map $(A_1)_{\mathfrak p}\to(B_1)_{\mathfrak q}$ must be formally smooth for the adic topology of its target maximal ideal.

entries.subject: ramification-solution
entries.name: Separable solution to eliminating ramification
entries.definition: The finite field extension $K_1/K$ is a solution to eliminating ramification for the specified extension of DVRs, and $K_1/K$ is separable.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Invertible module
entries.definition: Tensoring over $R$ with the module gives an equivalence from the category of $R$-modules to itself.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Trivial invertible module
entries.definition: The module is invertible and is isomorphic to $R$ as an $R$-module.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Module with a tensor inverse
entries.definition: There exists an $R$-module $N$ with $M\otimes_R N\cong R$ as $R$-modules.

entries.subject: module
entries.name: Finite locally free module of rank one
entries.definition: The module is finite locally free and each localization at a prime is free of rank one.

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Bézout domain
entries.definition: The ring is a domain in which every finitely generated ideal is principal.

entries.subject: ring
entries.name: Elementary divisor domain
entries.definition: The ring is a domain and every finite rectangular matrix can be brought by invertible row and column operations to diagonal form with consecutive diagonal entries ordered by divisibility.

entries.subject: local-ring
entries.name: Residue field of a local ring
entries.definition: For a local ring $(R,\mathfrak m)$ the residue field is the quotient $R/\mathfrak m$. The quotient map is defined using the unique maximal ideal.
refs: Stacks 07BI · residue field of a local ring

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Local homomorphism of local rings
entries.definition: A unital map $R\to S$ of local rings is local if it sends the maximal ideal of $R$ into the maximal ideal of $S$. Equivalently the preimage of the maximal ideal of $S$ is the maximal ideal of $R$.
refs: Stacks 07BI · local homomorphism of local rings

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Regular ring map
entries.definition: A map $R\to A$ is regular if it is flat and each fibre $A\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is geometrically regular over $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$, for every $\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Spec}(R)$.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Map between Noetherian rings
entries.definition: Both the source ring and the target ring are Noetherian.

entries.subject: ring-map
entries.name: Filtered colimit of smooth algebras
entries.definition: For a map $R\to A$, the $R$-algebra $A$ is isomorphic to a filtered colimit of smooth $R$-algebras.
refs: Stacks 07EP · regularity of smooth colimits with Noetherian fibres

theorems.proof: After base change to $\operatorname{Spec}V$, a faithfully flat cover lifts the specialization from the generic point to the closed point. theorems.subject: qcqs-cover

theorems.subject: qcqs-cover
theorems.proof: The valuation test can be expressed as lifting the specialization from the generic point to the closed point after base change to a valuation spectrum. Over a rank-one valuation ring, lifting that pair of points yields an extension of rank one. Thus an arbitrary-rank cover satisfies the rank-at-most-one test. See Proposition 2.1 and Corollary 2.5 of Bhatt–Mathew.

theorems.name: Regular local ring ⇒ Complete intersection local ring

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: Every prime localization is regular local, so each is a complete intersection.
theorems.name: Regular ring ⇒ Local complete intersection ring

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: Apply the definition at the maximal ideal. Conversely the complete-intersection property localizes to every prime.
refs: Stacks 09Q3 · local and global complete intersection conditions
theorems.name: Local ring + Local complete intersection ring ⇔ Complete intersection local ring

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: A regular local ring is Gorenstein. A quotient by a regular sequence remains Gorenstein. Apply flat local descent along the completion map.
refs: Stacks 0AWX · regular local rings are Gorenstein
theorems.name: Complete intersection local ring ⇒ Gorenstein local ring

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: Each prime localization is complete intersection and hence Gorenstein, by ascent along a regular-sequence quotient and descent from completion.
theorems.name: Local complete intersection ring ⇒ Gorenstein ring

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: A Noetherian ring is Gorenstein of finite dimension exactly when it has finite injective dimension over itself.
refs: Stacks 0HB2 · finite injective dimension and Gorenstein rings
theorems.name: Gorenstein ring + Finite Krull dimension ⇔ Noetherian ring + Finite injective dimension over itself

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: The local direction uses the unique maximal prime. The converse follows by localization of a dualizing complex.
refs: Stacks 0DW7 · global and local Gorenstein definitions
theorems.name: Local ring + Gorenstein ring ⇔ Gorenstein local ring

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: The dualizing complex of a Gorenstein local ring is concentrated in one degree, yielding the Cohen–Macaulay property.
theorems.name: Gorenstein ring ⇒ Cohen–Macaulay ring

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: Localize a Cohen–Macaulay local ring at each prime for the global condition. The other direction uses the maximal ideal.
theorems.name: Local ring + Cohen–Macaulay ring ⇔ Cohen–Macaulay local ring

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: Polynomial algebras over the ring are Cohen–Macaulay and hence catenary. Catenarity descends to their quotients.
refs: Stacks 00NM · Cohen–Macaulay rings are universally catenary
theorems.name: Cohen–Macaulay ring ⇒ Universally catenary ring

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: Hensel lifting converges in the maximal ideal adic topology.
refs: Stacks 04GM · complete local rings are henselian
theorems.name: Complete local ring ⇒ Henselian local ring

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: The maximal ideal is finitely generated if the ring is Noetherian. Conversely apply the Noetherianity criterion for complete local rings.
refs: Stacks 032B · finite maximal ideal in a complete local ring
theorems.name: Complete local ring + Local ring with finitely generated maximal ideal ⇔ Complete local ring + Noetherian ring

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: The predicate specifies a unique maximal ideal.
refs: Stacks 032B · finite maximal ideal in a complete local ring
theorems.name: Local ring with finitely generated maximal ideal ⇒ Local ring

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: The definition requires a complete DVR with the stated uniformizer.
theorems.name: Cohen ring ⇒ Complete local ring + Discrete valuation ring

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: The henselian condition is imposed on a local ring.
refs: Stacks 04GF · henselian and strictly henselian local rings
theorems.name: Henselian local ring ⇒ Local ring

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: Finite algebras over the ring have only finitely many primes, all maximal. Their local-product decomposition is the finite-algebra criterion for henselianity.
refs: Stacks 06RS · dimension-zero local rings are henselian
theorems.name: Local ring + Krull dimension at most zero ⇒ Henselian local ring

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: The maximal ideal is the Jacobson radical, which is nilpotent in an Artinian ring. The system of quotients by its powers is eventually constant.
theorems.name: Local ring + Artinian ring ⇒ Complete local ring

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: This is the definition of strictly henselian.
refs: Stacks 04GF · henselian and strictly henselian local rings
theorems.name: Henselian local ring + Separably closed residue field ⇔ Strictly henselian local ring

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: The residue-field predicate is specified for the unique maximal ideal of a local ring.
theorems.name: Separably closed residue field ⇒ Local ring

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: A normal local ring is a normal domain. Its normalization is itself, and its residue field extension is the identity.
theorems.name: Local ring + Normal ring ⇒ Geometrically unibranch local ring

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: Geometric unibranchness adds a purely inseparable residue-field condition to unibranchness.
refs: Stacks 0BPZ · unibranch and geometrically unibranch local rings
theorems.name: Geometrically unibranch local ring ⇒ Unibranch local ring

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: Locality and a domain reduction are two of the defining conditions.
theorems.name: Unibranch local ring ⇒ Local ring + Reduction is a domain

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: The height-zero primes are included among primes of height at most one.
refs: Stacks 031P · Serre conditions for rings and modules
theorems.name: Serre condition (R₁) ⇒ Serre condition (R₀)

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: The minimum of two and the local dimension is at least the minimum of one and that dimension.
refs: Stacks 031P · Serre conditions for rings and modules
theorems.name: Serre condition (S₂) ⇒ Serre condition (S₁)

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: The stated Serre predicate includes the Noetherian hypothesis.
refs: Stacks 031P · Serre conditions for rings and modules
theorems.name: Serre condition (R₀) ⇒ Noetherian ring

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: The stated Serre predicate includes the Noetherian hypothesis.
refs: Stacks 031P · Serre conditions for rings and modules
theorems.name: Serre condition (S₁) ⇒ Noetherian ring

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: The regular ring condition covers every prime, including all primes of height at most one.
refs: Stacks 031P · Serre conditions for rings and modules
theorems.name: Regular ring ⇒ Serre condition (R₁)

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: Depth equal to dimension satisfies every finite Serre depth bound.
refs: Stacks 031P · Serre conditions for rings and modules
theorems.name: Cohen–Macaulay ring ⇒ Serre condition (S₂)

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: Use the associated-prime criterion for Serre (S₁) over a Noetherian ring.
theorems.name: Serre condition (S₁) ⇔ No embedded associated primes

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: The two Serre conditions and the reducedness criterion are stated for Noetherian rings. The Noetherian premise appears explicitly on the reduced side.
theorems.name: Serre condition (R₀) + Serre condition (S₁) ⇔ Noetherian ring + Reduced ring

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: Serre’s normality criterion applies to a Noetherian ring. The Noetherian premise appears explicitly on the normal side.
theorems.name: Serre condition (R₁) + Serre condition (S₂) ⇔ Noetherian ring + Normal ring

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: In dimension at most one the (R₁) condition covers every prime. For the converse, a regular ring is Noetherian and normal.
theorems.name: Noetherian ring + Normal ring + Krull dimension at most one ⇔ Regular ring + Krull dimension at most one

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: The ring is a finite type algebra over itself.
theorems.name: Condition J-2 ⇒ Condition J-1

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: The predicate is defined for Noetherian rings and its regular locus contains a prime.
theorems.name: Condition J-0 ⇒ Noetherian ring + Nonzero ring

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: The regular-locus predicate here uses the Noetherian setting.
theorems.name: Condition J-1 ⇒ Noetherian ring

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: The definition of a G-ring includes the Noetherian hypothesis.
theorems.name: G-ring ⇒ Noetherian ring

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: The entire prime spectrum is the regular locus.
theorems.name: Regular ring ⇒ Condition J-1

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: The entire spectrum is regular and is nonempty for a nonzero ring.
theorems.name: Regular ring + Nonzero ring ⇒ Condition J-0

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: The three hypotheses are the defining conditions of quasi-excellence.
theorems.name: Noetherian ring + G-ring + Condition J-2 ⇔ Quasi-excellent ring

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: The two hypotheses are the defining conditions of excellence.
theorems.name: Quasi-excellent ring + Universally catenary ring ⇔ Excellent ring

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: Apply the finiteness theorem for normalization over quasi-excellent rings.
theorems.name: Quasi-excellent ring ⇒ Nagata ring

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: A Noetherian universally Japanese ring is Nagata by the definitions, and the converse is the Nagata theorem.
refs: Stacks 0334 · Nagata rings are universally Japanese
theorems.name: Noetherian ring + Universally Japanese ring ⇔ Nagata ring

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: The theorem on complete local Noetherian rings gives the requisite finiteness for every prime quotient and finite field extension.
refs: Stacks 032W · complete local Noetherian rings are Nagata
theorems.name: Noetherian ring + Complete local ring ⇒ Nagata ring

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.proof: Complete local Noetherian rings are among the standard classes of excellent rings.
theorems.name: Noetherian ring + Complete local ring ⇒ Excellent ring

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: The presentation includes a surjection from a finite free module.
theorems.name: Finitely presented module ⇒ Finite module

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: Finite generators and relations are exactly the condition that the represented Hom functor preserve filtered colimits.
theorems.name: Finitely presented module ⇔ Maps from the module commute with filtered colimits

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: A lift against a surjective map can be chosen on each basis vector.
theorems.name: Free module ⇒ Projective module

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: Tensoring with a free module gives a direct sum of copies of the input. Direct sums preserve exact sequences.
theorems.name: Free module ⇒ Flat module

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: If the base ring is nonzero, an infinite free basis cannot be generated by finitely many vectors with finite support. Over the zero ring the module is zero and admits the empty basis.
theorems.name: Finite module + Free module ⇔ Finite free module

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: A surjection from a free module onto a projective module splits, and a summand of a projective module is projective.
theorems.name: Projective module ⇔ Direct summand of a free module

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: The first Ext group vanishes for projective modules, and its vanishing against every module splits any short exact sequence ending in the module.
theorems.name: Projective module ⇔ Module with vanishing first Ext out of it

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: Projectivity implies flatness by the characterization. Equivalently, a direct summand of a flat module is flat.
theorems.name: Projective module ⇒ Flat module

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: This is the finite-generation and projectivity condition together.
theorems.name: Finite module + Projective module ⇔ Finite projective module

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: The finite-projective-module theorem identifies these two conditions.
theorems.name: Finitely presented module + Flat module ⇔ Finite projective module

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: Projectivity splits a finite free surjection, and a summand of a finite free module is finite projective.
theorems.name: Finite projective module ⇔ Direct summand of a finite free module

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: A finite projective module is finite locally free. Conversely, finite local freeness gives finite presentation and flatness.
theorems.name: Finite projective module ⇔ Finite locally free module

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: Use the same principal open covering and forget the fixed value of the rank.
theorems.name: Finite locally free module of a prescribed rank ⇒ Finite locally free module

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: Use the same principal open covering and forget the finiteness of the rank.
theorems.name: Finite locally free module ⇒ Locally free module

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: Each localization at a maximal ideal is free, hence flat.
theorems.name: Locally free module ⇒ Flat module

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: Lift a basis of the residue fibre. Nakayama gives a surjection, and flatness makes the lifted family a basis.
theorems.name: Module over a local ring + Finite module + Flat module ⇒ Finite free module

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: Kaplansky’s theorem applies without finite-generation assumptions.
theorems.name: Module over a local ring + Projective module ⇒ Free module

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: The kernel of a finite free presentation is a submodule of a finite module over a Noetherian ring, hence finite.
theorems.name: Module over a Noetherian ring + Finite module ⇒ Finitely presented module

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: Every submodule is finite. This is equivalent to the ascending chain condition.
theorems.name: Module over a Noetherian ring + Finite module ⇒ Noetherian module

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: A module with the ascending chain condition has a maximal finitely generated submodule, which must be the whole module.
theorems.name: Noetherian module ⇒ Finite module

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: The module is a finite submodule of itself.
theorems.name: Coherent module ⇒ Finitely presented module

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: Every finite submodule is finitely presented over a Noetherian base.
theorems.name: Module over a Noetherian ring + Finite module ⇒ Coherent module

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: The finite-ideal criterion for flatness is valid over any ring.
theorems.name: Flat module ⇔ Tensor injectivity for finite ideals

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: The ideal criterion for flatness is valid over any ring.
theorems.name: Flat module ⇔ Tensor injectivity for all ideals

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: Flatness gives vanishing of the derived functors of tensor. Conversely, the Tor exact sequence gives the injectivity of tensoring any inclusion.
theorems.name: Flat module ⇔ Module with vanishing first Tor against every module

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: Tensor kernels are detected after localizing at maximal ideals.
theorems.name: Flat module ⇔ Flatness at every maximal ideal

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: The fibre criterion for a flat module detects faithful flatness.
theorems.name: Flat module + Nonzero fibres at all maximal ideals ⇔ Faithfully flat module

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: The support of a finite module is the vanishing set of its annihilator.
theorems.name: Finite module ⇒ Module with closed support

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: Use a prime filtration and the inclusion of the associated primes of an extension in the union of those of its terms.
theorems.name: Module over a Noetherian ring + Finite module ⇒ Module with finitely many associated primes

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: A simple module has the composition series consisting of a single factor.
theorems.name: Simple module ⇒ Module of finite length

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: Lift finitely many generators of the quotient at each stage of the composition series.
theorems.name: Module of finite length ⇒ Finite module

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: Strict inclusions increase length, which is bounded by the length of the module.
theorems.name: Module of finite length ⇒ Noetherian module

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: Tensor multiplication by a nonzero scalar on the domain with the flat module.
theorems.name: Module over a domain + Flat module ⇒ Torsion-free module over a domain

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: Being a domain is part of the convention for valuation rings.
theorems.name: Module over a valuation ring ⇒ Module over a domain

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: Over a valuation ring, the finite-ideal criterion reduces to injectivity of multiplication by nonzero scalars.
theorems.name: Module over a valuation ring + Torsion-free module over a domain ⇒ Flat module

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: The characterization of projectivity yields both conditions.
theorems.name: Projective module ⇒ Mittag-Leffler module + Sum of countably generated modules

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: All three conditions are hypotheses of the projectivity characterization.
theorems.name: Flat module + Mittag-Leffler module + Sum of countably generated modules ⇒ Projective module

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: A finite projective resolution is a finite projective-dimension witness. Its first two terms are finitely presented, so their cokernel is finitely presented.
theorems.name: Perfect module ⇒ Finitely presented module + Module of finite projective dimension

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: A finite projective resolution computes derived tensor and is bounded.
theorems.name: Module of finite projective dimension ⇒ Module of finite Tor dimension

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: The specified interval is one of the bounded intervals permitted in the definition.
theorems.name: Module of Tor dimension at most d ⇒ Module of finite Tor dimension

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: Apply the perfect complex criterion to the module placed in degree zero.
theorems.name: Pseudo-coherent module + Module of finite Tor dimension ⇔ Perfect module

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: A finite projective module is its own resolution in degree zero.
theorems.name: Finite projective module ⇒ Perfect module

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: A bounded complex of finite projective modules is pseudo-coherent. Apply this to a finite projective resolution.
theorems.name: Perfect module ⇒ Pseudo-coherent module

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: A pseudo-coherent module has a resolution by finite free modules. The first two terms give a finite presentation.
theorems.name: Pseudo-coherent module ⇒ Finitely presented module

theorems.subject: module
theorems.proof: Successive syzygies over a Noetherian ring are finitely generated.
theorems.name: Module over a Noetherian ring + Finite module ⇒ Pseudo-coherent module

theorems.subject: ideal
theorems.proof: A generator is a finite generating family.
theorems.name: Principal ideal ⇒ Finitely generated ideal

theorems.subject: ideal
theorems.proof: The quotient by a maximal ideal is a field, hence a domain.
theorems.name: Maximal ideal ⇒ Prime ideal

theorems.subject: ideal
theorems.proof: A domain has no nonzero nilpotent elements.
theorems.name: Prime ideal ⇒ Radical ideal

theorems.subject: ideal
theorems.proof: A single exponent killing the ideal also kills every element.
theorems.name: Nilpotent ideal ⇒ Locally nilpotent ideal

theorems.subject: ideal
theorems.proof: If generators $x_i$ satisfy $x_i^{n_i}=0$, every monomial of total degree greater than the sum of the $n_i-1$ contains one of those powers.
theorems.name: Locally nilpotent ideal + Finitely generated ideal ⇒ Nilpotent ideal

theorems.subject: ideal
theorems.proof: Every ideal in a Noetherian ring is finitely generated.
theorems.name: Ideal in a Noetherian ring ⇒ Finitely generated ideal

theorems.subject: ideal
theorems.proof: The quotient flatness criterion identifies these conditions.
theorems.name: Pure ideal ⇔ Ideal satisfying the intersection-product test

theorems.subject: ideal
theorems.proof: The quotient flatness criterion also gives the condition on individual elements.
theorems.name: Pure ideal ⇔ Ideal with local unit for each element

theorems.subject: ideal
theorems.proof: The condition can also be imposed simultaneously on each finite family.
theorems.name: Pure ideal ⇔ Ideal with a common unit for each finite subset

theorems.subject: ideal
theorems.proof: Apply the common-unit condition to a generating family. The chosen element is idempotent and generates the ideal.
theorems.name: Pure ideal + Finitely generated ideal ⇔ Ideal generated by an idempotent

theorems.subject: ideal
theorems.proof: An idempotent splits the quotient map. Conversely, any section of the quotient splits the ambient module into ideals generated by complementary idempotents.
theorems.name: Ideal generated by an idempotent ⇔ Ideal with projective quotient

theorems.subject: ideal
theorems.proof: On every neighbourhood where regular generators exist, the Koszul complex is a resolution.
theorems.name: Regular ideal ⇒ Koszul-regular ideal

theorems.subject: ideal
theorems.proof: The same generators satisfy the required vanishing in degree one on each neighbourhood.
theorems.name: Koszul-regular ideal ⇒ H₁-regular ideal

theorems.subject: ideal
theorems.proof: The sequence implication from first Koszul homology to quasi-regularity applies on the same neighbourhoods.
theorems.name: H₁-regular ideal ⇒ Quasi-regular ideal

theorems.subject: ideal
theorems.proof: Quasi-regular generators locally on the vanishing set, together with the unit generator on its complement, yield finite generation.
theorems.name: Quasi-regular ideal ⇒ Finitely generated ideal

theorems.subject: ideal
theorems.proof: The degree-one graded piece is free on each principal neighbourhood from the definition. The conormal module is finite locally free over the quotient.
theorems.name: Quasi-regular ideal ⇒ Ideal with finite projective conormal module

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: A finite presentation supplies a finite generating family of the algebra.
theorems.name: Ring map of finite presentation ⇒ Ring map of finite type

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: A finite set of module generators also generates the target as an algebra.
theorems.name: Finite ring map ⇒ Ring map of finite type

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: A finite module presentation gives finite module generation and a finite algebra presentation.
theorems.name: Ring map with finitely presented target module ⇒ Finite ring map + Ring map of finite presentation

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: A finite free module has a finite presentation and its tensor functor is exact.
theorems.name: Ring map with finite free target module ⇒ Ring map with finitely presented target module + Flat ring map

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: The determinant trick yields a monic equation for each element of the target.
theorems.name: Finite ring map ⇒ Integral ring map

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: Reduce powers of each finite algebra generator using its monic equation. Products of bounded powers then generate the target as a module.
theorems.name: Integral ring map + Ring map of finite type ⇔ Finite ring map

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: Apply lying over to the inclusion of the source as a subring of the target.
theorems.name: Integral ring map + Injective ring map ⇒ Ring map surjective on spectra

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: Quotient by the chosen prime over the smaller prime and apply lying over.
theorems.name: Integral ring map ⇒ Going up for prime ideals

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: The fibre is integral over a field. Every prime in such an algebra is maximal.
theorems.name: Integral ring map ⇒ Incomparability of distinct primes in each fibre

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: A polynomial ring in finitely many variables over a Noetherian ring is Noetherian, so the kernel of its map onto the target is finitely generated.
theorems.name: Ring map with Noetherian source + Ring map of finite type ⇒ Ring map of finite presentation

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: Apply the finite-presentation theorem for flat algebras of finite type over a valuation ring.
theorems.name: Ring map with valuation-ring source + Flat ring map + Ring map of finite type ⇒ Ring map of finite presentation

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: Being a field is part of the definition.
theorems.name: Algebra over a perfect field ⇒ Algebra over a field

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: The geometric reducedness theorem over a perfect field supplies the assertion for all field extensions.
theorems.name: Algebra over a perfect field + Ring map with reduced target ⇒ Geometrically reduced algebra over a field

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: Use the trivial field extension to test the target.
theorems.name: Geometrically reduced algebra over a field ⇒ Algebra over a field + Ring map with reduced target

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: Over each extension the ring is a domain exactly when it is reduced with a nonempty irreducible spectrum.
theorems.name: Geometrically reduced algebra over a field + Geometrically irreducible algebra over a field ⇔ Geometrically integral algebra over a field

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: A nonempty irreducible space is connected. Apply this after every field extension.
theorems.name: Geometrically irreducible algebra over a field ⇒ Geometrically connected algebra over a field

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: Normality of a ring implies reducedness. Apply this after every field extension.
theorems.name: Geometrically normal algebra over a field ⇒ Geometrically reduced algebra over a field

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: Regular rings are normal. Test geometric normality after finitely generated field extensions by the equivalent criterion.
theorems.name: Geometrically regular Noetherian algebra over a field ⇒ Geometrically normal algebra over a field

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: For a flat map, surjectivity on spectra is equivalent to faithful flatness.
theorems.name: Flat ring map + Ring map surjective on spectra ⇔ Faithfully flat ring map

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: The spectrum-surjectivity criterion is preserved by every base change.
theorems.name: Ring map surjective on spectra ⇔ Ring map universally surjective on spectra

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: A faithfully flat map is universally injective as a module map. In particular, tensoring with the base ring shows ordinary injectivity.
theorems.name: Faithfully flat ring map ⇒ Injective ring map

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: Localize at the given target prime. The induced flat local map is faithfully flat, hence has a surjective map on spectra.
theorems.name: Flat ring map ⇒ Going down for prime ideals

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: The faithfully flat equalizer criterion shows such an epimorphism is an isomorphism.
theorems.name: Faithfully flat ring map + Epimorphism of rings ⇔ Ring isomorphism

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: A finite epimorphism is surjective, and a quotient ring is generated by the image of the unit as a module.
theorems.name: Finite ring map + Epimorphism of rings ⇔ Surjective ring map

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: The pushout of the two copies of the map is the tensor product of the target algebra with itself.
theorems.name: Epimorphism of rings ⇔ Tensor multiplication is an isomorphism

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: A ring epimorphism has at most one prime over each source prime.
theorems.name: Epimorphism of rings ⇒ Ring map injective on spectra

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: A quotient ring is of finite type and has zero relative differentials.
theorems.name: Surjective ring map ⇒ Unramified ring map

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: Finitely many generators of the kernel give a finite presentation. The relative differentials of a quotient vanish.
theorems.name: Surjective ring map with finitely generated kernel ⇒ Surjective ring map + G-unramified ring map

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: Localization is an exact tensor functor.
theorems.name: Localization map ⇒ Flat ring map

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: An element invertible modulo a nilpotent ideal already is invertible, and the universal property of localization gives the unique lift.
theorems.name: Localization map ⇒ Formally étale ring map

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: A map from a localization is uniquely determined by its restriction to the original ring.
theorems.name: Localization map ⇒ Epimorphism of rings

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: A principal localization has a finite presentation and is étale by the stated permanence result.
theorems.name: Principal localization map ⇒ Localization map + Étale ring map

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: A finitely presented flat quotient has an idempotent-generated kernel. Conversely a localization at an idempotent is a quotient with a single relation and is flat.
theorems.name: Surjective ring map + Flat ring map + Ring map of finite presentation ⇔ Localization at an idempotent

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: An idempotent is one element, so its localization is principal.
theorems.name: Localization at an idempotent ⇒ Principal localization map

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: Finite generators and relations detect factorization and equality at a finite stage of a directed system.
theorems.name: Ring map of finite presentation ⇔ Maps from the algebra commute with directed colimits

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: Tensor a finite generating family with the residue field.
theorems.name: Finite ring map ⇒ Ring map with finite-dimensional fibre algebras

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: The finite-dimensional fibre criterion for a finite type map.
theorems.name: Ring map of finite type + Ring map with finite-dimensional fibre algebras ⇔ Quasi-finite ring map

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: The unramified-at-a-prime criterion yields quasi-finiteness at every target prime.
theorems.name: Unramified ring map ⇒ Quasi-finite ring map

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: The invertible Jacobian minor gives the splitting of the presentation defining the naive cotangent complex.
theorems.name: Standard smooth ring map ⇒ Smooth ring map

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: Use the invertibility of the derivative and the Jacobian criterion for the localized one-variable presentation.
theorems.name: Standard étale ring map ⇒ Étale ring map

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: The naive cotangent complex is concentrated in degrees zero and one. The two homology conditions are the smoothness criterion.
theorems.name: Ring map of finite presentation + Ring map with vanishing first naive cotangent homology + Ring map with finite projective differentials ⇔ Smooth ring map

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: The standard smooth presentation locally on the target is syntomic.
theorems.name: Smooth ring map ⇒ Syntomic ring map

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: A Koszul-regular ideal is quasi-regular, hence finitely generated. Thus a finite polynomial presentation of a local complete intersection map is finitely presented.
theorems.name: Local complete intersection ring map ⇒ Ring map of finite presentation

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: The flat local-complete-intersection criterion is equivalent to the fibre definition.
theorems.name: Flat ring map + Local complete intersection ring map ⇔ Syntomic ring map

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: Finite presentation occurs in the definition of a syntomic map.
theorems.name: Syntomic ring map ⇒ Ring map of finite presentation

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: The naive cotangent complex is quasi-isomorphic to zero precisely when both its homology modules vanish.
theorems.name: Ring map of finite presentation + Ring map with vanishing first naive cotangent homology + Ring map with vanishing differentials ⇔ Étale ring map

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: The zero module is finite projective. An étale map meets the smoothness criterion with zero differentials.
theorems.name: Étale ring map ⇒ Smooth ring map

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: The criterion requires both flatness and G-unramifiedness, hence finite presentation.
theorems.name: Flat ring map + G-unramified ring map ⇔ Étale ring map

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: Étale maps are quasi-finite.
theorems.name: Étale ring map ⇒ Quasi-finite ring map

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: The condition is the conjunction of finiteness and étaleness.
theorems.name: Finite ring map + Étale ring map ⇔ Finite étale ring map

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: These are the two conditions defining unramifiedness.
theorems.name: Ring map of finite type + Ring map with vanishing differentials ⇔ Unramified ring map

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: G-unramifiedness uses finite presentation together with vanishing relative differentials.
theorems.name: Ring map of finite presentation + Ring map with vanishing differentials ⇔ G-unramified ring map

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: For a square-zero extension, the difference of two lifts is a derivation and conversely one may add any derivation to a lift.
theorems.name: Ring map with vanishing differentials ⇔ Formally unramified ring map

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: The finite presentation hypothesis is part of the equivalence between smoothness and formal smoothness.
theorems.name: Ring map of finite presentation + Formally smooth ring map ⇔ Smooth ring map

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: Existence and uniqueness of square-zero lifts are exactly the two lifting conditions together.
theorems.name: Formally smooth ring map + Formally unramified ring map ⇔ Formally étale ring map

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.proof: The formal lifting criterion for étaleness requires finite presentation.
theorems.name: Ring map of finite presentation + Formally étale ring map ⇔ Étale ring map

theorems.subject: ring-map-point
theorems.proof: On a principal neighbourhood where the map is étale, it is smooth.
theorems.name: Étale at a target prime ⇒ Smooth at a target prime

theorems.subject: ring-map-point
theorems.proof: An étale presentation on the neighbourhood is G-unramified.
theorems.name: Étale at a target prime ⇒ G-unramified at a target prime

theorems.subject: ring-map-point
theorems.proof: Every étale map near the chosen point is standard étale after further principal localization. The converse follows from standard étale implying étale.
theorems.name: Étale at a target prime ⇔ Standard étale on a principal neighbourhood

theorems.subject: ring-map-point
theorems.proof: Intersect the two principal neighbourhoods. Vanishing of differentials localizes, and localizing a finitely presented algebra at one element preserves finite presentation.
theorems.name: Unramified at a target prime + Finite presentation near a target prime ⇔ G-unramified at a target prime

theorems.subject: ring-map-point
theorems.proof: Unramifiedness at the chosen prime gives both residue conditions.
theorems.name: Unramified at a target prime ⇒ Maximal ideal generated from the base at a target prime + Finite separable residue extension at a target prime

theorems.subject: ring-map-point
theorems.proof: The smooth neighbourhood is flat of finite presentation, and flatness passes to the induced map on local rings.
theorems.name: Smooth at a target prime ⇒ Flatness at a target prime + Finite presentation near a target prime

theorems.subject: ring-map-point
theorems.proof: These hypotheses give smoothness by the fibre criterion. Conversely, a smooth neighbourhood is flat and finitely presented, and its base change to the residue field is smooth.
theorems.name: Finite presentation near a target prime + Flatness at a target prime + Smooth fibre at a target prime ⇔ Smooth at a target prime

theorems.subject: ring-map-point
theorems.proof: First restrict to the finitely presented principal neighbourhood, then use the flatness and residue conditions there. Conversely, an étale neighbourhood supplies finite presentation, flatness, and the stated residue conditions.
theorems.name: Finite presentation near a target prime + Flatness at a target prime + Maximal ideal generated from the base at a target prime + Finite separable residue extension at a target prime ⇔ Étale at a target prime

theorems.subject: ring-map-point
theorems.proof: The finite-type hypothesis allows the quasi-finiteness criterion for the fibre at the chosen prime.
theorems.name: Unramified at a target prime + Chosen point of a finite type ring map ⇒ Quasi-finite at a target prime

theorems.subject: ring-map-point
theorems.proof: For a finite-type map, the condition on the maximal ideal and separability of the residue extension give unramifiedness at the chosen point.
theorems.name: Chosen point of a finite type ring map + Maximal ideal generated from the base at a target prime + Finite separable residue extension at a target prime ⇒ Unramified at a target prime

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.proof: A finite Tor-amplitude bound lets one truncate the pseudo-coherent resolution to a bounded complex of finite projective modules.
theorems.name: Pseudo-coherent complex + Complex of finite Tor dimension ⇔ Perfect complex

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.proof: The specified interval provides the required bound.
theorems.name: Complex with Tor-amplitude in a given interval ⇒ Complex of finite Tor dimension

theorems.subject: field
theorems.proof: A characteristic-zero field contains the infinite prime subfield $\mathbf Q$.
theorems.name: Finite field ⇒ Positive characteristic

theorems.subject: field
theorems.proof: A number field is a finite extension of $\mathbf Q$, so its characteristic is zero.
theorems.name: Number field ⇒ Characteristic zero

theorems.subject: field
theorems.proof: The characteristic-zero case of the criterion for a perfect field.
theorems.name: Characteristic zero ⇒ Perfect field

theorems.subject: field
theorems.proof: The positive-characteristic case of the criterion for a perfect field.
theorems.name: Positive characteristic with surjective Frobenius ⇒ Perfect field

theorems.subject: field
theorems.proof: A finite field has positive characteristic. Frobenius is injective on a field and thus surjective on the finite underlying set.
theorems.name: Finite field ⇒ Positive characteristic with surjective Frobenius

theorems.subject: field
theorems.proof: Every separable algebraic extension is algebraic and hence trivial.
theorems.name: Algebraically closed field ⇒ Separably closed field

theorems.subject: field
theorems.proof: In positive characteristic, a root of $X^p-a$ lies in an algebraically closed field, for every element $a$. In characteristic zero every field is perfect.
refs: Stacks 09GR · polynomial criterion for algebraic closedness
theorems.name: Algebraically closed field ⇒ Perfect field

theorems.subject: field
theorems.proof: Over a perfect field, every algebraic extension is separable. If the field is also separably closed, each algebraic extension is therefore trivial. An algebraically closed field is perfect and separably closed.
theorems.name: Perfect field + Separably closed field ⇔ Algebraically closed field

theorems.subject: field
theorems.proof: Apply the minimal polynomial criterion to algebraic elements.
theorems.name: Every irreducible polynomial is linear ⇔ Algebraically closed field

theorems.subject: field
theorems.proof: An irreducible polynomial with a root is linear, and algebraic closedness ensures every nonconstant polynomial has a root.
theorems.name: Every nonconstant polynomial has a root ⇔ Algebraically closed field

theorems.subject: field
theorems.proof: Factor a polynomial into irreducibles. Splitting implies that every irreducible is linear.
theorems.name: Every nonconstant polynomial splits ⇔ Algebraically closed field

theorems.subject: field-polynomial-pair
theorems.proof: A nonconstant common irreducible factor gives a common root in an algebraic closure. A Bézout identity precludes a common root.
theorems.name: No common root in an algebraic closure ⇔ Relatively prime polynomials

theorems.subject: field-polynomial
theorems.proof: For an irreducible polynomial the derivative is relatively prime to the polynomial whenever it is nonzero, since it has smaller degree.
refs: Stacks 09H1 · definition of separable irreducible polynomial
theorems.name: Irreducible polynomial + Nonzero formal derivative ⇔ Separable irreducible polynomial

theorems.subject: field-polynomial
theorems.proof: A repeated root in an algebraic closure is precisely a common root of the polynomial and its derivative.
theorems.name: Irreducible polynomial + Only simple roots in an algebraic closure ⇔ Separable irreducible polynomial

theorems.subject: field-element
theorems.proof: The separability condition is imposed on the minimal polynomial of an algebraic element.
theorems.name: Separable algebraic element ⇒ Algebraic element

theorems.subject: field-element
theorems.proof: In characteristic $p>0$, $a$ is a root of $X^{p^r}-a^{p^r}\in F[X]$. An element of the base field is algebraic in any characteristic.
theorems.name: Purely inseparable element ⇒ Algebraic element

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.proof: A single generator gives a finite generating set.
theorems.name: Simple field extension ⇒ Finitely generated field extension

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.proof: Every finite set is at most countable.
theorems.name: Finitely generated field extension ⇒ Countably generated field extension

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.proof: Adjoin a finite algebraic generating set successively and multiply its finite degrees. Conversely a finite extension is algebraic, and a finite vector space basis generates the field.
theorems.name: Algebraic field extension + Finitely generated field extension ⇔ Finite field extension

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.proof: For an element $a$, the simple extension $F(a)$ is finite exactly when $a$ is algebraic over $F$.
theorems.name: Every simple subextension is finite ⇔ Algebraic field extension

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.proof: These are precisely the two defining conditions on $E/F$.
theorems.name: Algebraic field extension + Algebraically closed target field ⇔ Algebraic closure

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.proof: The adjective is used for an algebraic extension whose elements are separable.
theorems.name: Separable algebraic extension ⇒ Algebraic field extension

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.proof: Apply the polynomial $X^{p^r}-a^{p^r}$ to each element in positive characteristic, with equality handled in any characteristic.
theorems.name: Purely inseparable extension ⇒ Algebraic field extension

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.proof: Once the base has positive characteristic, the general and review definitions of pure inseparability agree.
theorems.name: Purely inseparable extension + Base field of positive characteristic ⇔ Purely inseparable extension in positive characteristic

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.proof: For $a^{p^r}\in F$, the polynomial $X^{p^r}-a^{p^r}=(X-a)^{p^r}$ over $E$ is divisible by the minimal polynomial of $a$, which therefore splits over $E$.
theorems.name: Purely inseparable extension ⇒ Normal field extension

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.proof: Each minimal polynomial of an element of a separable purely inseparable extension has only one distinct root and is separable, hence has degree one. A trivial extension satisfies both conditions.
theorems.name: Separable algebraic extension + Purely inseparable extension ⇔ Trivial extension

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.proof: All elements of an algebraic extension lie in its relative algebraic closure; if this is the base field the extension is trivial.
theorems.name: Algebraic field extension + Base field algebraically closed in the target ⇔ Trivial extension

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.proof: The empty set is a transcendence basis of an algebraic extension.
theorems.name: Separable algebraic extension ⇒ Separably generated extension

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.proof: A separably generated extension is separable in the general sense of Stacks 030O.
theorems.name: Separably generated extension ⇒ Separable field extension

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.proof: Take the independent generators as transcendence basis. The resulting algebraic extension is trivial and hence separable.
theorems.name: Purely transcendental extension ⇒ Separably generated extension

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.proof: For a simple subextension generated by an algebraic element, a transcendence basis is empty, so the general criterion forces this element to be separable.
theorems.name: Separable field extension + Algebraic field extension ⇔ Separable algebraic extension

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.proof: For a finitely generated separable extension, apply the definition of general separability to the whole extension.
theorems.name: Finitely generated field extension + Separable field extension ⇔ Finitely generated and separably generated extension

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.proof: The named condition is a conjunction of the two separately defined predicates.
theorems.name: Finitely generated field extension + Separably generated extension ⇔ Finitely generated and separably generated extension

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.proof: Geometric reducedness characterizes separability of a field extension in either characteristic.
theorems.name: Geometrically reduced field extension ⇔ Separable field extension

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.proof: Formal smoothness is equivalent to the general notion of separability for field extensions.
theorems.name: Formally smooth field extension ⇔ Separable field extension

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.proof: Each separable minimal polynomial has invertible derivative at its root, forcing the differential of that root to vanish.
theorems.name: Finite field extension + Separable algebraic extension ⇒ Vanishing relative differentials

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.proof: The finite-generation hypothesis is part of the criterion.
theorems.name: Finitely generated field extension + Vanishing relative differentials ⇒ Finite field extension + Separable algebraic extension

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.proof: A nonconstant polynomial in characteristic zero has nonzero derivative. Apply the criterion to the minimal polynomial of each element.
theorems.name: Base field of characteristic zero + Algebraic field extension ⇒ Separable algebraic extension

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.proof: For a finite extension the number of embeddings into an algebraic closure is at most the degree, with equality precisely in the separable case.
theorems.name: Finite field extension + Separable algebraic extension ⇔ Finite extension with the maximal number of embeddings

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.proof: The primitive element theorem applies to finite separable extensions.
theorems.name: Finite field extension + Separable algebraic extension ⇒ Simple field extension

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.proof: Each intermediate field is generated over the base by the coefficients of the minimal polynomial of the primitive element over that intermediate field. This polynomial must be one of the finitely many monic factors over the target.
theorems.name: Finite field extension + Simple field extension ⇒ Finitely many intermediate fields

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.proof: Over an infinite base, finitely many proper intermediate fields cannot cover the target vector space. For a finite base the target is a finite field with cyclic multiplicative group.
theorems.name: Finite field extension + Finitely many intermediate fields ⇒ Simple field extension

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.proof: The Stacks definition of normal extension starts with an algebraic extension.
theorems.name: Normal field extension ⇒ Algebraic field extension

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.proof: The image under an embedding contains every conjugate of every one of its elements precisely in the normal case.
theorems.name: Algebraic extension with a common image for all embeddings ⇔ Normal field extension

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.proof: The automorphism group embeds into the set of embeddings into an algebraic closure, and normality means every such embedding has image the target field.
theorems.name: Finite field extension + Normal field extension ⇔ Finite extension with as many automorphisms as its separable degree

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.proof: Both properties require algebraicity, and together they are the definition of a Galois extension.
theorems.name: Normal field extension + Separable algebraic extension ⇔ Galois extension

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.proof: The number of automorphisms is bounded by the separable degree, which in turn is bounded by the degree. Both equalities hold exactly for a finite Galois extension.
theorems.name: Finite field extension + Galois extension ⇔ Finite extension with as many automorphisms as its degree

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.proof: The cyclicity condition is imposed on a finite Galois extension.
theorems.name: Finite cyclic Galois extension ⇒ Finite field extension + Galois extension

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.proof: For a separable extension the sum of its distinct embeddings is nonzero by independence of characters. In a finite inseparable extension the trace is zero.
theorems.name: Finite field extension + Separable algebraic extension ⇔ Finite extension with nonzero trace map

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.proof: If the trace map is nonzero, choose $c$ of nonzero trace. Each nonzero $a$ pairs nontrivially with $a^{-1}c$. A zero trace map gives the zero pairing on the nonzero vector space.
theorems.name: Finite extension with nonzero trace map ⇔ Finite extension with nondegenerate trace pairing

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.proof: The matrix in a basis represents the linear map from the vector space to its dual. It is invertible exactly when its determinant is nonzero.
theorems.name: Finite extension with nondegenerate trace pairing ⇔ Finite extension with nonzero discriminant

theorems.subject: field-family
theorems.proof: These are the two defining conditions on the family.
theorems.name: Algebraically independent family + Target algebraic over the field generated by the family ⇔ Transcendence basis

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.proof: The empty family is algebraically independent and generates the base field. It is a transcendence basis precisely if the target is algebraic.
theorems.name: Transcendence degree zero ⇔ Algebraic field extension

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.proof: A subfield of a finite field is finite, and a generator of the cyclic group of units of the target generates the extension.
theorems.name: Finite target field ⇒ Finite base field + Finite field extension + Simple field extension

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.proof: Write $q=|F|$ and $[E:F]=n$. Every element of $E$ is a root of $X^{q^n}-X$, so $E$ is its splitting field, and the derivative is $-1$. The $q$-power Frobenius fixes $F$ and has order $n$: if its $i$th power were the identity for $0<i<n$, the degree-$q^i$ polynomial $X^{q^i}-X$ would have $q^n$ roots. The Galois group has order $n$, so this element generates it.
theorems.name: Finite target field ⇒ Finite cyclic Galois extension

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.proof: A finite-dimensional vector space over a finite field has finitely many elements.
theorems.name: Finite base field + Finite field extension ⇒ Finite target field

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.proof: The rational function field on an empty set of indeterminates is the base field.
theorems.name: Trivial extension ⇒ Purely transcendental extension

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.proof: A rational function involves only finitely many independent variables. In one variable any nonconstant rational function makes that variable algebraic over the subfield it generates. Induct on the number of variables by treating the last one over the rational function field on the others.
theorems.name: Purely transcendental extension ⇒ Base field algebraically closed in the target

theorems.subject: field-extension-pair
