theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.name: Vector space dimension of a rational function field
theorems.hypotheses: Let $T$ be transcendental over the field $F$.
theorems.statement: The extension $F(T)/F$ is infinite-dimensional. For an infinite field $F$ it has dimension $|F|$.
theorems.proof: The monomials give an infinite independent family. For each $a\in F$, the functions $1/(T-a)$ are linearly independent: clear the denominators in a finite relation and evaluate in turn at the corresponding values $a$. The number of rational functions is at most $|F|$ when $F$ is infinite.

theorems.subject: field
theorems.name: Field of meromorphic functions on a Riemann surface
theorems.hypotheses: Let $X$ be a connected Riemann surface.
theorems.statement: Meromorphic functions on $X$ form a field containing $\mathbf C$ via the constant functions. On the Riemann sphere this is $\mathbf C(T)$.
theorems.proof: A nonzero meromorphic function on a connected surface has a meromorphic inverse. On the sphere, subtract principal parts at its finitely many poles to obtain a constant holomorphic function.
refs: Stacks 09FY · constant functions give the extension of $\mathbf C$

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.name: Function field of a compact Riemann surface
theorems.hypotheses: Let $X$ be a compact connected Riemann surface and $f$ a nonconstant meromorphic function on $X$.
theorems.statement: The field $\mathbf C(X)$ is algebraic over $\mathbf C(f)$. It has transcendence degree one over $\mathbf C$.
theorems.proof: A nonconstant meromorphic function defines a finite holomorphic map to the sphere. For a meromorphic function on the source, the elementary symmetric functions in its values on the sheets define meromorphic coefficients on the sphere, giving an algebraic equation.
refs: Stacks 09IB · transcendence degree for the function field

theorems.subject: field-extension-pair
theorems.name: Common extension of two fields over a base
theorems.hypotheses: Let $E/F$ and $L/F$ be arbitrary field extensions.
theorems.statement: There is a field $M/F$ and injective $F$-maps from $E$ and $L$ to $M$.
theorems.proof: The tensor product $E\otimes_F L$ is nonzero. Quotient by a maximal ideal and use that unital maps from fields to the resulting field are injective.
refs: Stacks 09FU · field maps into nonzero rings

theorems.subject: field-tower
theorems.name: Degree in a tower of field extensions
theorems.hypotheses: Let $F\subseteq E\subseteq L$ be a tower of field extensions.
theorems.statement: $[L:F]=[L:E][E:F]$, with multiplication of cardinal numbers. If $L/F$ is finite, so are $L/E$ and $E/F$.
theorems.proof: Products of a basis of $L$ over $E$ with a basis of $E$ over $F$ form a basis of $L$ over $F$.
refs: Stacks 09G5 · finiteness over an intermediate field

theorems.subject: field-tower
theorems.name: Algebraicity in towers
theorems.hypotheses: Let $F\subseteq E\subseteq L$ be field extensions and let $a\in L$.
theorems.statement: If $a$ is algebraic over $F$ then it is algebraic over $E$. If $L/F$ is algebraic then $L/E$ is algebraic. If both $L/E$ and $E/F$ are algebraic then $L/F$ is algebraic.
theorems.proof: A polynomial with coefficients in $F$ is still a polynomial over $E$. For transitivity, the finitely many coefficients of a polynomial over $E$ belong to a finite extension of $F$.

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.name: Cardinality of an algebraic extension
theorems.hypotheses: Let $E/F$ be algebraic.
theorems.statement: The cardinality of $E$ is at most $\max(\aleph_0,|F|)$.
theorems.proof: There are at most this many nonzero polynomials in $F[T]$, and each has finitely many roots in $E$.

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.name: Algebraic elements form a subfield
theorems.hypotheses: Let $E/F$ be any field extension.
theorems.statement: The elements of $E$ algebraic over $F$ form the relative algebraic closure of $F$ in $E$.
theorems.proof: Any two such elements lie in a finite subextension, which also contains their sum, product and inverses when nonzero.

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.name: Intermediate subrings of algebraic extensions are fields
theorems.hypotheses: Let $E/F$ be algebraic and $F\subseteq A\subseteq E$ an intermediate unital subring.
theorems.statement: The subring $A$ is a field.
theorems.proof: For nonzero $a\in A$, its minimal polynomial over $F$ has nonzero constant term. Dividing the polynomial relation by $a$ expresses $a^{-1}$ as an $F$-polynomial in $a$.

theorems.subject: field-map
theorems.name: Endomorphisms of algebraic extensions are automorphisms
theorems.hypotheses: Let $E/F$ be algebraic and $u:E\to E$ a unital $F$-algebra map.
theorems.statement: The map $u$ is an $F$-automorphism.
theorems.proof: For every $a\in E$, the map permutes the finite set of roots in $E$ of the minimal polynomial of $a$ over $F$: injectivity gives a bijection on this set. Thus every $a$ is in the image.

theorems.subject: field-element
theorems.name: Minimal polynomial and degree of a simple extension
theorems.hypotheses: Let $a$ be algebraic over $F$ with minimal polynomial $P$ of degree $d$.
theorems.proof: Evaluation identifies $F(a)$ with $F[T]/(P)$ and the residue classes of $1,T,\dots,T^{d-1}$ form a basis.
refs: Stacks 09G7 · degree of a simple algebraic extension

theorems.subject: field
theorems.name: Existence and uniqueness of algebraic closures
theorems.hypotheses: Let $F$ be a field.
theorems.statement: There exists an algebraic closure of $F$. Any two are isomorphic over $F$, generally by more than one isomorphism.
theorems.proof: The construction adjoins algebraic roots in stages. An $F$-embedding of one algebraic closure in another is surjective, since its image is algebraically closed and the larger field is algebraic over it.
refs: Stacks 09GU · embedding into an algebraic closure

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.name: Embedding into an algebraic closure
theorems.hypotheses: Let $E/F$ be algebraic and let $\overline F$ be an algebraic closure of $F$.
theorems.statement: There exists an $F$-embedding $E\hookrightarrow\overline F$.
theorems.proof: Order partial $F$-embeddings of intermediate fields by extension. At a maximal partial embedding, a root of the transported minimal polynomial extends the map unless the entire domain has been embedded.

theorems.subject: field-polynomial
theorems.name: Decomposition of an inseparable irreducible polynomial
theorems.hypotheses: Let $P$ be an inseparable irreducible polynomial over a field $F$.
theorems.statement: The characteristic is $p>0$. There is a maximal power $q=p^r$ with $P(T)=Q(T^q)$, and $Q$ is irreducible and separable. The distinct roots of $P$ correspond to the distinct roots of $Q$ by the map $x\mapsto x^q$ in an algebraic closure.
theorems.proof: If the derivative is zero, all exponents with nonzero coefficient are multiples of $p$. Remove the largest common $p$-power from those exponents. The resulting derivative is nonzero and irreducibility descends to $Q$. Frobenius is bijective in the algebraic closure.
refs: Stacks 09H4 · the effect of Frobenius on the set of roots

theorems.subject: field-tower
theorems.name: Algebraic separability in towers
theorems.hypotheses: Let $F\subseteq E\subseteq L$ be a tower of algebraic field extensions.
theorems.statement: Elements separable over $F$ are separable over $E$, and separability of $L/F$ gives separability of both $E/F$ and $L/E$. If $L/E$ and $E/F$ are separable, then $L/F$ is separable.
theorems.proof: Changing the base upward replaces a minimal polynomial by a divisor. For transitivity, pass to finite intermediate extensions containing the elements and coefficients in question, then use the embedding count.

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.name: Separable elements form a subfield
theorems.hypotheses: Let $E/F$ be any field extension.
theorems.statement: The elements of $E$ separable over $F$ form a subfield containing $F$.
theorems.proof: Two separable elements generate a finite separable subextension by transitivity. This gives closure under the field operations.

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.name: Counting embeddings along a generating tower
theorems.hypotheses: Let $E=F(a_1,\dots,a_n)$ with each $a_i$ algebraic over $F$, and set $F_i=F(a_1,\dots,a_i)$. Let $P_i$ be the minimal polynomial of $a_i$ over $F_{i-1}$. Fix an algebraic closure $\overline F$.
theorems.statement: At each step, after choosing an embedding of $F_{i-1}$, the image of $a_i$ can be any distinct root of the transported $P_i$. This gives $\prod_{i=1}^n\deg_s(P_i)$ embeddings of $E$ over $F$. Their number equals $[E:F]$ if every step is separable and is smaller if some step is inseparable.
theorems.proof: The universal property of the simple-extension presentation gives one lift per root. The number of roots of the transported polynomial is the separable degree. Compare the product with the tower law.
refs: Stacks 09H7 · bijection with tuples of roots
Stacks 09H9 · criterion for separably generated finite towers

theorems.subject: field
theorems.name: Independence of distinct multiplicative characters
theorems.hypotheses: Let $F$ be a field and $G$ a monoid. Let $\chi_1,\dots,\chi_n:G\to(F,\cdot)$ be distinct monoid homomorphisms.
theorems.statement: These functions are linearly independent over $F$. In particular, distinct embeddings of an extension into $F$ are $F$-linearly independent as functions when their common domain and base are fixed.
theorems.proof: In a nontrivial linear relation of minimal support, compare the relation at $gh$ with the relation at $h$ multiplied by one of the character values at $g$. Choose $g$ on which two characters in the support differ. Subtraction gives a nonzero relation with smaller support.

theorems.subject: field
theorems.name: A nonzero power sum among distinct field elements
theorems.hypotheses: Let $a_1,\dots,a_n$ be pairwise distinct elements of a field $F$, with $n\geq 1$.
theorems.statement: There is an integer $e\geq0$ for which $\sum_i a_i^e\ne0$.
theorems.proof: The functions $e\mapsto a_i^e$ are distinct characters of the additive monoid of nonnegative integers. Their sum, whose coefficients are all $1$, cannot vanish identically.

theorems.subject: field-extension-pair
theorems.name: Splitting a finite separable extension after base change
theorems.hypotheses: Let $E/F$ be finite separable, and let $L/F$ be a field extension with $L$ algebraically closed.
theorems.statement: The map $E\otimes_F L\to\prod_{\sigma:E\hookrightarrow L}L$ given by $a\otimes b\mapsto(\sigma(a)b)_\sigma$ is an isomorphism of $L$-algebras.
theorems.proof: The primitive element theorem writes $E$ as a polynomial quotient. The minimal polynomial splits into distinct linear factors over $L$, and the Chinese remainder theorem gives the product.

theorems.subject: field-polynomial
theorems.name: Irreducibility of a missing pth root polynomial
theorems.hypotheses: Let $F$ have characteristic $p>0$ and let $a\in F$ be an element outside $F^p$.
theorems.statement: The polynomial $X^p-a$ is irreducible in $F[X]$.
theorems.proof: In an algebraic closure it is $(X-b)^p$. A proper nonconstant monic factor of degree $d<p$ would have coefficient $-db$ in $F$, forcing $b\in F$.

theorems.subject: field-tower
theorems.name: Pure inseparability in towers
theorems.hypotheses: Let $F\subseteq E\subseteq L$ be a tower, and assume $L/E$ and $E/F$ are purely inseparable.
theorems.statement: The extension $L/F$ is purely inseparable.
theorems.proof: In characteristic $p>0$, apply first a $p$-power carrying an element from $L$ to $E$, then a further $p$-power carrying its image to $F$. In characteristic zero the two extensions are trivial.

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.name: Purely inseparable elements form a subfield
theorems.hypotheses: Let $E/F$ be any field extension.
theorems.statement: The elements of $E$ purely inseparable over $F$ form a subfield containing $F$.
theorems.proof: For two such elements in positive characteristic, take a common exponent to send them to $F$ by the same Frobenius power, which respects the field operations. In characteristic zero the subfield is $F$.

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.name: A finite purely inseparable extension is built from pth roots
theorems.hypotheses: Let $E/F$ be finite purely inseparable with characteristic $p>0$.
theorems.statement: There is a finite tower from $F$ to $E$ whose nontrivial steps have degree $p$ and are obtained by adjoining a $p$th root. Consequently $[E:F]$ is a power of $p$.
theorems.proof: If an element is outside the current field, take its penultimate $p$-power for a minimal exponent that puts a power into that field. This produces a degree-$p$ step by the missing-root criterion. Finite degree bounds the number of steps.

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.name: Canonical separable and purely inseparable factorization
theorems.hypotheses: Let $E/F$ be algebraic.
theorems.statement: There is a unique intermediate field $E_s$ such that $E_s/F$ is separable and $E/E_s$ is purely inseparable. It consists of the elements of $E$ separable over $F$.
theorems.proof: An inseparable minimal polynomial is a separable irreducible polynomial in a $p$-power of its variable. This sends each element into the separable subfield by some $p$-power. A separable and purely inseparable extension is trivial, which yields uniqueness.

theorems.subject: field-tower
theorems.name: Separable and inseparable degrees in towers
theorems.hypotheses: Let $F\subseteq E\subseteq L$ be a tower of algebraic extensions.
theorems.statement: $[L:F]_s=[L:E]_s[E:F]_s$ and $[L:F]_i=[L:E]_i[E:F]_i$. For finite extensions the separable degree is the number of embeddings into an algebraic closure.
theorems.proof: Use the separable-first factorization and the degrees in the resulting tower. For the finite embedding statement, an embedding of the separable part extends uniquely across the purely inseparable part.
refs: Stacks 09HJ · finite separable degree and embeddings

theorems.subject: field-tower
theorems.name: Normality over an intermediate field
theorems.hypotheses: Let $L/F$ be normal and $F\subseteq E\subseteq L$.
theorems.statement: The extension $L/E$ is normal. If $L/F$ is Galois then $L/E$ is Galois.
theorems.proof: A minimal polynomial over $E$ divides a polynomial over $F$ that splits in $L$. The same divisor argument preserves separability.
refs: Stacks 09I2 · Galois extensions over intermediate fields

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.name: Intersections of normal subextensions
theorems.hypotheses: Let $L/F$ be algebraic and let $(E_i)_{i\in I}$ be a nonempty family of subextensions normal over $F$.
theorems.statement: Their intersection in $L$ is normal over $F$.
theorems.proof: For any element in the intersection, all the roots of its minimal polynomial over $F$ belong to each $E_i$.

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.name: The separable part of a normal extension is Galois
theorems.hypotheses: Let $E/F$ be normal and let $E_s$ be its maximal separable subextension.
theorems.statement: The extension $E_s/F$ is Galois, and $E/E_s$ is purely inseparable and normal.
theorems.proof: Every conjugate of an element separable over $F$ is again separable over $F$. Normality of $E/F$ puts all the conjugates in $E$, hence in $E_s$. Normality over $E_s$ follows by passage to an intermediate field.

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.name: Normality from the minimal polynomials of generators
theorems.hypotheses: Let $E/F$ be algebraic and suppose a family $(a_i)$ generates $E$ over $F$.
theorems.statement: The extension is normal exactly when the minimal polynomial over $F$ of each $a_i$ splits over $E$.
theorems.proof: If every generating polynomial splits, every embedding into an algebraic closure carries the field into itself. The same finite-root permutation argument as for an algebraic endomorphism gives equality of images.

theorems.subject: field-tower
theorems.name: Restriction and extension of automorphisms in normal towers
theorems.hypotheses: Let $F\subseteq E\subseteq L$ be a tower of algebraic field extensions.
theorems.statement: If $E/F$ is normal, every $F$-automorphism of $L$ preserves $E$. If $L/F$ is normal, every $F$-embedding $E\to L$ extends to an $F$-automorphism of $L$.
theorems.proof: Normality of $E/F$ fixes the image of $E$ under any embedding. For extension, enlarge the embedding into an algebraic closure using the algebraic embedding theorem. Normality of $L/F$ then makes its image equal to $L$.

theorems.subject: field-map
theorems.name: Embeddings of a normal extension differ by an automorphism
theorems.hypotheses: Let $E/F$ be algebraic normal and let $L/F$ be a field extension admitting an $F$-embedding $u:E\to L$.
theorems.statement: Every $F$-embedding $v:E\to L$ has the unique form $u\circ\sigma$ with $\sigma\in\operatorname{Aut}_F(E)$.
theorems.proof: The images of $u$ and $v$ coincide because both contain precisely all conjugates of elements of $E$ under the generating description. Set $\sigma=u^{-1}v$.

theorems.subject: field-polynomial
theorems.name: Existence and normality of splitting fields
theorems.hypotheses: Let $P\in F[T]$ be nonconstant over a field $F$.
theorems.statement: The subfield of an algebraic closure generated by all roots of $P$ is a finite normal extension of $F$, unique up to $F$-isomorphism. Every extension in which $P$ splits contains an $F$-isomorphic copy of it.
theorems.proof: There are finitely many algebraic roots. Embeddings permute the roots, which yields normality. Successively choosing corresponding roots yields a map to any field in which the polynomial splits.

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.name: Finite normal closures
theorems.hypotheses: Let $E/F$ be finite and view $E$ inside an algebraic closure of $F$.
theorems.statement: There is a least intermediate field containing $E$ and normal over $F$. It is finite over $F$, and it is Galois over $F$ when $E/F$ is separable.
theorems.proof: Take the splitting field of the product of the minimal polynomials of finitely many generators. Every normal field containing the generators contains their conjugates. In the separable case every adjoined root is separable.
refs: Stacks 0EXM · normal closure of a finite separable extension

theorems.subject: field-tower
theorems.name: Finite normal subextensions inside a normal extension
theorems.hypotheses: Let $L/F$ be algebraic normal and $E$ an intermediate field.
theorems.statement: If $E/F$ is finite, its normal closure over $F$ lies in $L$ and is finite. If $E/F$ is normal and $M/E$ is a finite intermediate extension in $L$, then $M$ is contained in an intermediate field normal over $F$ and finite over $E$.
theorems.proof: For the first statement all roots required by the normal closure already lie in $L$. For the second, choose a finite set of generators of $M/E$ and adjoin all their conjugates over $F$ to $E$.

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.name: Normal closure as a quotient of a tensor product
theorems.hypotheses: Let $E/F$ be finite and let $N$ be its normal closure in an algebraic closure of $F$.
theorems.statement: The tensor product over $F$ of $[E:F]_s$ copies of $E$ has a surjective $F$-algebra map onto $N$.
theorems.proof: Index the tensor factors by the embeddings of $E$ into the algebraic closure. Their images generate the normal closure. The subalgebra they generate is a field because it is an intermediate subring of an algebraic extension.
refs: Stacks 0BID · algebraic intermediate subrings are fields

theorems.subject: field
theorems.name: Finite subgroups of the multiplicative group are cyclic
theorems.hypotheses: Let $H$ be a finite subgroup of $F^\times$ for a field $F$.
theorems.statement: The group $H$ is cyclic. For each positive integer $n$, the subgroup of $n$th roots of unity is cyclic of order dividing $n$.
theorems.proof: If $n$ is an exponent of the group, for each $d$ dividing $n$ the elements of order dividing $d$ are roots of $T^d-1$ and number at most $d$. The cyclicity criterion for abelian groups applies.

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.name: Characteristic polynomial, trace and norm from a minimal polynomial
theorems.hypotheses: Let $E/F$ be finite, and let $a\in E$ have monic minimal polynomial $P(T)=T^d+c_1T^{d-1}+\cdots+c_d$. Put $m=[E:F(a)]$.
theorems.statement: The characteristic polynomial of multiplication by $a$ is $P(T)^m$. Consequently $\operatorname{Tr}_{E/F}(a)=-mc_1$ and $\operatorname{N}_{E/F}(a)=(-1)^{[E:F]}c_d^m$.
theorems.proof: Choose an $F(a)$-basis of $E$. On each of the resulting summands the multiplication operator has characteristic polynomial $P$. Compare the leading and constant coefficients.

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.name: Trace and determinant under restriction of scalars
theorems.hypotheses: Let $E/F$ be finite, $V$ a finite-dimensional $E$-vector space, and $u$ an $E$-linear endomorphism.
theorems.statement: $\operatorname{Tr}_F(u)=\operatorname{Tr}_{E/F}(\operatorname{Tr}_E(u))$ and $\det_F(u)=\operatorname{N}_{E/F}(\det_E(u))$.
theorems.proof: The trace follows by writing the $E$-matrix entries as multiplication operators on the $F$-vector space $E$. For the determinant, check elementary matrices and diagonal matrices in the invertible case. A singular map has zero determinant over both fields.

theorems.subject: field-tower
theorems.name: Transitivity of trace and norm
theorems.hypotheses: Let $F\subseteq E\subseteq L$ be a tower of finite field extensions.
theorems.statement: $\operatorname{Tr}_{L/F}=\operatorname{Tr}_{E/F}\circ\operatorname{Tr}_{L/E}$ and $\operatorname{N}_{L/F}=\operatorname{N}_{E/F}\circ\operatorname{N}_{L/E}$.
theorems.proof: Apply restriction of scalars to the $E$-linear map on $L$ given by multiplication by each element of $L$.

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.name: Discriminant of a quadratic field extension
theorems.hypotheses: Let $E/F$ have degree $2$ and let $u\in E\setminus F$ have minimal polynomial $T^2+bT+c$.
theorems.statement: The discriminant in the basis $(1,u)$ is $b^2-4c$. In characteristic $2$ it is zero in the purely inseparable case and has trivial nonzero square class in the separable case. In characteristic different from $2$ it is a nonsquare and adjoining its square root gives $E$.
theorems.proof: Use the multiplication matrices for $1$, $u$ and $u^2$ to compute the trace-pairing determinant. In characteristic $2$ the derivative is $b$, while in other characteristics the identity $(2u+b)^2=b^2-4c$ gives the quadratic description.
refs: Stacks 0BIL · separability and the trace pairing

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.name: A faithful finite group action yields a Galois extension
theorems.hypotheses: Let a finite group $G$ act faithfully by field automorphisms on a field $E$.
theorems.statement: For the fixed field $F=E^G$, the extension $E/F$ is finite Galois with degree $|G|$, and the given action identifies $G$ with $\operatorname{Gal}(E/F)$.
theorems.proof: The polynomial attached to each finite orbit has coefficients in $F$ and distinct roots. The field degree is bounded by $|G|$ using these orbit polynomials and the primitive element theorem on finite subextensions. Independence of distinct automorphisms gives the opposite bound.

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.name: Finite Galois correspondence
theorems.hypotheses: Let $E/F$ be finite Galois with group $G$.
theorems.statement: The assignments $H\mapsto E^H$ and $M\mapsto\operatorname{Gal}(E/M)$ are inverse inclusion-reversing bijections between subgroups and intermediate fields. Normal subgroups correspond to intermediate extensions Galois over $F$.
theorems.proof: Apply the fixed-field theorem to each subgroup. Over any intermediate field the extension is Galois, so that intermediate field is the fixed field of its automorphism group. Conjugation transports fixed fields and detects normality.
refs: Stacks 09I2 · Galois extensions over intermediate fields

theorems.subject: field-tower
theorems.name: Galois restriction exact sequence
theorems.hypotheses: Let $F\subseteq E\subseteq L$ with $L/F$ and $E/F$ Galois, finite or infinite.
theorems.statement: Restriction gives $1\to\operatorname{Gal}(L/E)\to\operatorname{Gal}(L/F)\to\operatorname{Gal}(E/F)\to1$. With Krull topologies these are continuous maps and the sequence is exact as profinite groups.
theorems.proof: The kernel consists of the automorphisms fixing $E$. An $F$-automorphism of $E$ extends to $L$ by normality. Continuity is checked on the stabilizers of finite subsets.

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.name: Galois groups are profinite in the Krull topology
theorems.hypotheses: Let $E/F$ be Galois. Give $E$ the discrete topology and $G=\operatorname{Gal}(E/F)$ the topology of pointwise convergence.
theorems.statement: The group $G$ is the inverse limit of the finite Galois groups of the finite Galois subextensions of $E/F$, with surjective restriction maps. Its underlying space is profinite.
theorems.proof: Finite Galois subextensions are directed under inclusion and exhaust $E$. Compatible automorphisms on them give a unique automorphism of $E$. Finite-subextension restriction determines the topology.
refs: Stacks 0BU2 · inverse limit over finite Galois subextensions

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.name: Infinite Galois correspondence
theorems.hypotheses: Let $E/F$ be Galois with Krull-topological group $G$.
theorems.statement: Closed subgroups of $G$ and intermediate fields correspond contravariantly by fixed field and pointwise stabilizer. Open subgroups correspond to finite subextensions, and closed normal subgroups to Galois subextensions.
theorems.proof: Apply the finite Galois correspondence to the finite Galois subextensions. A subgroup is recovered from its finite restriction images precisely when it is closed.

theorems.subject: field
theorems.name: Algebraic closedness of the complex numbers
theorems.hypotheses: Let the field be $\mathbf C$.
theorems.statement: Every nonconstant polynomial over $\mathbf C$ has a root, and $\mathbf C$ is algebraically closed.
theorems.proof: If a nonconstant polynomial has no zero, its reciprocal is bounded and entire, contradicting Liouville’s theorem.

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.name: Kummer generator for a cyclic Galois extension
theorems.hypotheses: Let $E/F$ be cyclic Galois of degree $n$. Assume that the characteristic of $F$ does not divide $n$, and that $F$ contains a primitive $n$th root of unity.
theorems.statement: There is an element $z\in E$ with $E=F(z)$ and $z^n\in F$.
theorems.proof: The linear operator given by a generator of the cyclic group has an eigenvector for a primitive $n$th root of unity by the character projection and independence of automorphisms. The vector has an orbit of size $n$, and its $n$th power is fixed.

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.name: Adjoining a primitive root of unity of prime order
theorems.hypotheses: Let $p$ be prime, $\operatorname{char}(F)\ne p$, and $\zeta$ a primitive $p$th root of unity in an algebraic closure.
theorems.statement: $F(\zeta)/F$ is Galois, with degree dividing $p-1$.
theorems.proof: It splits $T^p-1$, which has distinct roots, and its Galois group embeds in $(\mathbf Z/p\mathbf Z)^\times$ by its faithful action on $\zeta$.

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.name: Intermediate fields in a radical extension
theorems.hypotheses: Let $E=F(a)$ have degree $e$ over $F$, with $a^e\in F$. Assume every $e$th root of unity in $E$ belongs to $F$.
theorems.statement: Each intermediate field is $F(a^d)$ for some divisor $d$ of $e$.
theorems.proof: Use the source result on radical extensions. Its root-of-unity hypothesis and the equality between the exponent and the field degree are both required here.

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.name: Artin–Schreier generator for a cyclic degree-p extension
theorems.hypotheses: Let $F$ have characteristic $p>0$ and let $E/F$ be cyclic Galois of degree $p$.
theorems.statement: There is an element $z\in E$ with $E=F(z)$ and $z^p-z\in F$.
theorems.proof: For a generator $\sigma$ of the Galois group, the $F$-linear operator $\sigma-1$ has image equal to the trace-zero subspace. As $1$ has trace zero, choose $z$ with $\sigma(z)-z=1$. This gives the full orbit and makes $z^p-z$ invariant.

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.name: Existence and size of transcendence bases
theorems.hypotheses: Let $E/F$ be any field extension.
theorems.statement: Transcendence bases exist and all have the same cardinality.
theorems.proof: Take a maximal algebraically independent family by Zorn’s lemma. Exchange of algebraically independent elements gives invariance of cardinality.

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.name: Transcendence degree of fields generated by special real numbers
theorems.hypotheses: Use the real numbers $e$ and $\pi$ over $\mathbf Q$.
theorems.statement: The field $\mathbf Q(\pi)$ is purely transcendental of transcendence degree one. The transcendence degree of $\mathbf Q(e,\pi)$ is at least one and at most two.
theorems.proof: The transcendence of $\pi$ makes it a single algebraically independent generator. For the second field, the two generators bound the transcendence degree above, and its subfield $\mathbf Q(\pi)$ gives the lower bound.

theorems.subject: field-family
theorems.name: Distinct transcendence bases of the same field extension
theorems.hypotheses: Let $T$ be an indeterminate over $F$ and take the extension $F(T)/F$.
theorems.statement: Both $(T)$ and $(T^2)$ are transcendence bases of the same field extension.
theorems.proof: Both elements are transcendental, and $T$ is algebraic over $F(T^2)$ because it is a root of $X^2-T^2$. This argument also applies in characteristic two.

theorems.subject: field-tower
theorems.name: Transcendence degree in a tower
theorems.hypotheses: Let $F\subseteq E\subseteq L$ be a tower of field extensions.
theorems.statement: $\operatorname{trdeg}_F L=\operatorname{trdeg}_F E+\operatorname{trdeg}_E L$, using cardinal addition.
theorems.proof: The union of a transcendence basis of $E/F$ and a transcendence basis of $L/E$ is a transcendence basis of $L/F$.

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.name: Adjoining indeterminates preserves finite extension degree
theorems.hypotheses: Let $E/F$ be finite and $x_1,\dots,x_r$ algebraically independent over $E$.
theorems.statement: $[E(x_1,\dots,x_r):F(x_1,\dots,x_r)]=[E:F]$.
theorems.proof: An $F$-basis of $E$ remains linearly independent over the rational function field of $F$ by clearing denominators and comparing coefficients. It spans the resulting finite field extension.

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.name: Relative algebraic closure in a finitely generated extension
theorems.hypotheses: Let $E/F$ be a finitely generated field extension.
theorems.statement: The relative algebraic closure of $F$ in $E$ is finite over $F$.
theorems.proof: Choose a finite transcendence basis $S$ of $E/F$. Every finite subextension of the relative algebraic closure has degree over $F$ at most $[E:F(S)]$ by adjoining $S$ and using the tower law. The bounded degrees force the relative algebraic closure to be finite.
refs: Stacks 0G1M · degree unchanged by adjoining indeterminates

theorems.subject: field-extension
theorems.name: Tensor product decomposition of a normal algebraic extension
theorems.hypotheses: Let $E/F$ be algebraic normal. Let $E_s$ and $E_i$ be the subfields of separable and purely inseparable elements over $F$.
theorems.statement: The extension $E_s/F$ is Galois and $E/E_s$ purely inseparable. The extension $E_i/F$ is purely inseparable and $E/E_i$ Galois. Multiplication identifies $E_s\otimes_F E_i$ with $E$.
theorems.proof: The separable part is the canonical separable subextension. In a normal extension the purely inseparable part is fixed by all base-field automorphisms. The source result gives the two factorizations and linear disjointness.
refs: Stacks 0EXK · normality of the separable part

theorems.subject: field-element
theorems.name: A pth-root test in a separable algebraic extension
theorems.hypotheses: Let $E/F$ be separable algebraic in characteristic $p>0$ and let $a\in E$. Assume $a$ is a root of a polynomial $P\in F[T]$ with distinct roots in an algebraic closure and coefficients in $F^p$.
theorems.statement: The element $a$ is a $p$th power in $E$. This applies in particular if its minimal polynomial over $F$ has all coefficients in $F^p$.
theorems.proof: Take $p$th roots of the coefficients of $P$ to obtain a polynomial $Q$ with distinct roots. A $p$th root of $a$ is a root of $Q$. If it were absent from $E$, the irreducible polynomial $T^p-a$ over $E$ would divide $Q$, contradicting distinct roots.
refs: Stacks 09HF · irreducibility of a missing pth-root polynomial

theorems.subject: ring-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Henselian local rings and pairs
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be a local ring with its unique maximal ideal.
theorems.statement: The local ring is henselian if and only if the pair $(A,\mathfrak m)$ is henselian.
theorems.proof: The local ring is henselian if and only if the pair $(A,\mathfrak m)$ is henselian.

theorems.subject: ring-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Finite étale algebras over a henselian pair
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(A,I)$ be a henselian pair.
theorems.statement: Base change $B\mapsto B/IB$ gives an equivalence from finite étale $A$-algebras to finite étale $A/I$-algebras.
theorems.proof: Base change $B\mapsto B/IB$ gives an equivalence from finite étale $A$-algebras to finite étale $A/I$-algebras.

theorems.subject: ring-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Radical invariance of the henselian pair property
theorems.hypotheses: Let $I,J$ be ideals of $A$ with $\sqrt I=\sqrt J$.
theorems.statement: The pair $(A,I)$ is henselian if and only if $(A,J)$ is henselian.
theorems.proof: The pair $(A,I)$ is henselian if and only if $(A,J)$ is henselian.

theorems.subject: ring-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Henselianity along a chain of ideals
theorems.hypotheses: Let $I\subseteq J$ be ideals of a commutative ring $A$.
theorems.statement: The pair $(A,J)$ is henselian if and only if both $(A,I)$ and $(A/I,J/I)$ are henselian.
theorems.proof: The pair $(A,J)$ is henselian if and only if both $(A,I)$ and $(A/I,J/I)$ are henselian.

theorems.subject: module-system
theorems.name: Module colimit as a quotient of a direct sum
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(M_i,\mu_{ij})$ be a system of $R$-modules over a preordered set $I$.
theorems.statement: Its colimit is $\bigoplus_i M_i$ modulo the submodule generated by differences between $x\in M_i$ and its image $\mu_{ij}(x)$ in $M_j$, for all $i\leq j$. The maps from $M_i$ are the compositions of the inclusions and the quotient map.
theorems.proof: Its colimit is $\bigoplus_i M_i$ modulo the submodule generated by differences between $x\in M_i$ and its image $\mu_{ij}(x)$ in $M_j$, for all $i\leq j$. The maps from $M_i$ are the compositions of the inclusions and the quotient map.

theorems.subject: module-system
theorems.name: Representatives of a directed colimit
theorems.hypotheses: Let the indexing preorder of the module system be directed.
theorems.statement: Every colimit element has a representative in a single term. Representatives are equal precisely if their images agree in a common later term. Addition takes place at a common later term, and scalar multiplication takes place on a representative.
theorems.proof: Every colimit element has a representative in a single term. Representatives are equal precisely if their images agree in a common later term. Addition takes place at a common later term, and scalar multiplication takes place on a representative.

theorems.subject: module-system
theorems.name: A morphism of systems induces a morphism of colimits
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(\phi_i)$ be a morphism of two systems of $R$-modules over the same preordered index set.
theorems.statement: There is a unique map of colimits taking the class of $x$ from term $i$ to the class of $\phi_i(x)$. Compatibility with the transitions makes this map well defined.
theorems.proof: There is a unique map of colimits taking the class of $x$ from term $i$ to the class of $\phi_i(x)$. Compatibility with the transitions makes this map well defined.

theorems.subject: module-system
theorems.name: Directed colimits commute with homology
theorems.hypotheses: Let $L_i\to M_i\to N_i$ be compatible complexes over a directed index set. Write $H_i$ for the middle homology.
theorems.statement: The middle homology of the colimit complex is canonically the colimit of the middle homologies. In particular, taking directed colimits of exact sequences of modules is exact.
theorems.proof: The middle homology of the colimit complex is canonically the colimit of the middle homologies. In particular, taking directed colimits of exact sequences of modules is exact.

theorems.subject: module-system
theorems.name: Exact colimits over unions of filtered components
theorems.hypotheses: Let the small indexing category satisfy the following conditions. Every pair of arrows with a common source can be completed to a commutative square. Every parallel pair is equalized by postcomposing with some arrow.
theorems.statement: Colimits of diagrams of abelian groups over that category preserve exact sequences.
theorems.proof: Colimits of diagrams of abelian groups over that category preserve exact sequences.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Universal property of ring localization
theorems.hypotheses: Let $S\subseteq R$ be multiplicative. Let $R\to B$ send every element of $S$ to a unit.
theorems.statement: There is exactly one factorization through $S^{-1}R$, given on a fraction by sending its numerator to its image and multiplying by the inverse of the image of its denominator.
theorems.proof: There is exactly one factorization through $S^{-1}R$, given on a fraction by sending its numerator to its image and multiplying by the inverse of the image of its denominator.

theorems.subject: ring-subset
theorems.name: Criterion for a localization to be the zero ring
theorems.hypotheses: Let $S$ be a multiplicative subset of $R$.
theorems.statement: The ring $S^{-1}R$ is zero exactly when $0\in S$. Indeed $1/1=0/1$ precisely when some element of $S$ annihilates $1$.
theorems.proof: The ring $S^{-1}R$ is zero exactly when $0\in S$. Indeed $1/1=0/1$ precisely when some element of $S$ annihilates $1$.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Modules over a localization
theorems.hypotheses: Let $S\subseteq R$ be multiplicative.
theorems.statement: Restriction of scalars is an equivalence from $S^{-1}R$-modules to the full subcategory of $R$-modules on which every element of $S$ acts invertibly.
theorems.proof: Restriction of scalars is an equivalence from $S^{-1}R$-modules to the full subcategory of $R$-modules on which every element of $S$ acts invertibly.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Universal property of module localization
theorems.hypotheses: Let $M,N$ be $R$-modules and $S\subseteq R$ multiplicative. Suppose each $s\in S$ acts invertibly on $N$.
theorems.statement: Precomposition with $M\to S^{-1}M$ gives an isomorphism $\operatorname{Hom}_R(S^{-1}M,N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_R(M,N)$.
theorems.proof: Precomposition with $M\to S^{-1}M$ gives an isomorphism $\operatorname{Hom}_R(S^{-1}M,N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_R(M,N)$.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Prime, principal and total-quotient localizations
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be a ring and $M$ an $R$-module.
theorems.statement: A prime $\mathfrak p$ gives localization at $R\setminus\mathfrak p$. An element $f$ gives localization at its powers, and $R_f=0$ exactly when $f$ is nilpotent. Inverting all nonzerodivisors gives the total quotient ring, which is the fraction field when $R$ is a domain.
theorems.proof: A prime $\mathfrak p$ gives localization at $R\setminus\mathfrak p$. An element $f$ gives localization at its powers, and $R_f=0$ exactly when $f$ is nilpotent. Inverting all nonzerodivisors gives the total quotient ring, which is the fraction field when $R$ is a domain.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Localization is a colimit of principal localizations
theorems.hypotheses: Let $S\subseteq R$ be multiplicative and $M$ an $R$-module. Order $S$ by divisibility in $R$.
theorems.statement: There is a canonical isomorphism $S^{-1}M\cong\varinjlim_{f\in S}M_f$. If $f=f'h$, the transition sends $m/(f')^e$ to $mh^e/f^e$.
theorems.proof: There is a canonical isomorphism $S^{-1}M\cong\varinjlim_{f\in S}M_f$. If $f=f'h$, the transition sends $m/(f')^e$ to $mh^e/f^e$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Localizing a ring twice
theorems.hypotheses: Let $S,S'$ be multiplicative subsets of $R$. Let $\overline S$ be the image of $S$ in $(S')^{-1}R$.
theorems.statement: There is a canonical $R$-algebra isomorphism $(SS')^{-1}R\cong\overline S^{-1}((S')^{-1}R)$, since both localizations invert $S$ and $S'$.
theorems.proof: There is a canonical $R$-algebra isomorphism $(SS')^{-1}R\cong\overline S^{-1}((S')^{-1}R)$, since both localizations invert $S$ and $S'$.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Localizing a module twice
theorems.hypotheses: Let $S,S'\subseteq R$ be multiplicative and $M$ an $R$-module.
theorems.statement: The canonical comparison identifies $S^{-1}((S')^{-1}M)$ with $(SS')^{-1}M$.
theorems.proof: The canonical comparison identifies $S^{-1}((S')^{-1}M)$ with $(SS')^{-1}M$.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Localization of a quotient module
theorems.hypotheses: Let $N\subseteq M$ be $R$-modules and $S\subseteq R$ multiplicative.
theorems.statement: There is a canonical isomorphism $S^{-1}(M/N)\cong (S^{-1}M)/(S^{-1}N)$, with the denominator on the right embedded by exactness.
theorems.proof: There is a canonical isomorphism $S^{-1}(M/N)\cong (S^{-1}M)/(S^{-1}N)$, with the denominator on the right embedded by exactness.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Localization is exact
theorems.hypotheses: Let $S$ be multiplicative in $R$. Let $L\to M\to N$ be a complex of $R$-modules exact at $M$.
theorems.statement: The localized complex is exact at $S^{-1}M$. A class in the kernel is represented by a fraction $m/s$ whose numerator maps to an element annihilated by some $t\in S$. Thus $tm$ comes from $L$, and replacing $m/s$ by $tm/(ts)$ exhibits a preimage.
theorems.proof: The localized complex is exact at $S^{-1}M$. A class in the kernel is represented by a fraction $m/s$ whose numerator maps to an element annihilated by some $t\in S$. Thus $tm$ comes from $L$, and replacing $m/s$ by $tm/(ts)$ exhibits a preimage.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Localization of a quotient ring
theorems.hypotheses: Let $I$ be an ideal of $R$ and $S$ multiplicative. Write $\overline S$ for the image of $S$ in $R/I$.
theorems.statement: The image $S^{-1}I$ is an ideal of $S^{-1}R$ and $(S^{-1}R)/(S^{-1}I)\cong\overline S^{-1}(R/I)$ canonically.
theorems.proof: The image $S^{-1}I$ is an ideal of $S^{-1}R$ and $(S^{-1}R)/(S^{-1}I)\cong\overline S^{-1}(R/I)$ canonically.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Submodules of a localization come from submodules
theorems.hypotheses: Let $S\subseteq R$ be multiplicative and let $N'$ be an $S^{-1}R$-submodule of $S^{-1}M$.
theorems.statement: If $N$ is the inverse image of $N'$ under $M\to S^{-1}M$, then $S^{-1}N$ has image $N'$.
theorems.proof: If $N$ is the inverse image of $N'$ under $M\to S^{-1}M$, then $S^{-1}N$ has image $N'$.

theorems.subject: ideal
theorems.name: Ideals of a localization come from ideals
theorems.hypotheses: Let $S\subseteq R$ be multiplicative and let $I'$ be an ideal of $S^{-1}R$.
theorems.statement: The localization of the inverse image of $I'$ in $R$ is $I'$. This follows by clearing denominators within the ideal of the localization.
theorems.proof: The localization of the inverse image of $I'$ in $R$ is $I'$. This follows by clearing denominators within the ideal of the localization.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Functoriality of prime spectra
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\varphi:R\to S$ be a ring map.
theorems.statement: Contraction gives a continuous map $\operatorname{Spec}S\to\operatorname{Spec}R$. The inverse image of $D(f)$ is $D(\varphi(f))$.
theorems.proof: Contraction gives a continuous map $\operatorname{Spec}S\to\operatorname{Spec}R$. The inverse image of $D(f)$ is $D(\varphi(f))$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Spectrum of a localization
theorems.hypotheses: Let $S\subseteq R$ be multiplicative.
theorems.statement: Contraction identifies $\operatorname{Spec}(S^{-1}R)$ homeomorphically with the subspace of primes disjoint from $S$. Its inverse sends $\mathfrak p$ to $S^{-1}\mathfrak p$.
theorems.proof: Contraction identifies $\operatorname{Spec}(S^{-1}R)$ homeomorphically with the subspace of primes disjoint from $S$. Its inverse sends $\mathfrak p$ to $S^{-1}\mathfrak p$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Standard opens are spectra of principal localizations
theorems.hypotheses: Let $f\in R$.
theorems.statement: Contraction identifies $\operatorname{Spec}(R_f)$ homeomorphically with $D(f)$. The inverse sends $\mathfrak p$ to $\mathfrak pR_f$.
theorems.proof: Contraction identifies $\operatorname{Spec}(R_f)$ homeomorphically with $D(f)$. The inverse sends $\mathfrak p$ to $\mathfrak pR_f$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Spectrum of a quotient
theorems.hypotheses: Let $I$ be an ideal of $R$.
theorems.statement: Contraction identifies $\operatorname{Spec}(R/I)$ homeomorphically with the closed subspace $V(I)$. The inverse sends $\mathfrak p\supseteq I$ to $\mathfrak p/I$.
theorems.proof: Contraction identifies $\operatorname{Spec}(R/I)$ homeomorphically with the closed subspace $V(I)$. The inverse sends $\mathfrak p\supseteq I$ to $\mathfrak p/I$.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: An affine spectrum is quasi-compact
theorems.hypotheses: Let the spectrum of a commutative ring carry its Zariski topology.
theorems.statement: A cover by standard opens means that their defining elements generate the unit ideal. A finite subfamily already generates that ideal, hence supplies a finite subcover.
theorems.proof: A cover by standard opens means that their defining elements generate the unit ideal. A finite subfamily already generates that ideal, hence supplies a finite subcover.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: A spectrum has a quasi-compact basis closed under intersections
theorems.hypotheses: Let the spectrum of a commutative ring carry its Zariski topology.
theorems.statement: It is quasi-compact and the opens $D(f)$ form a basis of quasi-compact opens with $D(f)\cap D(g)=D(fg)$. Every quasi-compact open is a finite union of basis opens, so any two quasi-compact opens have quasi-compact intersection.
theorems.proof: It is quasi-compact and the opens $D(f)$ form a basis of quasi-compact opens with $D(f)\cap D(g)=D(fg)$. Every quasi-compact open is a finite union of basis opens, so any two quasi-compact opens have quasi-compact intersection.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Existence of primes and the empty-spectrum criterion
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be a ring. For the relative minimal-prime assertion, let $I\subseteq\mathfrak p$ with $I$ an ideal and $\mathfrak p$ prime.
theorems.statement: Every nonzero ring has a maximal ideal and a minimal prime. Thus $\operatorname{Spec}(R)=\varnothing$ exactly when $R=0$. There is also a prime $\mathfrak q\subseteq\mathfrak p$ minimal among primes containing $I$.
theorems.proof: Every nonzero ring has a maximal ideal and a minimal prime. Thus $\operatorname{Spec}(R)=\varnothing$ exactly when $R=0$. There is also a prime $\mathfrak q\subseteq\mathfrak p$ minimal among primes containing $I$.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Radicals and the lattice operations on vanishing sets
theorems.hypotheses: Let $T\subseteq R$, let $I,J$ be ideals, and let $(I_a)$ be a family of ideals.
theorems.statement: One has $V(T)=V((T))$, $V(I)=V(\sqrt I)$, and $\sqrt I=\bigcap_{\mathfrak p\supseteq I}\mathfrak p$. The set $V(I)$ is empty exactly when $I=R$. Finite union satisfies $V(I)\cup V(J)=V(I\cap J)$ and arbitrary intersection satisfies $\bigcap_aV(I_a)=V(\bigcup_a I_a)$.
theorems.proof: One has $V(T)=V((T))$, $V(I)=V(\sqrt I)$, and $\sqrt I=\bigcap_{\mathfrak p\supseteq I}\mathfrak p$. The set $V(I)$ is empty exactly when $I=R$. Finite union satisfies $V(I)\cup V(J)=V(I\cap J)$ and arbitrary intersection satisfies $\bigcap_aV(I_a)=V(\bigcup_a I_a)$.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Standard-open calculus on an affine spectrum
theorems.hypotheses: Let $f,g\in R$, let $(f_a)$ be a family in $R$, and let $I$ be an ideal of $R$.
theorems.statement: The open $D(f)$ complements $V(f)$, is empty exactly when $f$ is nilpotent, and is the whole spectrum exactly when $f$ is a unit. Unit multiples define the same open. One has $D(f)\cap D(g)=D(fg)$ and $\bigcup_a D(f_a)=\operatorname{Spec}(R)\setminus V(\{f_a\})$. A prime outside $V(I)$ belongs to some $D(h)$ with $h\in I$, disjoint from $V(I)$.
theorems.proof: The open $D(f)$ complements $V(f)$, is empty exactly when $f$ is nilpotent, and is the whole spectrum exactly when $f$ is a unit. Unit multiples define the same open. One has $D(f)\cap D(g)=D(fg)$ and $\bigcup_a D(f_a)=\operatorname{Spec}(R)\setminus V(\{f_a\})$. A prime outside $V(I)$ belongs to some $D(h)$ with $h\in I$, disjoint from $V(I)$.

theorems.subject: ring-ideal-pair
theorems.name: An ideal lies in the Jacobson radical exactly when its translates of one are units
theorems.hypotheses: Let $I$ be an ideal of $R$.
theorems.statement: The containment $I\subseteq\operatorname{Jac}(R)$ is equivalent to all elements of $1+I$ being units. Under that condition an element invertible modulo $I$ is invertible in $R$.
theorems.proof: The containment $I\subseteq\operatorname{Jac}(R)$ is equivalent to all elements of $1+I$ being units. Under that condition an element invertible modulo $I$ is invertible in $R$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Maps surjective on spectra detect units
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ induce a surjection $\operatorname{Spec}S\to\operatorname{Spec}R$.
theorems.statement: An element of $R$ is a unit exactly when its image in $S$ is a unit. If it is a nonunit, a maximal ideal containing it has a prime lying over it.
theorems.proof: An element of $R$ is a unit exactly when its image in $S$ is a unit. If it is a nonunit, a maximal ideal containing it has a prime lying over it.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Nakayama’s determinant criterion
theorems.hypotheses: Let $I$ be an ideal of $R$ and $M$ a finite $R$-module with $IM=M$.
theorems.statement: There is an $f\in 1+I$ with $fM=0$. Write a generating vector as its product with a matrix $A$ whose entries lie in $I$. Then $\det(1-A)\in1+I$ kills the vector by the adjugate identity. If $I\subseteq\operatorname{Jac}(R)$, the determinant is a unit, so $M=0$.
theorems.proof: There is an $f\in 1+I$ with $fM=0$. Write a generating vector as its product with a matrix $A$ whose entries lie in $I$. Then $\det(1-A)\in1+I$ kills the vector by the adjugate identity. If $I\subseteq\operatorname{Jac}(R)$, the determinant is a unit, so $M=0$.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Nakayama’s submodule criterion
theorems.hypotheses: Let $N,N'\subseteq M$ with $M=N+IN'$ and $N'$ finite.
theorems.statement: Some $f\in1+I$ satisfies $fM\subseteq N$ and $M_f=N_f$. If $I\subseteq\operatorname{Jac}(R)$, then $M=N$. The quotient $M/N$ is finite since it is generated by the image of $N'$, and it equals $I(M/N)$.
theorems.proof: Some $f\in1+I$ satisfies $fM\subseteq N$ and $M_f=N_f$. If $I\subseteq\operatorname{Jac}(R)$, then $M=N$. The quotient $M/N$ is finite since it is generated by the image of $N'$, and it equals $I(M/N)$.

theorems.subject: module-map
theorems.name: Nakayama’s criterion for surjectivity and lifting generators
theorems.hypotheses: Let $u:N\to M$ be a module map with $M$ finite and $u$ surjective modulo an ideal $I$.
theorems.statement: Some $f\in1+I$ makes $u_f$ surjective, and $u$ is already surjective if $I\subseteq\operatorname{Jac}(R)$. Taking $u$ to be the map from a finite free module on a tuple that generates $M/IM$ gives the corresponding generation assertions.
theorems.proof: Some $f\in1+I$ makes $u_f$ surjective, and $u$ is already surjective if $I\subseteq\operatorname{Jac}(R)$. Taking $u$ to be the map from a finite free module on a tuple that generates $M/IM$ gives the corresponding generation assertions.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Nakayama’s lemma for nilpotent ideals without module finiteness
theorems.hypotheses: Let $I\subseteq R$ satisfy $I^d=0$ for some $d>0$. The modules and generating families may be arbitrary.
theorems.statement: For any module $Q$, $IQ=Q$ gives $Q=I^dQ=0$. Applying this to $M/N$ proves $M=N$ whenever $M=N+IN'$ with $N,N'\subseteq M$. Applying it to cokernels proves that surjectivity and generation modulo $I$ lift to $R$.
theorems.proof: For any module $Q$, $IQ=Q$ gives $Q=I^dQ=0$. Applying this to $M/N$ proves $M=N$ whenever $M=N+IN'$ with $N,N'\subseteq M$. Applying it to cokernels proves that surjectivity and generation modulo $I$ lift to $R$.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Nakayama criterion for generators after localization
theorems.hypotheses: Let $I\subseteq R$ be an ideal, $S$ a multiplicative subset, and $M$ a finite $R$-module. Suppose the images of $x_1,\dots,x_r\in M$ generate $S^{-1}(M/IM)$.
theorems.statement: For some $f\in S+I$, the images of $x_1,\dots,x_r$ generate $M_f$ over $R_f$.
theorems.proof: For some $f\in S+I$, the images of $x_1,\dots,x_r$ generate $M_f$ over $R_f$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Residue and cotangent criteria for surjectivity of a finite local map
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A\to B$ be a finite local map of local rings. Suppose $\mathfrak m_B$ is finitely generated, the induced residue field map is an isomorphism, and $\mathfrak m_A/\mathfrak m_A^2\to\mathfrak m_B/\mathfrak m_B^2$ is surjective.
theorems.statement: Then $A\to B$ is surjective. The cotangent hypothesis gives $\mathfrak m_B=\mathfrak m_AB$ by Nakayama, and the residue field hypothesis gives surjectivity after reducing the finite $A$-module $B$ modulo $\mathfrak m_A$. Apply Nakayama again to the cokernel.
theorems.proof: Then $A\to B$ is surjective. The cotangent hypothesis gives $\mathfrak m_B=\mathfrak m_AB$ by Nakayama, and the residue field hypothesis gives surjectivity after reducing the finite $A$-module $B$ modulo $\mathfrak m_A$. Apply Nakayama again to the cokernel.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Composition of essentially finite type or essentially finitely presented maps
theorems.hypotheses: Let two composable ring maps both be essentially of finite type, or both be essentially of finite presentation.
theorems.statement: The composite has the same property, using composition of finite type or finite presentation maps and the description by localization.
theorems.proof: The composite has the same property, using composition of finite type or finite presentation maps and the description by localization.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Base change of essentially finite type or essentially finitely presented maps
theorems.hypotheses: Let a ring map be essentially of finite type or essentially of finite presentation. Make an arbitrary base change.
theorems.statement: The base changed map has the corresponding property, because base change commutes with localization and preserves the relevant finiteness condition.
theorems.proof: The base changed map has the corresponding property, because base change commutes with localization and preserves the relevant finiteness condition.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Finiteness of a map into an Artinian local ring
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ have Artinian local target with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$.
theorems.statement: For each of the properties finite, finite type, and essentially finite type, the map $R\to S$ has that property exactly when $R\to S/\mathfrak m$ has it.
theorems.proof: For each of the properties finite, finite type, and essentially finite type, the map $R\to S$ has that property exactly when $R\to S/\mathfrak m$ has it.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Presenting an essentially finite type map between local rings
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ and $S$ be local rings and $R\to S$ essentially of finite type. The ring homomorphism itself may fail to be local.
theorems.statement: There is a maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ of a polynomial ring $R[X_1,\dots,X_n]$ lying over $\mathfrak m_R$ such that $S$ is a localization of a quotient of $R[X_1,\dots,X_n]_{\mathfrak m}$.
theorems.proof: There is a maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ of a polynomial ring $R[X_1,\dots,X_n]$ lying over $\mathfrak m_R$ such that $S$ is a localization of a quotient of $R[X_1,\dots,X_n]_{\mathfrak m}$.

theorems.subject: ideal
theorems.name: Associated prime of a symbolic power quotient
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be Noetherian, $\mathfrak p$ prime, and $n>0$.
theorems.statement: The associated primes of $R/\mathfrak p^{(n)}$ consist of $\mathfrak p$ alone.
theorems.proof: The associated primes of $R/\mathfrak p^{(n)}$ consist of $\mathfrak p$ alone.

theorems.subject: ideal
theorems.name: Flat extension of symbolic powers
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be flat and suppose $\mathfrak p\subseteq R$ is prime and $\mathfrak q=\mathfrak pS$ is prime in $S$.
theorems.statement: For $n\geq0$ one has $\mathfrak p^{(n)}S=\mathfrak q^{(n)}$.
theorems.proof: For $n\geq0$ one has $\mathfrak p^{(n)}S=\mathfrak q^{(n)}$.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Local criterion for weak association
theorems.hypotheses: Let $M$ be any $R$-module and $\mathfrak p$ a prime of $R$.
theorems.statement: Weak association of $\mathfrak p$ to $M$ is equivalent to weak association of $\mathfrak pR_{\mathfrak p}$ to $M_{\mathfrak p}$, and to the existence there of an element whose annihilator has radical $\mathfrak pR_{\mathfrak p}$.
theorems.proof: Weak association of $\mathfrak p$ to $M$ is equivalent to weak association of $\mathfrak pR_{\mathfrak p}$ to $M_{\mathfrak p}$, and to the existence there of an element whose annihilator has radical $\mathfrak pR_{\mathfrak p}$.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Weak assassin of a reduced ring
theorems.hypotheses: Let the ring be reduced.
theorems.statement: Its weakly associated primes as a module over itself are exactly its minimal primes.
theorems.proof: Its weakly associated primes as a module over itself are exactly its minimal primes.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Weakly associated primes and extensions
theorems.hypotheses: Let $0\to M'\to M\to M''\to0$ be a short exact sequence of $R$-modules.
theorems.statement: One has $\operatorname{WeakAss}(M')\subseteq\operatorname{WeakAss}(M)\subseteq\operatorname{WeakAss}(M')\cup\operatorname{WeakAss}(M'')$.
theorems.proof: One has $\operatorname{WeakAss}(M')\subseteq\operatorname{WeakAss}(M)\subseteq\operatorname{WeakAss}(M')\cup\operatorname{WeakAss}(M'')$.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: The weak assassin detects zero modules
theorems.hypotheses: Let the module be arbitrary over a commutative ring.
theorems.statement: The module is zero exactly when its weak assassin is empty. For a nonzero element, its annihilator is proper and has a minimal prime over it.
theorems.proof: The module is zero exactly when its weak assassin is empty. For a nonzero element, its annihilator is proper and has a minimal prime over it.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Associated primes, weakly associated primes and support
theorems.hypotheses: Let $M$ be an $R$-module.
theorems.statement: There are inclusions $\operatorname{Ass}(M)\subseteq\operatorname{WeakAss}(M)\subseteq\operatorname{Supp}(M)$.
theorems.proof: There are inclusions $\operatorname{Ass}(M)\subseteq\operatorname{WeakAss}(M)\subseteq\operatorname{Supp}(M)$.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Zerodivisors on a module from its weak assassin
theorems.hypotheses: Let $M$ be an $R$-module.
theorems.statement: The set of scalars that are zerodivisors on $M$ equals $\bigcup_{\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{WeakAss}(M)}\mathfrak p$.
theorems.proof: The set of scalars that are zerodivisors on $M$ equals $\bigcup_{\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{WeakAss}(M)}\mathfrak p$.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Minimal points of support are weakly associated
theorems.hypotheses: Let $M$ be an $R$-module and $\mathfrak p$ a minimal element of its support ordered by inclusion.
theorems.statement: The prime $\mathfrak p$ is weakly associated to $M$.
theorems.proof: The prime $\mathfrak p$ is weakly associated to $M$.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Weak association at a finitely generated prime
theorems.hypotheses: Let $M$ be any $R$-module and $\mathfrak p$ a finitely generated prime ideal.
theorems.statement: The prime $\mathfrak p$ is associated to $M$ exactly when it is weakly associated to $M$. In particular the two sets agree over a Noetherian ring.
theorems.proof: The prime $\mathfrak p$ is associated to $M$ exactly when it is weakly associated to $M$. In particular the two sets agree over a Noetherian ring.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Weak assassin after passing to a quotient ring
theorems.hypotheses: Let $I\subseteq R$ and let $M$ be an $R/I$-module.
theorems.statement: Under contraction of primes, the weak assassins over $R/I$ and $R$ agree.
theorems.proof: Under contraction of primes, the weak assassins over $R/I$ and $R$ agree.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Weak assassin after localization
theorems.hypotheses: Let $S\subseteq R$ be multiplicative and $M$ an $R$-module.
theorems.statement: The weak assassin of $S^{-1}M$ over $R$ agrees under contraction with its weak assassin over $S^{-1}R$, and is the subset of $\operatorname{WeakAss}_R(M)$ of primes disjoint from $S$.
theorems.proof: The weak assassin of $S^{-1}M$ over $R$ agrees under contraction with its weak assassin over $S^{-1}R$, and is the subset of $\operatorname{WeakAss}_R(M)$ of primes disjoint from $S$.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Inverting nonzerodivisors preserves the weak assassin
theorems.hypotheses: Let $S\subseteq R$ be multiplicative and let every $s\in S$ act injectively on $M$.
theorems.statement: Every weakly associated prime is disjoint from $S$, so under contraction $\operatorname{WeakAss}(S^{-1}M)=\operatorname{WeakAss}(M)$.
theorems.proof: Every weakly associated prime is disjoint from $S$, so under contraction $\operatorname{WeakAss}(S^{-1}M)=\operatorname{WeakAss}(M)$.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Localizations at weakly associated primes detect elements
theorems.hypotheses: Let $M$ be an $R$-module.
theorems.statement: The diagonal localization map $M\to\prod_{\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{WeakAss}(M)}M_{\mathfrak p}$ is injective.
theorems.proof: The diagonal localization map $M\to\prod_{\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{WeakAss}(M)}M_{\mathfrak p}$ is injective.

theorems.subject: module-sequence
theorems.name: Regular sequences can be permuted over Noetherian local rings
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be Noetherian local, $M$ finite, and $(f_i)$ an $M$-regular sequence.
theorems.statement: Every permutation is again regular on the same module.
theorems.proof: Every permutation is again regular on the same module.

theorems.subject: module-sequence
theorems.name: Flat local base change preserves and reflects regular sequences
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be a flat local map of local rings, $M$ any $R$-module, and $(f_i)$ a tuple in $R$.
theorems.statement: The tuple is $M$-regular exactly when its image is $M\otimes_R S$-regular. Faithful flatness detects the injectivity tests and the nonzero last quotient.
theorems.proof: The tuple is $M$-regular exactly when its image is $M\otimes_R S$-regular. Faithful flatness detects the injectivity tests and the nonzero last quotient.
refs: Stacks 00HR · flat local maps are faithfully flat

theorems.subject: module-sequence
theorems.name: Regularity at a prime holds on some standard neighborhood
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be Noetherian, $M$ finite, and $(f_i)$ a tuple whose image is $M_{\mathfrak p}$-regular for a prime $\mathfrak p$.
theorems.statement: Some $g\notin\mathfrak p$ makes the tuple $M_g$-regular over $R_g$.
theorems.proof: Some $g\notin\mathfrak p$ makes the tuple $M_g$-regular over $R_g$.

theorems.subject: ring-parameters
theorems.name: Concatenating regular sequences
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(f_i)$ be regular in $R$, with ideal $I$. Suppose $(g_j)$ is a tuple in $R$ whose image is regular in $R/I$.
theorems.statement: The concatenated tuple is regular in the original ring.
theorems.proof: The concatenated tuple is regular in the original ring.

theorems.subject: module-sequence
theorems.name: Regularity on both end terms implies regularity on the middle term
theorems.hypotheses: Let $0\to M_1\to M_2\to M_3\to0$ be exact and let $(f_i)$ be regular on both $M_1$ and $M_3$.
theorems.statement: The same tuple is regular on $M_2$.
theorems.proof: The same tuple is regular on $M_2$.

theorems.subject: module-sequence
theorems.name: Positive powers preserve and reflect regular sequences
theorems.hypotheses: Let $M$ be an $R$-module, $(f_i)$ a tuple in $R$, and $e_i>0$ integers.
theorems.statement: The tuple $(f_i)$ is $M$-regular exactly when $(f_i^{e_i})$ is $M$-regular.
theorems.proof: The tuple $(f_i)$ is $M$-regular exactly when $(f_i^{e_i})$ is $M$-regular.

theorems.subject: ring-parameters
theorems.name: Criterion for permutability by adjoining indeterminates
theorems.hypotheses: Let $f_1,\dots,f_r$ generate a proper ideal of $R$.
theorems.statement: All permutations are regular exactly when every subsequence in its inherited order is regular, and exactly when $f_1X_1,\ldots,f_rX_r$ is regular in $R[X_1,\ldots,X_r]$.
theorems.proof: All permutations are regular exactly when every subsequence in its inherited order is regular, and exactly when $f_1X_1,\ldots,f_rX_r$ is regular in $R[X_1,\ldots,X_r]$.

theorems.subject: module-sequence
theorems.name: Flat base change preserves quasi-regularity
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to R'$ be flat and suppose $(f_i)$ is $M$-quasi-regular.
theorems.statement: Its image is $M\otimes_RR'$-quasi-regular, since flat base change preserves the associated graded quotients in the canonical comparison.
theorems.proof: Its image is $M\otimes_RR'$-quasi-regular, since flat base change preserves the associated graded quotients in the canonical comparison.

theorems.subject: module-sequence
theorems.name: Quasi-regularity at a prime holds on a standard neighborhood
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be Noetherian, $M$ finite, and $(f_i)$ a tuple that is $M_{\mathfrak p}$-quasi-regular at a prime $\mathfrak p$.
theorems.statement: There is a $g\notin\mathfrak p$ such that the images of $(f_i)$ in $R_g$ are $M_g$-quasi-regular.
theorems.proof: There is a $g\notin\mathfrak p$ such that the images of $(f_i)$ in $R_g$ are $M_g$-quasi-regular.

theorems.subject: module-sequence
theorems.name: The remaining sequence stays quasi-regular after quotienting out the initial segment
theorems.hypotheses: Let $f_1,\dots,f_r$ be $M$-quasi-regular and $0\leq i\leq r$.
theorems.statement: The images of $f_{i+1},\ldots,f_r$ are quasi-regular on $M/(f_1,\ldots,f_i)M$ over $R/(f_1,\ldots,f_i)$.
theorems.proof: The images of $f_{i+1},\ldots,f_r$ are quasi-regular on $M/(f_1,\ldots,f_i)M$ over $R/(f_1,\ldots,f_i)$.

theorems.subject: module-sequence
theorems.name: Quasi-regularity implies regularity under local finiteness hypotheses
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be Noetherian local, $M$ a nonzero finite module, and $(f_i)$ an $M$-quasi-regular tuple in $\mathfrak m$.
theorems.statement: The tuple is $M$-regular. Nonzeroness of the final quotient follows from Nakayama, and separatedness for the maximal ideal filtration gives the injectivity tests.
theorems.proof: The tuple is $M$-regular. Nonzeroness of the final quotient follows from Nakayama, and separatedness for the maximal ideal filtration gives the injectivity tests.

theorems.subject: module-sequence
theorems.name: Quasi-regularity after separating the ideal-adic filtration
theorems.hypotheses: Let $J=(f_1,\dots,f_r)$, $\overline R=R/\bigcap_{n\geq0}J^n$, and $\overline M=M/\bigcap_{n\geq0}J^nM$.
theorems.statement: The tuple is $M$-quasi-regular exactly when its image is $\overline M$-quasi-regular over $\overline R$, since the graded quotients in the comparison are unchanged.
theorems.proof: The tuple is $M$-quasi-regular exactly when its image is $\overline M$-quasi-regular over $\overline R$, since the graded quotients in the comparison are unchanged.

theorems.subject: ring-ideal-pair
theorems.name: The distinguished element of an affine blowup chart
theorems.hypotheses: Let $I\subseteq R$ be an ideal, $a\in I$, and $A=R[I/a]$ the affine blowup algebra.
theorems.statement: Multiplication by $a$ is injective on $A$, the ideal $IA$ equals $aA$, and $A_a\cong R_a$. The degree-zero localization identifies $A$ with the subring of $R_a$ generated over the image of $R$ by $x/a$ for $x\in I$.
theorems.proof: Multiplication by $a$ is injective on $A$, the ideal $IA$ equals $aA$, and $A_a\cong R_a$. The degree-zero localization identifies $A$ with the subring of $R_a$ generated over the image of $R$ by $x/a$ for $x\in I$.

theorems.subject: ring-ideal-pair
theorems.name: An affine blowup chart after arbitrary base change
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$, $I\subseteq R$, $a\in I$, $J=IS$, and $b$ be the image of $a$.
theorems.statement: The natural map $S\otimes_RR[I/a]\to S[J/b]$ is surjective, and its kernel is the ideal of elements killed by some power of $b$.
theorems.proof: The natural map $S\otimes_RR[I/a]\to S[J/b]$ is surjective, and its kernel is the ideal of elements killed by some power of $b$.

theorems.subject: ring-ideal-pair
theorems.name: A presentation of a finitely generated affine blowup chart
theorems.hypotheses: Let $I=(a_1,\ldots,a_n)$ with $n\geq1$ and set $a=a_1$.
theorems.statement: The map $R[x_2,\ldots,x_n]/(ax_2-a_2,\ldots,ax_n-a_n)\to R[I/a]$ sending $x_i$ to $a_i/a$ is surjective. Its kernel consists precisely of the elements annihilated by a power of $a$.
theorems.proof: The map $R[x_2,\ldots,x_n]/(ax_2-a_2,\ldots,ax_n-a_n)\to R[I/a]$ sending $x_i$ to $a_i/a$ is surjective. Its kernel consists precisely of the elements annihilated by a power of $a$.

theorems.subject: ring-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Reducedness passes to every affine blowup chart
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be reduced and choose any $a\in I\subseteq R$ with $I$ an ideal.
theorems.statement: The chart $R[I/a]$ is reduced. A localization of a reduced ring is reduced, and the chart is a subring of $R_a$.
theorems.proof: The chart $R[I/a]$ is reduced. A localization of a reduced ring is reduced, and the chart is a subring of $R_a$.

theorems.subject: ring-ideal-pair
theorems.name: A domain has domain charts at nonzero elements
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be a domain, $I\subseteq R$ an ideal, and $0\neq a\in I$.
theorems.statement: The chart $R[I/a]$ is a domain because it is a subring of $R_a$ containing $1\neq0$.
theorems.proof: The chart $R[I/a]$ is a domain because it is a subring of $R_a$ containing $1\neq0$.

theorems.subject: ring-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Density of an affine blowup chart over its original spectrum
theorems.hypotheses: Let $I\subseteq R$ be an ideal and choose $a\in I$ that lies in no minimal prime of $R$.
theorems.statement: The morphism $\operatorname{Spec}(R[I/a])\to\operatorname{Spec}(R)$ has dense image. Its image contains $D(a)$, which contains every minimal prime.
theorems.proof: The morphism $\operatorname{Spec}(R[I/a])\to\operatorname{Spec}(R)$ has dense image. Its image contains $D(a)$, which contains every minimal prime.

theorems.subject: ring-ideal-pair
theorems.name: A principal defining equation of the center on an affine blowup chart
theorems.hypotheses: Let $I\subseteq R$, $a\in I$, and $f\in R$ satisfy $V(f)=V(I)$. Put $A=R[I/a]$.
theorems.statement: Multiplication by $f$ on $A$ is injective, and $A_f\cong A_a\cong R_a$. In $A$ the radicals of $fA$ and $aA=IA$ agree, so a power of $a$ belongs to $fA$ and a power of $f$ belongs to $aA$.
theorems.proof: Multiplication by $f$ on $A$ is injective, and $A_f\cong A_a\cong R_a$. In $A$ the radicals of $fA$ and $aA=IA$ agree, so a power of $a$ belongs to $fA$ and a power of $f$ belongs to $aA$.

theorems.subject: ring-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Scaling the center of an affine blowup chart
theorems.hypotheses: Let $I\subseteq R$ be an ideal, $a\in I$, and $f\in R$.
theorems.statement: The map $R[I/a]\to R[fI/(fa)]$ given by $x/a^n\mapsto f^nx/(fa)^n$ is surjective with kernel the ideal of elements killed by some power of $f$.
theorems.proof: The map $R[I/a]\to R[fI/(fa)]$ given by $x/a^n\mapsto f^nx/(fa)^n$ is surjective with kernel the ideal of elements killed by some power of $f$.

theorems.subject: ring-ideal-pair
theorems.name: A dominating valuation ring as a directed union of affine blowup charts
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a local domain with fraction field $K$ and nonzero maximal ideal. Let $R\subseteq A\subseteq K$ be a valuation ring dominating $R$.
theorems.statement: The ring $A$ is the directed union of charts $R[I/a]\subseteq A$ with $I\subseteq\mathfrak m$ finitely generated, $0\neq a\in I$, and nonzero fibre at $\mathfrak m$. Any finite subset of $A$ is contained in such a chart by scaling a common denominator and numerators by a fixed nonzero element of $\mathfrak m$. The maximal ideal of $A$ gives a prime above $\mathfrak m$ on each chart. If $\mathfrak m=0$, then $A=R=K$.
theorems.proof: The ring $A$ is the directed union of charts $R[I/a]\subseteq A$ with $I\subseteq\mathfrak m$ finitely generated, $0\neq a\in I$, and nonzero fibre at $\mathfrak m$. Any finite subset of $A$ is contained in such a chart by scaling a common denominator and numerators by a fixed nonzero element of $\mathfrak m$. The maximal ideal of $A$ gives a prime above $\mathfrak m$ on each chart. If $\mathfrak m=0$, then $A=R=K$.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Existence of free resolutions
theorems.hypotheses: Let $M$ be a module over $R$. For a resolution by finite free modules, assume $R$ is Noetherian and $M$ is finite.
theorems.statement: A free resolution exists by choosing a free surjection onto each successive kernel. Under the two extra hypotheses these kernels are all finite, so the free modules can be chosen finite in every degree.
theorems.proof: A free resolution exists by choosing a free surjection onto each successive kernel. Under the two extra hypotheses these kernels are all finite, so the free modules can be chosen finite in every degree.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Homotopic chain maps act identically on homology
theorems.hypotheses: Let two maps between the same complexes be chain homotopic.
theorems.statement: The induced maps on every (co)homology group coincide. Their difference is $dh+hd$, which sends a cycle to a boundary.
theorems.proof: The induced maps on every (co)homology group coincide. Their difference is $dh+hd$, which sends a cycle to a boundary.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Lifting a module map to a resolution up to homotopy
theorems.hypotheses: Let $M\to N$ be an $R$-module map, $N_\bullet\to N$ a resolution, and $F_\bullet\to M$ a nonnegative augmented complex with every $F_i$ free.
theorems.statement: There exists a chain map $F_\bullet\to N_\bullet$ compatible with the augmentations and $M\to N$. Any two such lifts are chain homotopic.
theorems.proof: There exists a chain map $F_\bullet\to N_\bullet$ compatible with the augmentations and $M\to N$. Any two such lifts are chain homotopic.

theorems.subject: module-pair
theorems.name: Ext is independent of the chosen free resolution
theorems.hypotheses: Let $M_1\to M_2$ be a module map, choose free resolutions $F_\bullet$ and $G_\bullet$ of $M_1$ and $M_2$, and fix an $R$-module $N$.
theorems.statement: A lift $F_\bullet\to G_\bullet$ induces maps $H^i(\operatorname{Hom}_R(G_\bullet,N))\to H^i(\operatorname{Hom}_R(F_\bullet,N))$ independent of the lift. An isomorphism induces isomorphisms, and the identity on a module lifts to the identity in cohomology. The direction is contravariant by precomposition.
theorems.proof: A lift $F_\bullet\to G_\bullet$ induces maps $H^i(\operatorname{Hom}_R(G_\bullet,N))\to H^i(\operatorname{Hom}_R(F_\bullet,N))$ independent of the lift. An isomorphism induces isomorphisms, and the identity on a module lifts to the identity in cohomology. The direction is contravariant by precomposition.

theorems.subject: module-exact-sequence
theorems.name: Long exact Ext sequence in the second variable
theorems.hypotheses: Fix an $R$-module $M$ and a short exact sequence $0\to N'\to N\to N''\to0$.
theorems.statement: There is a natural long exact sequence beginning with $0\to\operatorname{Hom}_R(M,N')\to\operatorname{Hom}_R(M,N)\to\operatorname{Hom}_R(M,N'')$ and continuing with $\operatorname{Ext}_R^i(M,N')\to\operatorname{Ext}_R^i(M,N)\to\operatorname{Ext}_R^i(M,N'')\to\operatorname{Ext}_R^{i+1}(M,N')$ for $i\geq0$.
theorems.proof: There is a natural long exact sequence beginning with $0\to\operatorname{Hom}_R(M,N')\to\operatorname{Hom}_R(M,N)\to\operatorname{Hom}_R(M,N'')$ and continuing with $\operatorname{Ext}_R^i(M,N')\to\operatorname{Ext}_R^i(M,N)\to\operatorname{Ext}_R^i(M,N'')\to\operatorname{Ext}_R^{i+1}(M,N')$ for $i\geq0$.

theorems.subject: module-exact-sequence
theorems.name: Long exact Ext sequence in the first variable
theorems.hypotheses: Fix an $R$-module $N$ and a short exact sequence $0\to M'\to M\to M''\to0$.
theorems.statement: There is a natural long exact sequence beginning with $0\to\operatorname{Hom}_R(M'',N)\to\operatorname{Hom}_R(M,N)\to\operatorname{Hom}_R(M',N)$ and continuing with $\operatorname{Ext}_R^i(M'',N)\to\operatorname{Ext}_R^i(M,N)\to\operatorname{Ext}_R^i(M',N)\to\operatorname{Ext}_R^{i+1}(M'',N)$ for $i\geq0$.
theorems.proof: There is a natural long exact sequence beginning with $0\to\operatorname{Hom}_R(M'',N)\to\operatorname{Hom}_R(M,N)\to\operatorname{Hom}_R(M',N)$ and continuing with $\operatorname{Ext}_R^i(M'',N)\to\operatorname{Ext}_R^i(M,N)\to\operatorname{Ext}_R^i(M',N)\to\operatorname{Ext}_R^{i+1}(M'',N)$ for $i\geq0$.

theorems.subject: module-pair
theorems.name: Annihilation of Ext by a scalar annihilating either argument
theorems.hypotheses: Let $M,N$ be $R$-modules and $x\in R$ satisfy $xM=0$ or $xN=0$.
theorems.statement: The scalar $x$ annihilates every $\operatorname{Ext}^i_R(M,N)$. If $xN=0$ it kills the cochain complex. If $xM=0$ multiplication by $x$ on a free resolution lifts the zero endomorphism of $M$ and hence acts trivially on cohomology.
theorems.proof: The scalar $x$ annihilates every $\operatorname{Ext}^i_R(M,N)$. If $xN=0$ it kills the cochain complex. If $xM=0$ multiplication by $x$ on a free resolution lifts the zero endomorphism of $M$ and hence acts trivially on cohomology.

theorems.subject: module-pair
theorems.name: Finiteness of Ext over a Noetherian ring
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be Noetherian and let $M,N$ be finite $R$-modules.
theorems.statement: Each $\operatorname{Ext}^i_R(M,N)$ is finite because a resolution by finite free modules computes it as a subquotient of a finite $R$-module.
