theorems.proof: Each $\operatorname{Ext}^i_R(M,N)$ is finite because a resolution by finite free modules computes it as a subquotient of a finite $R$-module.

theorems.subject: module-exact-sequence
theorems.name: A test for universal exactness using finitely presented modules
theorems.hypotheses: Let the given sequence of modules be short exact.
theorems.statement: It is universally exact exactly when tensoring it with every finitely presented module preserves exactness.
theorems.proof: It is universally exact exactly when tensoring it with every finitely presented module preserves exactness.

theorems.subject: module-exact-sequence
theorems.name: A finite linear system criterion for universal exactness
theorems.hypotheses: Let $0\to M_1\xrightarrow{i}M_2\to M_3\to0$ be short exact.
theorems.statement: It is universally exact exactly when every finite linear system $i(x_i)=\sum_j a_{ij}y_j$ with $x_i\in M_1$, $a_{ij}\in R$, and a solution $(y_j)$ in $M_2$ also has a solution $x_i=\sum_j a_{ij}z_j$ in $M_1$. Equivalently, for every commutative square with top arrow $R^n\to R^m$ and bottom arrow $i$, the map $R^n\to M_1$ extends along the top arrow.
theorems.proof: It is universally exact exactly when every finite linear system $i(x_i)=\sum_j a_{ij}y_j$ with $x_i\in M_1$, $a_{ij}\in R$, and a solution $(y_j)$ in $M_2$ also has a solution $x_i=\sum_j a_{ij}z_j$ in $M_1$. Equivalently, for every commutative square with top arrow $R^n\to R^m$ and bottom arrow $i$, the map $R^n\to M_1$ extends along the top arrow.

theorems.subject: module-exact-sequence
theorems.name: Lifting maps from finitely presented modules through a universally exact quotient
theorems.hypotheses: Let $0\to M_1\to M_2\to M_3\to0$ be short exact.
theorems.statement: It is universally exact exactly when $\operatorname{Hom}_R(P,M_2)\to\operatorname{Hom}_R(P,M_3)$ is surjective for every finitely presented $P$.
theorems.proof: It is universally exact exactly when $\operatorname{Hom}_R(P,M_2)\to\operatorname{Hom}_R(P,M_3)$ is surjective for every finitely presented $P$.

theorems.subject: module-exact-sequence
theorems.name: Universally exact sequences as directed colimits of split sequences
theorems.hypotheses: Let $0\to M_1\to M_2\to M_3\to0$ be short exact.
theorems.statement: It is universally exact exactly when it is the directed colimit of split exact sequences $0\to M_1\to M_{2,i}\to M_{3,i}\to0$ with the left term fixed and each $M_{3,i}$ finitely presented.
theorems.proof: It is universally exact exactly when it is the directed colimit of split exact sequences $0\to M_1\to M_{2,i}\to M_{3,i}\to0$ with the left term fixed and each $M_{3,i}$ finitely presented.

theorems.subject: module-exact-sequence
theorems.name: Directed colimits preserve universal exactness
theorems.hypotheses: Let a directed system of short exact sequences have universally exact terms as sequences.
theorems.statement: Its termwise colimit sequence is universally exact. Tensor product commutes with colimits and taking directed colimits of modules is exact.
theorems.proof: Its termwise colimit sequence is universally exact. Tensor product commutes with colimits and taking directed colimits of modules is exact.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Flatness tested by every short exact sequence with the given quotient
theorems.hypotheses: Fix an $R$-module $M$.
theorems.statement: The module is flat exactly when every short exact sequence having that module as quotient is universally exact. One particular split sequence places no flatness restriction on its quotient.
theorems.proof: The module is flat exactly when every short exact sequence having that module as quotient is universally exact. One particular split sequence places no flatness restriction on its quotient.

theorems.subject: module-map
theorems.name: Tensoring a universally injective module map preserves universal injectivity
theorems.hypotheses: Let $u:M\to M'$ be universally injective over $R$ and let $N$ be an arbitrary $R$-module.
theorems.statement: The map $u\otimes_R\mathrm{id}_N$ is universally injective, since a further test module $Q$ amounts to testing $u$ against $N\otimes_R Q$.
theorems.proof: The map $u\otimes_R\mathrm{id}_N$ is universally injective, since a further test module $Q$ amounts to testing $u$ against $N\otimes_R Q$.

theorems.subject: module-map
theorems.name: Compositions of universally injective maps are universally injective
theorems.hypotheses: Let two composable module maps over the same ring be universally injective.
theorems.statement: The composite is universally injective. Tensoring gives a composite of injective maps for every test module.
theorems.proof: The composite is universally injective. Tensoring gives a composite of injective maps for every test module.

theorems.subject: module-map
theorems.name: A universally injective composite has universally injective first map
theorems.hypotheses: Let $u:M\to M'$ and $v:M'\to M''$ be $R$-linear. Assume $v\circ u$ is universally injective.
theorems.statement: Then $u$ is universally injective, since the kernel of the first tensor map is contained in the kernel of the composite for every test module.
theorems.proof: Then $u$ is universally injective, since the kernel of the first tensor map is contained in the kernel of the composite for every test module.

theorems.subject: module-map
theorems.name: Universal injectivity can be checked on localizations
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be a ring map and $u:M\to M'$ be $S$-linear.
theorems.statement: Universal injectivity over $R$ is equivalent to universal injectivity of $u_{\mathfrak q}$ over $R$ at every prime $\mathfrak q$ of $S$, and equivalent to the corresponding condition just at maximal ideals. In either test the base ring may instead be $R_{\mathfrak p}$, where $\mathfrak p$ is the contraction of the tested prime or maximal ideal.
theorems.proof: Universal injectivity over $R$ is equivalent to universal injectivity of $u_{\mathfrak q}$ over $R$ at every prime $\mathfrak q$ of $S$, and equivalent to the corresponding condition just at maximal ideals. In either test the base ring may instead be $R_{\mathfrak p}$, where $\mathfrak p$ is the contraction of the tested prime or maximal ideal.

theorems.subject: module-map
theorems.name: Universal injectivity under simultaneous localization
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A\to B$, with multiplicative subsets $S\subseteq A$ and $S'\subseteq B$ such that the image of $S$ lies in $S'$. Let $u$ be a map of $B$-modules.
theorems.statement: If $u$ is universally injective over $A$, then $(S')^{-1}u$ is universally injective both over $A$ and over $S^{-1}A$. For a map of $(S')^{-1}B$-modules, universal injectivity over $A$ and over $S^{-1}A$ are equivalent.
theorems.proof: If $u$ is universally injective over $A$, then $(S')^{-1}u$ is universally injective both over $A$ and over $S^{-1}A$. For a map of $(S')^{-1}B$-modules, universal injectivity over $A$ and over $S^{-1}A$ are equivalent.

theorems.subject: module-map
theorems.name: A quotient test for universal injectivity into a flat module
theorems.hypotheses: Let $u:M\to M'$ be $R$-linear and suppose $M'$ is flat.
theorems.statement: Universal injectivity is equivalent to injectivity of $M/IM\to M'/IM'$ for every finitely generated ideal $I$ of $R$. The condition includes $I=0$.
theorems.proof: Universal injectivity is equivalent to injectivity of $M/IM\to M'/IM'$ for every finitely generated ideal $I$ of $R$. The condition includes $I=0$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Base change along a pure ring map reflects injections and surjections
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be universally injective on underlying $R$-modules.
theorems.statement: For any $R$-linear $u:M\to N$, injectivity of $u\otimes_R S$ implies injectivity of $u$, and surjectivity of $u\otimes_R S$ implies surjectivity of $u$. Consequently the functor reflects isomorphisms. The injection assertion uses $M\hookrightarrow M\otimes_R S$, and the surjection assertion uses the corresponding injection for the cokernel.
theorems.proof: For any $R$-linear $u:M\to N$, injectivity of $u\otimes_R S$ implies injectivity of $u$, and surjectivity of $u\otimes_R S$ implies surjectivity of $u$. Consequently the functor reflects isomorphisms. The injection assertion uses $M\hookrightarrow M\otimes_R S$, and the surjection assertion uses the corresponding injection for the cokernel.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Faithfully flat extension contracts ideals back to themselves
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be faithfully flat and let $I\subseteq R$ be any ideal.
theorems.statement: The map $R/I\to S/IS$ is injective by universal injectivity, so the contraction of $IS$ is $I$.
theorems.proof: The map $R/I\to S/IS$ is injective by universal injectivity, so the contraction of $IS$ is $I$.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Direct-sum dévissage gives a direct sum of the successor quotients
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(M_\alpha)_{\alpha\in S}$ be a direct-sum dévissage of $M$.
theorems.statement: The module $M$ is isomorphic to the direct sum of $M_{\alpha+1}/M_\alpha$ over indices with $\alpha+1\in S$. Choose a complement at each successor step and use unions at limit steps.
theorems.proof: The module $M$ is isomorphic to the direct sum of $M_{\alpha+1}/M_\alpha$ over indices with $\alpha+1\in S$. Choose a complement at each successor step and use unions at limit steps.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Kaplansky dévissages characterize sums of countably generated modules
theorems.hypotheses: Let the module be arbitrary.
theorems.statement: It admits a Kaplansky dévissage exactly when it is a direct sum of countably generated modules.
theorems.proof: It admits a Kaplansky dévissage exactly when it is a direct sum of countably generated modules.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Direct summands of direct sums of countably generated modules
theorems.hypotheses: Let $M$ be a direct sum of countably generated $R$-modules and $P$ a direct summand of $M$.
theorems.statement: The module $P$ is itself a direct sum of countably generated $R$-modules. The transfinite decomposition in the source chooses successive summands compatible with a fixed decomposition $M=P\oplus Q$.
theorems.proof: The module $P$ is itself a direct sum of countably generated $R$-modules. The transfinite decomposition in the source chooses successive summands compatible with a fixed decomposition $M=P\oplus Q$.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Kaplansky’s decomposition of projective modules
theorems.hypotheses: Let the module be projective over a commutative ring.
theorems.statement: It is a direct sum of countably generated projective modules.
theorems.proof: It is a direct sum of countably generated projective modules.

theorems.subject: module-system
theorems.name: Mittag-Leffler systems can be replaced by their stable images
theorems.hypotheses: Let the directed inverse system of sets or modules be Mittag-Leffler.
theorems.statement: The subsystem of stable images has surjective transitions and the same inverse limit.
theorems.proof: The subsystem of stable images has surjective transitions and the same inverse limit.

theorems.subject: module-system
theorems.name: A countable Mittag-Leffler system of nonempty sets has nonempty limit
theorems.hypotheses: Let the directed indexing set be countable. Suppose the inverse system is Mittag-Leffler and all terms are nonempty.
theorems.statement: The inverse limit is nonempty. Pass to stable images, choose a cofinal sequence, and successively lift elements along its surjective transitions.
theorems.proof: The inverse limit is nonempty. Pass to stable images, choose a cofinal sequence, and successively lift elements along its surjective transitions.

theorems.subject: module-system
theorems.name: Exactness of inverse limits under the Mittag-Leffler condition on the kernels
theorems.hypotheses: Let $0\to A_i\to B_i\to C_i\to0$ be a short exact sequence of inverse systems of abelian groups over a countable directed set. Suppose $(A_i)$ is Mittag-Leffler.
theorems.statement: Then $0\to\varprojlim A_i\to\varprojlim B_i\to\varprojlim C_i\to0$ is exact.
theorems.proof: Then $0\to\varprojlim A_i\to\varprojlim B_i\to\varprojlim C_i\to0$ is exact.

theorems.subject: module-system
theorems.name: Surjective transition maps and stable images
theorems.hypotheses: Take a directed inverse system of sets or of modules.
theorems.statement: Surjective transition maps imply the Mittag–Leffler condition. For a Mittag–Leffler system the stable images form a subsystem with surjective transition maps, and inclusion induces an isomorphism on inverse limits.
theorems.proof: Surjective transition maps imply the Mittag–Leffler condition. For a Mittag–Leffler system the stable images form a subsystem with surjective transition maps, and inclusion induces an isomorphism on inverse limits.

theorems.subject: module-system
theorems.name: Nonempty inverse limit over a countable index set
theorems.hypotheses: Take a directed inverse system of nonempty sets over a countable directed set. Suppose it is Mittag–Leffler.
theorems.statement: The inverse limit is nonempty.
theorems.proof: The inverse limit is nonempty.

theorems.subject: module-system
theorems.name: Exact inverse limit over a countable directed set
theorems.hypotheses: Take a short exact sequence of inverse systems of abelian groups over a countable directed set. Assume the kernel system is Mittag–Leffler.
theorems.statement: The induced sequence of inverse limits is short exact.
theorems.proof: The induced sequence of inverse limits is short exact.

theorems.subject: module-system
theorems.name: Exactness of countable Mittag–Leffler inverse limits
theorems.hypotheses: Take an inverse sequence of short exact sequences of modules indexed by the positive integers. Assume the images in each fixed term of the kernel sequence eventually stabilize.
theorems.statement: Taking inverse limits gives a short exact sequence. In particular, the induced map on inverse limits of the two rightmost systems is surjective.
theorems.proof: Taking inverse limits gives a short exact sequence. In particular, the induced map on inverse limits of the two rightmost systems is surjective.

theorems.subject: module-map-pair
theorems.name: Testing domination with finitely presented modules
theorems.hypotheses: Let two module maps have the same source over a fixed commutative ring.
theorems.statement: To decide whether the second map dominates the first, it suffices to test the kernel inclusion after tensoring with every finitely presented module.
theorems.proof: To decide whether the second map dominates the first, it suffices to test the kernel inclusion after tensoring with every finitely presented module.

theorems.subject: module-map-pair
theorems.name: Domination via the pushout
theorems.hypotheses: Let $f:M\to N$ and $g:M\to M'$ be module maps. Form their pushout $N'=N\amalg_M M'$ with induced map $f':M'\to N'$.
theorems.statement: The map $g$ dominates $f$ exactly when $f'$ is universally injective, meaning that $f'\otimes_R Q$ is injective for every $R$-module $Q$.
theorems.proof: The map $g$ dominates $f$ exactly when $f'$ is universally injective, meaning that $f'\otimes_R Q$ is injective for every $R$-module $Q$.

theorems.subject: module-map-pair
theorems.name: Domination and factorization
theorems.hypotheses: Let $f:M\to N$ and $g:M\to M'$ be module maps. Assume $\operatorname{coker}(f)$ is finitely presented.
theorems.statement: The map $g$ dominates $f$ if and only if there exists an $R$-linear map $h:N\to M'$ with $g=h\circ f$.
theorems.proof: The map $g$ dominates $f$ if and only if there exists an $R$-linear map $h:N\to M'$ with $g=h\circ f$.

theorems.subject: module-system
theorems.name: Five criteria for a Mittag–Leffler presentation
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(M_i,f_{ij})_{i\in I}$ be a directed system of finitely presented $R$-modules with colimit $M$ and structural maps $f_i:M_i\to M$.
theorems.statement: The following conditions are equivalent. Each map $f:P\to M$ from a finitely presented module admits a map $g:P\to Q$ to a finitely presented module with the same tensor kernels as $f$ for every tensor factor. Each $i$ has some $j\geq i$ such that $f_{ij}$ dominates $f_i$. Each $i$ has some $j\geq i$ such that $f_{ij}$ factors through $f_{ik}$ for every $k\geq i$. The inverse system $\operatorname{Hom}_R(M_i,N)$ is Mittag–Leffler for every $R$-module $N$. This Hom system is Mittag–Leffler for $N=\prod_{s\in I}M_s$.
theorems.proof: The following conditions are equivalent. Each map $f:P\to M$ from a finitely presented module admits a map $g:P\to Q$ to a finitely presented module with the same tensor kernels as $f$ for every tensor factor. Each $i$ has some $j\geq i$ such that $f_{ij}$ dominates $f_i$. Each $i$ has some $j\geq i$ such that $f_{ij}$ factors through $f_{ik}$ for every $k\geq i$. The inverse system $\operatorname{Hom}_R(M_i,N)$ is Mittag–Leffler for every $R$-module $N$. This Hom system is Mittag–Leffler for $N=\prod_{s\in I}M_s$.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Mittag–Leffler modules in universally exact sequences
theorems.hypotheses: Let $0\to M_1\to M_2\to M_3\to0$ remain exact after tensoring with every $R$-module.
theorems.statement: If $M_2$ is Mittag–Leffler then so is $M_1$. If both $M_1$ and $M_3$ are Mittag–Leffler then so is $M_2$.
theorems.proof: If $M_2$ is Mittag–Leffler then so is $M_1$. If both $M_1$ and $M_3$ are Mittag–Leffler then so is $M_2$.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Direct sums of Mittag–Leffler modules
theorems.hypotheses: Take an arbitrary family of modules over one commutative ring.
theorems.statement: Its direct sum is Mittag–Leffler if and only if every summand is Mittag–Leffler.
theorems.proof: Its direct sum is Mittag–Leffler if and only if every summand is Mittag–Leffler.

theorems.subject: module-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Surjections, flat quotients and completion
theorems.hypotheses: Let $I$ be an ideal of $R$. All completions are $I$-adic.
theorems.statement: A map $M\to N$ surjective modulo $I$ induces a surjection on completions. Completion takes a short exact sequence with flat quotient to a short exact sequence. For finite $M$, the natural map $M\otimes_R\widehat R\to\widehat M$ is surjective.
theorems.proof: A map $M\to N$ surjective modulo $I$ induces a surjection on completions. Completion takes a short exact sequence with flat quotient to a short exact sequence. For finite $M$, the natural map $M\otimes_R\widehat R\to\widehat M$ is surjective.

theorems.subject: module-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Completion with respect to a finitely generated ideal
theorems.hypotheses: Let $I\subset R$ be finitely generated and let $M$ be any $R$-module.
theorems.statement: The completion $\widehat M$ is $I$-adically complete. For $n\geq1$, its submodule $I^n\widehat M$ is the kernel of $\widehat M\to M/I^nM$ and is canonically the completion of $I^nM$.
theorems.proof: The completion $\widehat M$ is $I$-adically complete. For $n\geq1$, its submodule $I^n\widehat M$ is the kernel of $\widehat M\to M/I^nM$ and is canonically the completion of $I^nM$.

theorems.subject: module-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Exact completion with a power-torsion quotient
theorems.hypotheses: Let $0\to M\to N\to Q\to0$ be exact and suppose $I^nQ=0$ for some $n\geq1$.
theorems.statement: The sequence $0\to\widehat M\to\widehat N\to Q\to0$ is exact.
theorems.proof: The sequence $0\to\widehat M\to\widehat N\to Q\to0$ is exact.

theorems.subject: module-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Criterion for a completion to be complete
theorems.hypotheses: Let $I$ be an arbitrary ideal of a ring $R$ and $M$ any $R$-module. Put $K_n=\ker(\widehat M\to M/I^nM)$.
theorems.statement: The completion $\widehat M$ is $I$-adically complete if and only if $K_n=I^n\widehat M$ for every $n\geq1$.
theorems.proof: The completion $\widehat M$ is $I$-adically complete if and only if $K_n=I^n\widehat M$ for every $n\geq1$.

theorems.subject: ring-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Units and the Jacobson radical in a completion
theorems.hypotheses: Let $I\subseteq R$ be any ideal and $\widehat R=\varprojlim_n R/I^n$.
theorems.statement: An element of $\widehat R$ mapping to a unit of $R/I$ is a unit. Both $I\widehat R$ and the kernel of $\widehat R\to R/I$ lie in the Jacobson radical of $\widehat R$.
theorems.proof: An element of $\widehat R$ mapping to a unit of $R/I$ is a unit. Both $I\widehat R$ and the kernel of $\widehat R\to R/I$ lie in the Jacobson radical of $\widehat R$.

theorems.subject: module-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Surjectivity to completion from principal generators
theorems.hypotheses: Let $I=(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$ be a finitely generated ideal of $R$ and let $M$ be an $R$-module. For each $i$, assume $M\to\varprojlim_n M/f_i^nM$ is surjective.
theorems.statement: The map $M\to\varprojlim_n M/I^nM$ is surjective.
theorems.proof: The map $M\to\varprojlim_n M/I^nM$ is surjective.

theorems.subject: module-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Completeness for a smaller finitely generated ideal
theorems.hypotheses: Let $I\subseteq J$ be ideals of $R$ with $I$ finitely generated, and assume $M$ is $J$-adically complete.
theorems.statement: The module $M$ is $I$-adically complete.
theorems.proof: The module $M$ is $I$-adically complete.

theorems.subject: module-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Completion for cofinal powers
theorems.hypotheses: Let $I,J$ be ideals of $R$. Assume $I^c\subseteq J$ and $J^d\subseteq I$ for positive integers $c,d$.
theorems.statement: The $I$-adic and $J$-adic completions of any $R$-module agree canonically, and completeness with respect to either ideal implies completeness with respect to the other.
theorems.proof: The $I$-adic and $J$-adic completions of any $R$-module agree canonically, and completeness with respect to either ideal implies completeness with respect to the other.

theorems.subject: module-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Complete quotient and closed submodule
theorems.hypotheses: Let $M$ be $I$-adically complete and $K\subseteq M$ a submodule.
theorems.statement: The quotient $M/K$ is $I$-adically complete if and only if $K=\bigcap_{n\geq1}(K+I^nM)$.
theorems.proof: The quotient $M/K$ is $I$-adically complete if and only if $K=\bigcap_{n\geq1}(K+I^nM)$.

theorems.subject: module-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Completeness of a separated finite module
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be $I$-adically complete and let $M$ be finite over $R$. Assume $\bigcap_{n\geq1}I^nM=0$.
theorems.statement: Then $M$ is $I$-adically complete.
theorems.proof: Then $M$ is $I$-adically complete.

theorems.subject: module-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Finiteness detected modulo the ideal
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be $I$-adically complete and $M$ an $I$-adically separated $R$-module. Assume $M/IM$ is finite over $R/I$.
theorems.statement: The module $M$ is finite over $R$.
theorems.proof: The module $M$ is finite over $R$.

theorems.subject: module-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Completion as tensor product for finite modules
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be Noetherian, $I\subseteq R$ an ideal and $M$ finite over $R$.
theorems.statement: The natural map $M\otimes_R\widehat R\to\widehat M$ is an isomorphism. Completion is exact on short exact sequences of finite $R$-modules.
theorems.proof: The natural map $M\otimes_R\widehat R\to\widehat M$ is an isomorphism. Completion is exact on short exact sequences of finite $R$-modules.

theorems.subject: ring-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Flatness of Noetherian completion
theorems.hypotheses: Let $I$ be an ideal of a Noetherian ring $R$.
theorems.statement: The ring map $R\to\widehat R$ is flat. The $I$-adic completion functor is exact on finite $R$-modules.
theorems.proof: The ring map $R\to\widehat R$ is flat. The $I$-adic completion functor is exact on finite $R$-modules.

theorems.subject: ring-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Faithful flatness of Noetherian completion
theorems.hypotheses: Let $I$ be an ideal of a Noetherian ring $R$ contained in its Jacobson radical.
theorems.statement: The ring map $R\to\widehat R$ is faithfully flat. In particular this holds for maximal-ideal completion of a Noetherian local ring.
theorems.proof: The ring map $R\to\widehat R$ is faithfully flat. In particular this holds for maximal-ideal completion of a Noetherian local ring.

theorems.subject: module-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Completeness after completion over a Noetherian ring
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be Noetherian, let $I\subseteq R$ be an ideal and $M$ any $R$-module.
theorems.statement: Its completion is complete, with $I^n\widehat M$ canonically the completion of $I^nM$ and $\widehat M/I^n\widehat M\cong M/I^nM$.
theorems.proof: Its completion is complete, with $I^n\widehat M$ canonically the completion of $I^nM$ and $\widehat M/I^n\widehat M\cong M/I^nM$.

theorems.subject: ring-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Noetherianity from the completed quotient
theorems.hypotheses: Let $I$ be a finitely generated ideal of a ring $R$ such that $R/I$ is Noetherian.
theorems.statement: The completion $\widehat R$ is Noetherian and is complete with respect to $I\widehat R$.
theorems.proof: The completion $\widehat R$ is Noetherian and is complete with respect to $I\widehat R$.

theorems.subject: ring-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Noetherianity of the completion
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be Noetherian and $I\subseteq R$ any ideal.
theorems.statement: The $I$-adic completion $\widehat R$ is Noetherian.
theorems.proof: The $I$-adic completion $\widehat R$ is Noetherian.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Finiteness after completion of a local map
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)\to(S,\mathfrak n)$ be a local map of local rings. Assume $\mathfrak m,\mathfrak n$ are finitely generated and $S/\mathfrak mS$ has finite dimension over $R/\mathfrak m$.
theorems.statement: The $\mathfrak n$-adic completion of $S$ agrees with its $\mathfrak mS$-adic completion and is finite over the $\mathfrak m$-adic completion of $R$.
theorems.proof: The $\mathfrak n$-adic completion of $S$ agrees with its $\mathfrak mS$-adic completion and is finite over the $\mathfrak m$-adic completion of $R$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-point
theorems.name: Completion of a finite algebra at a prime
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be Noetherian, let $S$ be finite over $R$, and let $\mathfrak p$ be a prime of $R$. Write $\mathfrak q_1,\ldots,\mathfrak q_m$ for all primes of $S$ over $\mathfrak p$.
theorems.statement: There are canonical isomorphisms $\widehat{R_{\mathfrak p}}\otimes_R S\cong\widehat{S_{\mathfrak p}}\cong\prod_{i=1}^m\widehat{S_{\mathfrak q_i}}$. Complete $S_{\mathfrak p}$ with respect to $\mathfrak p S_{\mathfrak p}$ and each of the local rings with respect to its maximal ideal.
theorems.proof: There are canonical isomorphisms $\widehat{R_{\mathfrak p}}\otimes_R S\cong\widehat{S_{\mathfrak p}}\cong\prod_{i=1}^m\widehat{S_{\mathfrak q_i}}$. Complete $S_{\mathfrak p}$ with respect to $\mathfrak p S_{\mathfrak p}$ and each of the local rings with respect to its maximal ideal.

theorems.subject: module-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Split completion of an exact sequence
theorems.hypotheses: Let $I\subseteq R$ be an ideal and $0\to K\to P\to M\to0$ exact. Assume $M$ is flat over $R$ and $M/IM$ projective over $R/I$.
theorems.statement: The sequence of $I$-adic completions $0\to\widehat K\to\widehat P\to\widehat M\to0$ is split exact.
theorems.proof: The sequence of $I$-adic completions $0\to\widehat K\to\widehat P\to\widehat M\to0$ is split exact.

theorems.subject: ring-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Completeness from completion of a quotient
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A$ be Noetherian and let $I,J$ be ideals of $A$. Assume $A$ is $I$-adically complete and $A/I$ is complete with respect to the image of $J$.
theorems.statement: The ring $A$ is $J$-adically complete.
theorems.proof: The ring $A$ is $J$-adically complete.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Projective syzygies in any partial projective resolution
theorems.hypotheses: Let $M$ have projective dimension $d$, and take an exact partial resolution $F_e\to F_{e-1}\to\cdots\to F_0\to M\to0$ with projective terms and $e\geq d-1$.
theorems.statement: The kernel of $F_e\to F_{e-1}$ is projective. When $e=0$ this means the kernel of $F_0\to M$.
theorems.proof: The kernel of $F_e\to F_{e-1}$ is projective. When $e=0$ this means the kernel of $F_0\to M$.

theorems.subject: ring-index
theorems.name: Fixed-index Serre conditions as specializations
theorems.hypotheses: Use a Noetherian ring $R$ and, for the module condition, a finite $R$-module $M$.
theorems.statement: The predicates $(R_0)$ and $(R_1)$ specialize the ring regularity bound to indices zero and one. The ring predicates $(S_1)$ and $(S_2)$ specialize the ring depth bound to one and two. The module predicate $(S_1)$ specializes the module depth bound to one.
theorems.proof: The predicates $(R_0)$ and $(R_1)$ specialize the ring regularity bound to indices zero and one. The ring predicates $(S_1)$ and $(S_2)$ specialize the ring depth bound to one and two. The module predicate $(S_1)$ specializes the module depth bound to one.

theorems.subject: ring-presentation
theorems.name: Standard smoothness and a presentation with invertible Jacobian
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be a ring map.
theorems.statement: The map is standard smooth exactly when it admits a standard smooth presentation. If an invertible maximal minor uses a different set of variables, permute those variables into the first $c$ places.
theorems.proof: The map is standard smooth exactly when it admits a standard smooth presentation. If an invertible maximal minor uses a different set of variables, permute those variables into the first $c$ places.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Cohen–Macaulayness modulo a module nonzerodivisor
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be Noetherian local, $M$ finite over $R$ and $x$ in the maximal ideal. Assume multiplication by $x$ is injective on $M$.
theorems.statement: The module $M$ is Cohen–Macaulay if and only if $M/xM$ is Cohen–Macaulay.
theorems.proof: The module $M$ is Cohen–Macaulay if and only if $M/xM$ is Cohen–Macaulay.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Cohen–Macaulayness across a quotient of local rings
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be a surjection of Noetherian local rings and let $M$ be a finite $S$-module.
theorems.statement: The module $M$ is Cohen–Macaulay over $S$ if and only if it is Cohen–Macaulay over $R$.
theorems.proof: The module $M$ is Cohen–Macaulay over $S$ if and only if it is Cohen–Macaulay over $R$.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Localization of a Cohen–Macaulay module
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be Noetherian local, let $M$ be Cohen–Macaulay over $R$, and choose a prime $\mathfrak p$ of $R$.
theorems.statement: The localization $M_{\mathfrak p}$ is Cohen–Macaulay over $R_{\mathfrak p}$.
theorems.proof: The localization $M_{\mathfrak p}$ is Cohen–Macaulay over $R_{\mathfrak p}$.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Cohen–Macaulayness under polynomial extension
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be Noetherian and $M$ a Cohen–Macaulay module. Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer.
theorems.statement: Then $M\otimes_R R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ is Cohen–Macaulay over $R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$.
theorems.proof: Then $M\otimes_R R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ is Cohen–Macaulay over $R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Projective and global dimensions under localization
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be any ring, $M$ an $R$-module, and $S\subseteq R$ a multiplicative subset.
theorems.statement: If $M$ has projective dimension at most $n$, then $S^{-1}M$ has projective dimension at most $n$ over $S^{-1}R$. If $R$ has global dimension at most $n$, the same holds for $S^{-1}R$.
theorems.proof: If $M$ has projective dimension at most $n$, then $S^{-1}M$ has projective dimension at most $n$ over $S^{-1}R$. If $R$ has global dimension at most $n$, the same holds for $S^{-1}R$.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Auslander–Buchsbaum formula
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be a Noetherian local ring and $M$ a nonzero finite $R$-module of finite projective dimension.
theorems.statement: Then $\operatorname{depth}(R)=\operatorname{pd}_R(M)+\operatorname{depth}_R(M)$.
theorems.proof: Then $\operatorname{depth}(R)=\operatorname{pd}_R(M)+\operatorname{depth}_R(M)$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Dimension lower bound under going up or going down
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ satisfy either going up or going down. Assume the map on prime spectra is surjective.
theorems.statement: Then $\dim R\leq\dim S$.
theorems.proof: Then $\dim R\leq\dim S$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Contraction of a maximal ideal under going up
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ satisfy going up and let $\mathfrak q$ be a maximal ideal of $S$.
theorems.statement: Its contraction in $R$ is maximal.
theorems.proof: Its contraction in $R$ is maximal.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Dimension upper bound for integral maps
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be an integral ring map.
theorems.statement: Then $\dim S\leq\dim R$, and closed points of $\operatorname{Spec}(S)$ map to closed points of $\operatorname{Spec}(R)$.
theorems.proof: Then $\dim S\leq\dim R$, and closed points of $\operatorname{Spec}(S)$ map to closed points of $\operatorname{Spec}(R)$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Dimension preserved by integral inclusions
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\subseteq S$ be an integral inclusion of rings.
theorems.statement: Then $\dim R=\dim S$.
theorems.proof: Then $\dim R=\dim S$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-point
theorems.name: Local dimension inequality with a fibre
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be a map of Noetherian rings and $\mathfrak q$ a prime of $S$ over $\mathfrak p$.
theorems.statement: Then $\dim S_{\mathfrak q}\leq\dim R_{\mathfrak p}+\dim(S_{\mathfrak q}/\mathfrak pS_{\mathfrak q})$.
theorems.proof: Then $\dim S_{\mathfrak q}\leq\dim R_{\mathfrak p}+\dim(S_{\mathfrak q}/\mathfrak pS_{\mathfrak q})$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-point
theorems.name: Local dimension equality under going down
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be a map of Noetherian rings satisfying going down and $\mathfrak q$ a prime of $S$ over $\mathfrak p$.
theorems.statement: Then $\dim S_{\mathfrak q}=\dim R_{\mathfrak p}+\dim(S_{\mathfrak q}/\mathfrak pS_{\mathfrak q})$.
theorems.proof: Then $\dim S_{\mathfrak q}=\dim R_{\mathfrak p}+\dim(S_{\mathfrak q}/\mathfrak pS_{\mathfrak q})$.

theorems.subject: local-ring
theorems.name: Additivity of lengths for products of nonzerodivisors
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be semilocal Noetherian of dimension one and let $a,b\in R$ be nonzerodivisors.
theorems.statement: The three quotient lengths are finite and $\ell_R(R/(ab))=\ell_R(R/(a))+\ell_R(R/(b))$.
theorems.proof: The three quotient lengths are finite and $\ell_R(R/(ab))=\ell_R(R/(a))+\ell_R(R/(b))$.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Containment and lengths of lattices
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be a one-dimensional Noetherian local domain with fraction field $K$, and let $V$ be finite-dimensional over $K$. Let $M\subseteq V$ be a lattice.
theorems.statement: A submodule of $V$ containing $M$ is a lattice exactly when it is finitely generated, or equivalently when its quotient by $M$ has finite length. A submodule $N\subseteq M$ is a lattice exactly when $M/N$ has finite length. Two lattices have lattice intersection and sum. Lengths of quotients add along chains of nested lattices, and the distance between two lattices equals the difference of their quotient lengths by any common sublattice.
theorems.proof: A submodule of $V$ containing $M$ is a lattice exactly when it is finitely generated, or equivalently when its quotient by $M$ has finite length. A submodule $N\subseteq M$ is a lattice exactly when $M/N$ has finite length. Two lattices have lattice intersection and sum. Lengths of quotients add along chains of nested lattices, and the distance between two lattices equals the difference of their quotient lengths by any common sublattice.

theorems.subject: lattice-pair
theorems.name: Additivity of signed lattice distance
theorems.hypotheses: Let $M,N,P$ be lattices in a fixed finite-dimensional vector space over the fraction field of a one-dimensional Noetherian local domain.
theorems.statement: One has $d(M,P)=d(M,N)+d(N,P)$ and $d(M,N)=-d(N,M)$.
theorems.proof: One has $d(M,P)=d(M,N)+d(N,P)$ and $d(M,N)=-d(N,M)$.

theorems.subject: lattice-pair
theorems.name: Lattice distance and determinant
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be a one-dimensional Noetherian local domain with fraction field $K$, let $M$ be a lattice in a finite-dimensional $K$-vector space, and let $u$ be a $K$-linear automorphism of that space.
theorems.statement: Then $d(M,uM)=\operatorname{ord}_R(\det u)$.
theorems.proof: Then $d(M,uM)=\operatorname{ord}_R(\det u)$.

theorems.subject: local-ring
theorems.name: Orders of vanishing and field norms
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A$ be a one-dimensional Noetherian local domain with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$, and let $A\subseteq B$ be a finite extension of domains. Write $L/K$ for the fraction-field extension, and choose $y\in L^\times$.
theorems.statement: The ring $B$ is semilocal. The order of $\operatorname{Nm}_{L/K}(y)$ at $A$ equals $\sum_{\mathfrak n}[\kappa(\mathfrak n):\kappa(\mathfrak m)]\operatorname{ord}_{B_{\mathfrak n}}(y)$, summed over the maximal ideals $\mathfrak n$ of $B$.
theorems.proof: The ring $B$ is semilocal. The order of $\operatorname{Nm}_{L/K}(y)$ at $A$ equals $\sum_{\mathfrak n}[\kappa(\mathfrak n):\kappa(\mathfrak m)]\operatorname{ord}_{B_{\mathfrak n}}(y)$, summed over the maximal ideals $\mathfrak n$ of $B$.

theorems.subject: algebra-element
theorems.name: Strong transcendence modulo a minimal prime
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\subseteq S$ be reduced rings and let $x\in S$ be strongly transcendental over $R$. Choose a minimal prime $\mathfrak q$ of $S$, and let $\mathfrak p=R\cap\mathfrak q$.
theorems.statement: The image of $x$ in $S/\mathfrak q$ is strongly transcendental over $R/\mathfrak p$.
theorems.proof: The image of $x$ in $S/\mathfrak q$ is strongly transcendental over $R/\mathfrak p$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Strong transcendence excludes quasi-finiteness
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\subseteq S$ be reduced rings and let $x\in S$ be strongly transcendental over $R$. Assume $S$ is finite over $R[x]$.
theorems.statement: The map $R\to S$ is quasi-finite at no prime of $S$.
theorems.proof: The map $R\to S$ is quasi-finite at no prime of $S$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Openness of the quasi-finite locus
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be of finite type.
theorems.statement: The locus of primes where $R\to S$ is quasi-finite is open in $\operatorname{Spec}(S)$.
theorems.proof: The locus of primes where $R\to S$ is quasi-finite is open in $\operatorname{Spec}(S)$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Quasi-finite map through the integral closure
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be a quasi-finite finite type map and let $S'$ be the integral closure of the image of $R$ in $S$.
theorems.statement: The map $\operatorname{Spec}(S)\to\operatorname{Spec}(S')$ is a homeomorphism onto an open subset. If $g\in S'$ and $D(g)$ lies in that subset, then $S'_g\cong S_g$. There exists a finite $R$-subalgebra $S''\subseteq S'$ for which these conclusions hold for $S''\to S$.
theorems.proof: The map $\operatorname{Spec}(S)\to\operatorname{Spec}(S')$ is a homeomorphism onto an open subset. If $g\in S'$ and $D(g)$ lies in that subset, then $S'_g\cong S_g$. There exists a finite $R$-subalgebra $S''\subseteq S'$ for which these conclusions hold for $S''\to S$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-point
theorems.name: Local polynomial factorization of a prescribed relative dimension
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be finite type and suppose $\dim_{\mathfrak q}(S/R)=n$.
theorems.statement: There is a $g\notin\mathfrak q$ and a quasi-finite map $R[t_1,\ldots,t_n]\to S_g$.
theorems.proof: There is a $g\notin\mathfrak q$ and a quasi-finite map $R[t_1,\ldots,t_n]\to S_g$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-point
theorems.name: Local polynomial factorization with prescribed contraction
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be finite type, let $\mathfrak q$ lie over $\mathfrak p$, and put $n=\dim_{\mathfrak q}(S/R)$ and $r=\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(\mathfrak p)}\kappa(\mathfrak q)$.
theorems.statement: There exist $f\notin\mathfrak p$ and $g\notin\mathfrak q$ and a quasi-finite map $R_f[t_1,\ldots,t_n]\to S_g$ under which the contraction of $\mathfrak qS_g$ is $(\mathfrak p,t_{r+1},\ldots,t_n)$.
theorems.proof: There exist $f\notin\mathfrak p$ and $g\notin\mathfrak q$ and a quasi-finite map $R_f[t_1,\ldots,t_n]\to S_g$ under which the contraction of $\mathfrak qS_g$ is $(\mathfrak p,t_{r+1},\ldots,t_n)$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-point
theorems.name: Dimension bound at a quasi-finite point
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be finite type and quasi-finite at the prime $\mathfrak q$ of $S$ lying over $\mathfrak p$.
theorems.statement: Then $\dim S_{\mathfrak q}\leq\dim R_{\mathfrak p}$.
theorems.proof: Then $\dim S_{\mathfrak q}\leq\dim R_{\mathfrak p}$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Dimension of a quasi-finite algebra over affine space
theorems.hypotheses: Let $S$ be a finite type algebra over a field $k$ with a quasi-finite inclusion $k[t_1,\ldots,t_n]\subseteq S$.
theorems.statement: Then $\dim S\leq n$.
theorems.proof: Then $\dim S\leq n$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-point
theorems.name: Upper semicontinuity of relative dimension on the source
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be finite type and let $n=\dim_{\mathfrak q}(S/R)$ at a prime $\mathfrak q$ of $S$.
theorems.statement: There is an open neighbourhood of $\mathfrak q$ on which relative dimension is at most $n$.
theorems.proof: There is an open neighbourhood of $\mathfrak q$ on which relative dimension is at most $n$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-point
theorems.name: Relative dimension and base change
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be finite type, let $R\to R'$ be any ring map, and put $S'=S\otimes_R R'$.
theorems.statement: For each nonnegative integer $n$, the inverse image of the locus in $\operatorname{Spec}(S)$ of relative dimension at most $n$ is the corresponding locus in $\operatorname{Spec}(S')$ over $R'$.
theorems.proof: For each nonnegative integer $n$, the inverse image of the locus in $\operatorname{Spec}(S)$ of relative dimension at most $n$ is the corresponding locus in $\operatorname{Spec}(S')$ over $R'$.

theorems.subject: ring-map-point
theorems.name: Quasi-compactness of the bounded relative dimension locus
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be of finite presentation and let $n\geq0$.
theorems.statement: The subset of $\operatorname{Spec}(S)$ of relative dimension at most $n$ is open and quasi-compact.
theorems.proof: The subset of $\operatorname{Spec}(S)$ of relative dimension at most $n$ is open and quasi-compact.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Comparison of fibre dimensions over a valuation ring
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be a valuation ring with residue field $k$ and fraction field $K$. Let $S$ be a finite type domain containing $R$. Assume $S\otimes_R k\ne0$.
theorems.statement: The dimensions of $S\otimes_R k$ and $S\otimes_R K$ agree, and the spectrum of $S\otimes_R k$ is equidimensional.
theorems.proof: The dimensions of $S\otimes_R k$ and $S\otimes_R K$ agree, and the spectrum of $S\otimes_R k$ is equidimensional.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Universal property of Kähler differentials
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be a ring map and let $M$ be an $S$-module.
theorems.statement: Composition with the universal derivation identifies $\operatorname{Hom}_S(\Omega_{S/R},M)$ with $\operatorname{Der}_R(S,M)$ naturally in $M$.
theorems.proof: Composition with the universal derivation identifies $\operatorname{Hom}_S(\Omega_{S/R},M)$ with $\operatorname{Der}_R(S,M)$ naturally in $M$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Kähler differentials and directed colimits
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(R_i\to S_i)$ be a directed system of ring maps with colimit $R\to S$.
theorems.statement: The canonical map $\varinjlim_i\Omega_{S_i/R_i}\to\Omega_{S/R}$ is an isomorphism with respect to the natural $S$-module structure on the colimit.
theorems.proof: The canonical map $\varinjlim_i\Omega_{S_i/R_i}\to\Omega_{S/R}$ is an isomorphism with respect to the natural $S$-module structure on the colimit.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Differentials in a commutative square with surjective target map
theorems.hypotheses: Let a commutative square consist of $R\to S$, $\beta:R'\to S'$, and compatible maps $R\to R'$, $\varphi:S\to S'$. Assume $\varphi$ is surjective.
theorems.statement: The induced map $\Omega_{S/R}\to\Omega_{S'/R'}$ is surjective. Its kernel as an $S$-module is generated by $\mathrm da$ for $a\in S$ such that $\varphi(a)\in\beta(R')$.
theorems.proof: The induced map $\Omega_{S/R}\to\Omega_{S'/R'}$ is surjective. Its kernel as an $S$-module is generated by $\mathrm da$ for $a\in S$ such that $\varphi(a)\in\beta(R')$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Transitivity sequence of differentials
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A\to B\to C$ be ring maps.
theorems.statement: There is a canonical exact sequence $C\otimes_B\Omega_{B/A}\to\Omega_{C/A}\to\Omega_{C/B}\to0$.
theorems.proof: There is a canonical exact sequence $C\otimes_B\Omega_{B/A}\to\Omega_{C/A}\to\Omega_{C/B}\to0$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Kähler differentials and localization
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A\to B$ be a ring map. On the source, localize at a multiplicative subset whose image in $B$ is invertible. On the target, localize at any multiplicative subset $T$ of $B$.
theorems.statement: Localizing the source does not change $\Omega_{B/A}$. Localizing the target identifies $T^{-1}\Omega_{B/A}$ with $\Omega_{T^{-1}B/A}$.
theorems.proof: Localizing the source does not change $\Omega_{B/A}$. Localizing the target identifies $T^{-1}\Omega_{B/A}$ with $\Omega_{T^{-1}B/A}$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Conormal sequence of a quotient
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be a ring map and $S'=S/I$ for an ideal $I$ of $S$.
theorems.statement: There is a canonical exact sequence $I/I^2\to\Omega_{S/R}\otimes_S S'\to\Omega_{S'/R}\to0$ in which the first map sends $f\bmod I^2$ to $\mathrm df\otimes1$.
theorems.proof: There is a canonical exact sequence $I/I^2\to\Omega_{S/R}\otimes_S S'\to\Omega_{S'/R}\to0$ in which the first map sends $f\bmod I^2$ to $\mathrm df\otimes1$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Split conormal sequence for a quotient with a section
theorems.hypotheses: Let $S\to S'=S/I$ be a surjection of $R$-algebras admitting an $R$-algebra section.
theorems.statement: Its conormal sequence $0\to I/I^2\to\Omega_{S/R}\otimes_S S'\to\Omega_{S'/R}\to0$ is split exact.
theorems.proof: Its conormal sequence $0\to I/I^2\to\Omega_{S/R}\otimes_S S'\to\Omega_{S'/R}\to0$ is split exact.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Differentials of a quotient modulo an earlier ideal power
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be a ring map, $I$ an ideal of $S$, and $n\geq1$. Write $S'=S/I^{n+1}$.
theorems.statement: The canonical map $\Omega_{S/R}\otimes_S S/I^n\to\Omega_{S'/R}\otimes_{S'} S/I^n$ is an isomorphism.
theorems.proof: The canonical map $\Omega_{S/R}\otimes_S S/I^n\to\Omega_{S'/R}\otimes_{S'} S/I^n$ is an isomorphism.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Arbitrary base change for Kähler differentials
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to R'$ and $R\to S$ be ring maps and put $S'=S\otimes_R R'$.
theorems.statement: The canonical map $\Omega_{S/R}\otimes_R R'\to\Omega_{S'/R'}$ is an isomorphism.
theorems.proof: The canonical map $\Omega_{S/R}\otimes_R R'\to\Omega_{S'/R'}$ is an isomorphism.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Kähler differentials as the conormal of the diagonal
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be a ring map and $J=\ker(S\otimes_R S\to S)$, where the map is multiplication.
theorems.statement: There is a canonical isomorphism $\Omega_{S/R}\cong J/J^2$ taking $a\,\mathrm db$ to $a\otimes b-ab\otimes1$ modulo $J^2$.
theorems.proof: There is a canonical isomorphism $\Omega_{S/R}\cong J/J^2$ taking $a\,\mathrm db$ to $a\otimes b-ab\otimes1$ modulo $J^2$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Differentials of a polynomial ring
theorems.hypotheses: Let $S=R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$.
theorems.statement: The module $\Omega_{S/R}$ is free over $S$ on $\mathrm dx_1,\ldots,\mathrm dx_n$.
theorems.proof: The module $\Omega_{S/R}$ is free over $S$ on $\mathrm dx_1,\ldots,\mathrm dx_n$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Finite presentation of the module of differentials
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be of finite presentation.
theorems.statement: Then $\Omega_{S/R}$ is finitely presented over $S$.
theorems.proof: Then $\Omega_{S/R}$ is finitely presented over $S$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Finite generation of the module of differentials
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be of finite type.
theorems.statement: Then $\Omega_{S/R}$ is finite over $S$.
theorems.proof: Then $\Omega_{S/R}$ is finite over $S$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Base change for the de Rham complex
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A\to A'$ and $A\to B$ be ring maps. Set $B'=B\otimes_A A'$.
theorems.statement: The canonical map $\Omega^\bullet_{B/A}\otimes_A A'\to\Omega^\bullet_{B'/A'}$ is an isomorphism of complexes.
theorems.proof: The canonical map $\Omega^\bullet_{B/A}\otimes_A A'\to\Omega^\bullet_{B'/A'}$ is an isomorphism of complexes.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: De Rham differential on a quotient of differentials
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A\to B$ be a ring map with a surjection $\Omega_{B/A}\to W$. Assume its kernel is generated by forms whose de Rham differential maps to zero in $\bigwedge^2_B W$.
theorems.statement: Exterior powers of $W$ carry the induced de Rham differential given by $\mathrm d(f_0\,\mathrm df_1\wedge\cdots\wedge\mathrm df_p)=\mathrm df_0\wedge\cdots\wedge\mathrm df_p$.
theorems.proof: Exterior powers of $W$ carry the induced de Rham differential given by $\mathrm d(f_0\,\mathrm df_1\wedge\cdots\wedge\mathrm df_p)=\mathrm df_0\wedge\cdots\wedge\mathrm df_p$.

theorems.subject: module-map
theorems.name: Order bound for composition of differential operators
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be a ring map and let composable operators of $S$-modules have orders at most $k$ and $k'$ over $R$.
theorems.statement: Their composite has order at most $k+k'$.
theorems.proof: Their composite has order at most $k+k'$.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Principal parts represent differential operators
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be a ring map, let $M,N$ be $S$-modules, and choose $k\geq0$.
theorems.statement: There is a natural isomorphism between the $R$-linear differential operators $M\to N$ of order at most $k$ and $\operatorname{Hom}_S(P^k_{S/R}(M),N)$.
theorems.proof: There is a natural isomorphism between the $R$-linear differential operators $M\to N$ of order at most $k$ and $\operatorname{Hom}_S(P^k_{S/R}(M),N)$.

theorems.subject: module-map
theorems.name: First-order operators from the algebra itself
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be a ring map and $N$ an $S$-module.
theorems.statement: An operator $D:S\to N$ of order at most one decomposes uniquely into the derivation $s\mapsto D(s)-sD(1)$ and multiplication by $D(1)$. In particular $P^1_{S/R}(S)\cong\Omega_{S/R}\oplus S$.
theorems.proof: An operator $D:S\to N$ of order at most one decomposes uniquely into the derivation $s\mapsto D(s)-sD(1)$ and multiplication by $D(1)$. In particular $P^1_{S/R}(S)\cong\Omega_{S/R}\oplus S$.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Short exact sequence of first principal parts
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be a ring map and $M$ an $S$-module.
theorems.statement: There is a natural short exact sequence $0\to\Omega_{S/R}\otimes_S M\to P^1_{S/R}(M)\to M\to0$.
theorems.proof: There is a natural short exact sequence $0\to\Omega_{S/R}\otimes_S M\to P^1_{S/R}(M)\to M\to0$.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Functoriality of the principal parts tower
theorems.hypotheses: Take a commutative square from a ring map $A\to B$ to a ring map $A'\to B'$, together with a $B$-linear map $M\to M'$ from a $B$-module to a $B'$-module.
theorems.statement: For every $k\geq0$ there is an induced $B$-linear map $P^k_{B/A}(M)\to P^k_{B'/A'}(M')$. These maps commute with transition maps in the order filtration and with composition of morphisms between such data.
theorems.proof: For every $k\geq0$ there is an induced $B$-linear map $P^k_{B/A}(M)\to P^k_{B'/A'}(M')$. These maps commute with transition maps in the order filtration and with composition of morphisms between such data.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Base change for principal parts
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A\to A'$ and $A\to B$ be ring maps, $M$ a $B$-module, $B'=B\otimes_A A'$, and $M'=M\otimes_A A'$.
theorems.statement: The canonical map $P^k_{B/A}(M)\otimes_A A'\to P^k_{B'/A'}(M')$ is an isomorphism.
theorems.proof: The canonical map $P^k_{B/A}(M)\otimes_A A'\to P^k_{B'/A'}(M')$ is an isomorphism.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Principal parts as a quotient by powers of the diagonal ideal
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be a ring map, let $M$ be an $S$-module and $J=\ker(S\otimes_R S\to S)$.
theorems.statement: There is an $S$-module isomorphism $P^k_{S/R}(M)\cong (S\otimes_R M)/J^{k+1}(S\otimes_R M)$. The $S$-action is on the first factor and the universal operator sends $m$ to the class of $1\otimes m$.
theorems.proof: There is an $S$-module isomorphism $P^k_{S/R}(M)\cong (S\otimes_R M)/J^{k+1}(S\otimes_R M)$. The $S$-action is on the first factor and the universal operator sends $m$ to the class of $1\otimes m$.

theorems.subject: module-map
theorems.name: Order of the de Rham differential
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A\to B$ be a ring map and let $i\geq0$.
theorems.statement: The de Rham differential $\Omega^i_{B/A}\to\Omega^{i+1}_{B/A}$ is a differential operator of order at most one over $A$.
theorems.proof: The de Rham differential $\Omega^i_{B/A}\to\Omega^{i+1}_{B/A}$ is a differential operator of order at most one over $A$.

theorems.subject: module-map
theorems.name: Testing order of a differential operator on algebra generators
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A\to B$ be a ring map, $(g_i)$ a set of generators of $B$ as an $A$-algebra, and $D$ an $A$-linear map of $B$-modules. Fix $k\geq1$.
theorems.statement: To prove that $D$ has order at most $k$, it suffices to check the commutators with the $g_i$ have order at most $k-1$.
theorems.proof: To prove that $D$ has order at most $k$, it suffices to check the commutators with the $g_i$ have order at most $k-1$.

theorems.subject: module-map
theorems.name: Localization of differential operators
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A\to B$ be a ring map, $T\subseteq B$ multiplicative and $D:M\to N$ an operator of $B$-modules of order at most $k$ over $A$.
theorems.statement: The map $D$ extends uniquely to an operator of order at most $k$ on the localized modules over $A\to T^{-1}B$.
theorems.proof: The map $D$ extends uniquely to an operator of order at most $k$ on the localized modules over $A\to T^{-1}B$.

theorems.subject: module-map
theorems.name: Tensoring a differential operator with another module
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to A$ and $R\to B$ be ring maps, $D:M\to M'$ an operator of $A$-modules of order at most $k$ over $R$, and $N$ a $B$-module.
theorems.statement: Then $D\otimes_R\operatorname{id}_N$ has order at most $k$ for $B\to A\otimes_R B$.
theorems.proof: Then $D\otimes_R\operatorname{id}_N$ has order at most $k$ for $B\to A\otimes_R B$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Independence of presentation for the naive cotangent complex
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be a ring map, with a polynomial presentation $P\twoheadrightarrow S$.
theorems.statement: The two-term complex from this presentation maps to the canonical naive cotangent complex by a quasi-isomorphism well-defined up to homotopy. Changes of presentation induce homotopy-compatible maps.
theorems.proof: The two-term complex from this presentation maps to the canonical naive cotangent complex by a quasi-isomorphism well-defined up to homotopy. Changes of presentation induce homotopy-compatible maps.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Flat base change of the naive cotangent complex
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ and $R\to R'$ be ring maps with $R\to R'$ flat. Write $S'=S\otimes_R R'$.
theorems.statement: The canonical map $\mathrm{NL}_{S/R}\otimes_S S'\to\mathrm{NL}_{S'/R'}$ is a homotopy equivalence.
theorems.proof: The canonical map $\mathrm{NL}_{S/R}\otimes_S S'\to\mathrm{NL}_{S'/R'}$ is a homotopy equivalence.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Naive cotangent complex of a localization
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A$ be a ring and $T\subseteq A$ a multiplicative subset.
theorems.statement: The naive cotangent complex of $A\to T^{-1}A$ is homotopy equivalent to zero.
theorems.proof: The naive cotangent complex of $A\to T^{-1}A$ is homotopy equivalent to zero.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Stable isomorphism of conormal modules of presentations
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be finite type, with two finite polynomial presentations on $n$ and $m$ variables and kernels $I$ and $J$, respectively.
theorems.statement: There is an $S$-module isomorphism $I/I^2\oplus S^{\oplus m}\cong J/J^2\oplus S^{\oplus n}$.
theorems.proof: There is an $S$-module isomorphism $I/I^2\oplus S^{\oplus m}\cong J/J^2\oplus S^{\oplus n}$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Existence of the universal first-order thickening
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be formally unramified.
theorems.statement: A square-zero surjection $S'\to S$ representing the universal first-order lifting problem exists.
theorems.proof: A square-zero surjection $S'\to S$ representing the universal first-order lifting problem exists.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Universal first-order thickening of a quotient
theorems.hypotheses: Let $I$ be an ideal of $R$ and $S=R/I$.
theorems.statement: The universal first-order thickening of $S$ over $R$ is $R/I^2\to R/I$, and its conormal module is $I/I^2$.
theorems.proof: The universal first-order thickening of $S$ over $R$ is $R/I^2\to R/I$, and its conormal module is $I/I^2$.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Localization of universal first-order thickenings
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A\to B$ be formally unramified and let $B'\to B$ be its universal first-order thickening.
theorems.statement: A multiplicative subset of $A$ can be inverted in both $B'$ and $B$ to obtain the universal thickening over the localized base. For a multiplicative subset of $B$, invert its inverse image in $B'$ to get the universal thickening over $A$ of the localized target. The conormal modules localize accordingly.
theorems.proof: A multiplicative subset of $A$ can be inverted in both $B'$ and $B$ to obtain the universal thickening over the localized base. For a multiplicative subset of $B$, invert its inverse image in $B'$ to get the universal thickening over $A$ of the localized target. The conormal modules localize accordingly.

theorems.subject: ring-map
theorems.name: Differentials for a universal first-order thickening
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to A\to B$ be ring maps with $A\to B$ formally unramified. Let $B'\to B$ be the universal first-order thickening over $A$.
theorems.statement: The map $A\to B'$ is formally unramified and the canonical map $\Omega_{A/R}\otimes_A B\to\Omega_{B'/R}\otimes_{B'}B$ is an isomorphism.
theorems.proof: The map $A\to B'$ is formally unramified and the canonical map $\Omega_{A/R}\otimes_A B\to\Omega_{B'/R}\otimes_{B'}B$ is an isomorphism.

theorems.subject: local-ring
theorems.name: Construction of henselization
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(R,\mathfrak m,\kappa)$ be a local ring.
theorems.statement: There is a local map $R\to R^h$ into a henselian local ring with maximal ideal $\mathfrak mR^h$ and residue field $\kappa$. The ring $R^h$ is a filtered colimit of étale $R$-algebras.
theorems.proof: There is a local map $R\to R^h$ into a henselian local ring with maximal ideal $\mathfrak mR^h$ and residue field $\kappa$. The ring $R^h$ is a filtered colimit of étale $R$-algebras.

theorems.subject: local-ring
theorems.name: Construction of strict henselization
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(R,\mathfrak m,\kappa)$ be a local ring with a specified separable algebraic closure $\kappa^{\mathrm{sep}}$ of its residue field.
theorems.statement: There is a local map $R^h\to R^{\mathrm{sh}}$, compatible with $\kappa\subseteq\kappa^{\mathrm{sep}}$. Its target is strictly henselian with maximal ideal $\mathfrak mR^{\mathrm{sh}}$, residue field $\kappa^{\mathrm{sep}}$, and is a filtered colimit of étale $R$-algebras.
theorems.proof: There is a local map $R^h\to R^{\mathrm{sh}}$, compatible with $\kappa\subseteq\kappa^{\mathrm{sep}}$. Its target is strictly henselian with maximal ideal $\mathfrak mR^{\mathrm{sh}}$, residue field $\kappa^{\mathrm{sep}}$, and is a filtered colimit of étale $R$-algebras.

theorems.subject: local-ring
theorems.name: The Cohen structure theorem
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a complete local ring.
theorems.statement: The ring has a coefficient ring. If $\mathfrak m$ is finitely generated, $R$ is a quotient of a formal power series ring in finitely many variables over a field or a Cohen ring.
theorems.proof: The ring has a coefficient ring. If $\mathfrak m$ is finitely generated, $R$ is a quotient of a formal power series ring in finitely many variables over a field or a Cohen ring.

theorems.subject: ring-inclusion
theorems.name: Descent of N-1 and N-2 along finite extensions
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be a Noetherian domain and $R\subseteq S$ a finite extension of domains.
theorems.statement: If $S$ satisfies N-1 then $R$ satisfies N-1. If $S$ satisfies N-2 then $R$ satisfies N-2.
theorems.proof: If $S$ satisfies N-1 then $R$ satisfies N-1. If $S$ satisfies N-2 then $R$ satisfies N-2.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Purely inseparable test for N-2
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be a Noetherian domain with fraction field $K$ of positive characteristic.
theorems.statement: The ring $R$ satisfies N-2 precisely when its integral closure in every finite purely inseparable extension of $K$ is finite over $R$.
theorems.proof: The ring $R$ satisfies N-2 precisely when its integral closure in every finite purely inseparable extension of $K$ is finite over $R$.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Local and generic test for N-1
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be a Noetherian domain.
theorems.statement: The ring satisfies N-1 exactly when it has a normal principal open $D(f)$ with $f\ne0$ and every localization at a maximal ideal satisfies N-1.
theorems.proof: The ring satisfies N-1 exactly when it has a normal principal open $D(f)$ with $f\ne0$ and every localization at a maximal ideal satisfies N-1.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Analytical unramifiedness and minimal primes
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be a Noetherian local ring.
theorems.statement: If $R$ is analytically unramified then it is reduced, all its minimal primes are analytically unramified, and its normalization in its total ring of fractions is finite over $R$. Conversely a reduced $R$ is analytically unramified if all its minimal primes are analytically unramified.
theorems.proof: If $R$ is analytically unramified then it is reduced, all its minimal primes are analytically unramified, and its normalization in its total ring of fractions is finite over $R$. Conversely a reduced $R$ is analytically unramified if all its minimal primes are analytically unramified.

theorems.subject: ring-map-point
theorems.name: Discrete valuation rings above analytically unramified primes
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be Noetherian local and $\mathfrak p$ an analytically unramified prime such that $R_{\mathfrak p}$ is a discrete valuation ring. Let $\mathfrak q$ be an associated prime of $\widehat R/\mathfrak p\widehat R$.
theorems.statement: Then $(\widehat R)_{\mathfrak q}$ is a discrete valuation ring.
theorems.proof: Then $(\widehat R)_{\mathfrak q}$ is a discrete valuation ring.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Analytical unramifiedness from a hypersurface section
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be a Noetherian local domain and $x$ a nonzero element of its maximal ideal. Assume $R/xR$ has no embedded primes, and for each associated prime $\mathfrak p$ of $R/xR$ assume $R_{\mathfrak p}$ is regular and $\mathfrak p$ is analytically unramified.
theorems.statement: Then $R$ is analytically unramified.
theorems.proof: Then $R$ is analytically unramified.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Analytical criterion for a local ring to be Nagata
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a Noetherian local ring.
theorems.statement: The ring $R$ is Nagata if and only if every local ring $S_{\mathfrak n}$ at a maximal ideal of a finite domain algebra $S$ over $R$ is analytically unramified. Equivalently it suffices to test finite local homomorphisms into domains.
theorems.proof: The ring $R$ is Nagata if and only if every local ring $S_{\mathfrak n}$ at a maximal ideal of a finite domain algebra $S$ over $R$ is analytically unramified. Equivalently it suffices to test finite local homomorphisms into domains.

theorems.subject: ring-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Definition of a Zariski pair
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A$ be a commutative ring and $I\subseteq A$ an ideal.
theorems.statement: The pair is a Zariski pair exactly when $I$ lies in the Jacobson radical of $A$.
theorems.proof: The pair is a Zariski pair exactly when $I$ lies in the Jacobson radical of $A$.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Stable freeness in a short exact sequence
theorems.hypotheses: Let $0\to M_1\to M_2\to M_3\to0$ be short exact, with all three modules finite projective over $R$.
theorems.statement: If any two of the three modules are stably free, so is the third. The short exact sequence splits because the quotient is projective.
theorems.proof: If any two of the three modules are stably free, so is the third. The short exact sequence splits because the quotient is projective.

theorems.subject: ring-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Lifting a finite stably free module
theorems.hypotheses: Let $I\subseteq\operatorname{Jac}(R)$ and let $E$ be a finite stably free $R/I$-module.
theorems.statement: There exists a finite stably free $R$-module $M$ with $M/IM\cong E$.
theorems.proof: There exists a finite stably free $R$-module $M$ with $M/IM\cong E$.

theorems.subject: ring-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Projectivity from a projective reduction
theorems.hypotheses: Let $I\subseteq\operatorname{Jac}(R)$, and let $M$ be a finite flat $R$-module such that $M/IM$ is projective over $R/I$.
theorems.statement: The module $M$ is finite projective over $R$.
theorems.proof: The module $M$ is finite projective over $R$.

theorems.subject: ring-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Detecting isomorphisms of finite projective modules
theorems.hypotheses: Let $I\subseteq\operatorname{Jac}(R)$ and let $P,P'$ be finite projective $R$-modules.
theorems.statement: Every homomorphism $P\to P'$ inducing an isomorphism modulo $I$ is an isomorphism. In particular an isomorphism $P/IP\cong P'/IP'$ lifts to an isomorphism $P\cong P'$.
theorems.proof: Every homomorphism $P\to P'$ inducing an isomorphism modulo $I$ is an isomorphism. In particular an isomorphism $P/IP\cong P'/IP'$ lifts to an isomorphism $P\cong P'$.

theorems.subject: ring-ideal-pair
theorems.name: A Zariski pair detects equality of idempotents
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(A,I)$ be a Zariski pair.
theorems.statement: Reduction from idempotents of $A$ to idempotents of $A/I$ is injective.
theorems.proof: Reduction from idempotents of $A$ to idempotents of $A/I$ is injective.

theorems.subject: ring-ideal-pair
theorems.name: A Zariski pair detects certain algebra isomorphisms
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(A,I)$ be a Zariski pair and $A\to B$ a flat integral map of finite presentation. Assume that $A/I\to B/IB$ is an isomorphism.
theorems.statement: The map $A\to B$ is an isomorphism.
theorems.proof: The map $A\to B$ is an isomorphism.

theorems.subject: ring-ideal-pair
theorems.name: A monic annihilator of a lifted idempotent
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(A,I)$ be a Zariski pair and $B$ a finite $A$-algebra. Suppose $B/IB=B_1\times B_2$, $A/I\to B_1$ is surjective and $b\in B$ maps to $(1,0)$.
theorems.statement: There is a monic $F(T)\in A[T]$ with $F(b)=0$ and $F(T)\equiv (T-1)T^d$ modulo $I$ for some $d\geq1$.
theorems.proof: There is a monic $F(T)\in A[T]$ with $F(b)=0$ and $F(T)\equiv (T-1)T^d$ modulo $I$ for some $d\geq1$.

theorems.subject: ring-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Jacobson localization away from a Zariski pair
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(A,I)$ be a Zariski pair, assume $A$ is Noetherian and take $f\in I$.
theorems.statement: The localization $A_f$ is a Jacobson ring.
theorems.proof: The localization $A_f$ is a Jacobson ring.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Absolute integral closedness passes to quotients and localizations
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A$ be an absolutely integrally closed ring.
theorems.statement: For every ideal $I$ and every multiplicative subset $S$, the rings $A/I$ and $S^{-1}A$ are absolutely integrally closed.
theorems.proof: For every ideal $I$ and every multiplicative subset $S$, the rings $A/I$ and $S^{-1}A$ are absolutely integrally closed.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Descent of absolute integral closedness from a localization
theorems.hypotheses: Let $S$ consist of nonzerodivisors of $A$. Suppose $A$ is integrally closed in $S^{-1}A$ and $S^{-1}A$ is absolutely integrally closed.
theorems.statement: The ring $A$ is absolutely integrally closed.
theorems.proof: The ring $A$ is absolutely integrally closed.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Fraction field criterion for a normal domain
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A$ be a normal domain with fraction field $K$.
theorems.statement: The ring $A$ is absolutely integrally closed if and only if $K$ is algebraically closed.
theorems.proof: The ring $A$ is absolutely integrally closed if and only if $K$ is algebraically closed.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Embedding in an absolutely integrally closed algebra
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A$ be any commutative ring.
theorems.statement: There exists an embedding $A\hookrightarrow B$ into an absolutely integrally closed ring such that $B$ is free over $A$ and is a filtered colimit of finite free $A$-algebras.
theorems.proof: There exists an embedding $A\hookrightarrow B$ into an absolutely integrally closed ring such that $B$ is free over $A$ and is a filtered colimit of finite free $A$-algebras.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Localizations of absolutely integrally closed rings are strictly henselian
theorems.hypotheses: Let $A$ be absolutely integrally closed and let $\mathfrak p\subset A$ be prime.
theorems.statement: The local ring $A_{\mathfrak p}$ is strictly henselian.
theorems.proof: The local ring $A_{\mathfrak p}$ is strictly henselian.

theorems.subject: ring-ideal-pair
theorems.name: Henselianity in an absolutely integrally closed ring
theorems.hypotheses: Let $I$ be an ideal of an absolutely integrally closed ring $A$.
theorems.statement: The pair $(A,I)$ is henselian exactly when $I\subseteq\operatorname{Jac}(A)$ and reduction from idempotents of $A$ to idempotents of $A/I$ is bijective.
theorems.proof: The pair $(A,I)$ is henselian exactly when $I\subseteq\operatorname{Jac}(A)$ and reduction from idempotents of $A$ to idempotents of $A/I$ is bijective.

theorems.subject: ring
theorems.name: Testing universal injectivity of a projective-module map
theorems.hypotheses: Assume every proper finitely generated ideal of $R$ has a nonzero annihilator. Let $u:N\to M$ be a homomorphism of projective $R$-modules.
theorems.statement: The map $u$ is universally injective if and only if it is injective.
theorems.proof: The map $u$ is universally injective if and only if it is injective.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Rank is invariant under a map with torsion kernel and cokernel
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be a domain and let $u:M\to N$ be an $R$-linear map with torsion kernel and cokernel.
theorems.statement: Tensoring with the fraction field makes $u$ an isomorphism, so $\operatorname{rank}_R(M)=\operatorname{rank}_R(N)$.
theorems.proof: Tensoring with the fraction field makes $u$ an isomorphism, so $\operatorname{rank}_R(M)=\operatorname{rank}_R(N)$.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Rank is additive in a short exact sequence
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be a domain and let $0\to M_1\to M_2\to M_3\to0$ be short exact.
theorems.statement: One has $\operatorname{rank}(M_2)=\operatorname{rank}(M_1)+\operatorname{rank}(M_3)$, with cardinal addition when necessary.
theorems.proof: One has $\operatorname{rank}(M_2)=\operatorname{rank}(M_1)+\operatorname{rank}(M_3)$, with cardinal addition when necessary.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Ranks of tensor products and Hom modules
theorems.hypotheses: Let $M,N$ be modules over a domain $R$. For the Hom formula assume additionally that $M$ is finitely presented.
theorems.statement: The tensor rank is the cardinal product $\operatorname{rank}(M)\operatorname{rank}(N)$. For Hom the rank is the dimension of $\operatorname{Hom}_K(M\otimes_RK,N\otimes_RK)$ over the fraction field $K$, equal to $\operatorname{rank}(M)\operatorname{rank}(N)$ because $M$ has finite rank.
theorems.proof: The tensor rank is the cardinal product $\operatorname{rank}(M)\operatorname{rank}(N)$. For Hom the rank is the dimension of $\operatorname{Hom}_K(M\otimes_RK,N\otimes_RK)$ over the fraction field $K$, equal to $\operatorname{rank}(M)\operatorname{rank}(N)$ because $M$ has finite rank.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Rank under an injective extension of domains
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\hookrightarrow R'$ be an injective homomorphism of domains and $M$ an $R$-module.
theorems.statement: The rank of $M\otimes_R R'$ over $R'$ is the rank of $M$ over $R$.
theorems.proof: The rank of $M\otimes_R R'$ over $R'$ is the rank of $M$ over $R$.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: A finite module is free on a nonempty principal open
theorems.hypotheses: Let $M$ be a finite module of rank $r$ over a domain $R$.
theorems.statement: There is a map $M\to R^r$ with torsion kernel and cokernel. There is a nonzero $f\in R$ with $M_f\cong R_f^r$, and an injection $R^r\to M$ with torsion cokernel.
theorems.proof: There is a map $M\to R^r$ with torsion kernel and cokernel. There is a nonzero $f\in R$ with $M_f\cong R_f^r$, and an injection $R^r\to M$ with torsion cokernel.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Hom into a finite reflexive module is reflexive
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be a Noetherian domain and let $M,N$ be finite $R$-modules with $N$ reflexive.
theorems.statement: The module $\operatorname{Hom}_R(M,N)$ is reflexive.
theorems.proof: The module $\operatorname{Hom}_R(M,N)$ is reflexive.

theorems.subject: module
theorems.name: Codimension-one formula for the reflexive hull
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R$ be a Noetherian normal domain with fraction field $K$, and $M$ a finite $R$-module. Write $M_{\mathrm{tors}}$ for its torsion submodule.
theorems.statement: Inside $M\otimes_RK$, the reflexive hull is $\bigcap_{\operatorname{ht}\mathfrak p=1}(M/M_{\mathrm{tors}})_{\mathfrak p}$. The intersection over an empty family is the ambient vector space.
theorems.proof: Inside $M\otimes_RK$, the reflexive hull is $\bigcap_{\operatorname{ht}\mathfrak p=1}(M/M_{\mathrm{tors}})_{\mathfrak p}$. The intersection over an empty family is the ambient vector space.

theorems.subject: module-element
theorems.name: An existing content ideal is finitely generated
theorems.hypotheses: Let $M$ be flat over $A$, let $x\in M$ and assume its content ideal $I$ exists.
theorems.statement: The ideal $I$ is finitely generated: a finite expression for $x$ in $IM$ already uses a finitely generated subideal of $I$.
theorems.proof: The ideal $I$ is finitely generated: a finite expression for $x$ in $IM$ already uses a finitely generated subideal of $I$.

theorems.subject: module-element
theorems.name: Preservation of content under an injective map on closed fibres
theorems.hypotheses: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be local. Let $u:M\to N$ be a homomorphism of flat modules inducing an injection $M/\mathfrak m M\to N/\mathfrak m N$, and let $x\in M$ have content $I$.
theorems.statement: The element $u(x)$ has content $I$.
theorems.proof: The element $u(x)$ has content $I$.

theorems.subject: module-element
theorems.name: Content exists in a flat Mittag–Leffler module
theorems.hypotheses: Let $M$ be a flat Mittag–Leffler module over $A$.
theorems.statement: Each $x\in M$ has a content ideal.
theorems.proof: Each $x\in M$ has a content ideal.

theorems.subject: topological-ring-map
theorems.name: Continuity test for adic ring maps
theorems.hypotheses: Let $\varphi:R\to S$ be a ring map with $R$ given the $I$-adic topology and $S$ given the $J$-adic topology.
theorems.statement: The map $\varphi$ is continuous if and only if $\varphi(I^n)\subseteq J$ for some $n\geq1$.
theorems.proof: The map $\varphi$ is continuous if and only if $\varphi(I^n)\subseteq J$ for some $n\geq1$.

theorems.subject: topological-ring-map
theorems.name: The adic formal smoothness test can take the source discrete
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be continuous for the $I$-adic topology on $R$ and the $J$-adic topology on $S$.
theorems.statement: Formal smoothness for these topologies is equivalent to formal smoothness with the discrete topology on $R$ and the $J$-adic topology on $S$.
theorems.proof: Formal smoothness for these topologies is equivalent to formal smoothness with the discrete topology on $R$ and the $J$-adic topology on $S$.

theorems.subject: topological-ring-map
theorems.name: Adic formal smoothness and completion
theorems.hypotheses: Let $R\to S$ be continuous for the $I$-adic and $J$-adic topologies, with $I,J$ finitely generated.
theorems.statement: Formal smoothness of $R\to S$, $R\to\widehat S$, and $\widehat R\to\widehat S$ for their adic topologies are equivalent.
theorems.proof: Formal smoothness of $R\to S$, $R\to\widehat S$, and $\widehat R\to\widehat S$ for their adic topologies are equivalent.

theorems.subject: field-family
theorems.name: Extending a p-independent subset to a p-basis
theorems.hypotheses: Let $K/k$ be a field extension of characteristic $p>0$, and let $E\subseteq K$ be $p$-independent over $k$.
theorems.statement: The set $E$ is contained in a $p$-basis of $K/k$. Applying this to the empty set proves existence of a $p$-basis.
theorems.proof: The set $E$ is contained in a $p$-basis of $K/k$. Applying this to the empty set proves existence of a $p$-basis.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: Tensoring with a K-flat complex preserves quasi-isomorphisms
theorems.hypotheses: Let $F^\bullet$ be K-flat over $R$ and let $u$ be a quasi-isomorphism of complexes over $R$.
theorems.statement: Tensoring $u$ with $F^\bullet$ and taking the direct-sum total complex yields a quasi-isomorphism.
theorems.proof: Tensoring $u$ with $F^\bullet$ and taking the direct-sum total complex yields a quasi-isomorphism.

theorems.subject: complex
theorems.name: K-flatness is preserved by scalar extension
